- New `ui/lists.js` (`window.PSBListsUI`), a COPY of apps/steel-bridge/ui/lists.js with this app's selectors: `[id="i_spans.lengths"]`, `[id="i_xs.skews"]`, `[id="i_xs.bays"]`.
  - The page's `<input data-kind="list">` stays, hidden, holding the text "a, b, c" that the page's own `parseList` reads, so the arrays are stored as before.
  - One change from the copy, in `bind()`'s focusout: when the page was redrawn before the deferred commit ran (a click on an input tab), the edit is committed through the input of the same id. Before, it was lost.
- `index.html`:
  - Scripts: `../../shared/list-input.js`, `ui/lists.js`, `ui/plan.js`.
  - Bridge layout tab: `ph('Plan', …)` → `planCard()`. The list notes say "One row per …". The list units are now in the table headers, so `list(…, '')`.
  - Cross-section tab: `sel('xs.spMode', 'Girder spacing', [individual, equal])`. In equal mode, `equalRows()` (W_cc, the step `xs.eqS` S = W_cc / (N_b − 1), the deck width out to out) replaces the bay list.
  - New card `lineTypeCard()`: a select per line and span (`data-lt="s|g"`) → `BR.assignLine(P, k, g)`, the same data as the Girders & strands line boxes. A line keeps a type once it has one, as the boxes.
  - Change handler: `xs.spMode` to equal sets `xs.Wcc` = Σ bays, then `M.applyEqual(P)` runs on every change.
  - `drawInputs()` mounts the plan on the Bridge layout tab.
- `engine/model.js`:
  - `equalSpacing(xs)`, a byte-for-byte COPY of apps/steel-bridge/engine/model.js equalSpacing;
  - `applyEqual(P)`;
  - `validate()`: `xs.spMode` must be individual / equal; in equal mode `xs.Wcc` > 0 and N_b ≥ 2;
  - the header documents `xs.spMode` / `xs.Wcc`.
- `ui/inputcheck.js`: the steel app's list handling (`isList`, `cellIn`). An error on `xs.bays.1` marks and focuses that row's cell of the table.
- Tests:
  - `tests/engine/psbridge-layout.test.mjs` (4 tests; see below). `psbridge-model.test.mjs` has the script list updated.
  - The skeleton and types smokes now set the three lists through their hidden input (`setList`). The skeleton smoke's "error link opens the field" now expects the bay's row cell of the table.
  - `ps-bridge-figures.mjs`: the plan (lines, continuity diaphragm, diaphragms, labels, ×2, not saved), a span typed into its row, + Add, equal spacing, back to individual, and the girder type of each line.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- The stored fields and formats are unchanged: `spans.lengths`, `xs.skews` and `xs.bays` stay arrays of numbers. The row tables write the same text into the page's input, and the page parses it as before.
- New optional fields `xs.spMode` ('individual' | 'equal') and `xs.Wcc` (ft). Absent means individual bays, today's behaviour. They change no result by themselves: in equal mode the page writes S into every `xs.bays` entry, which everything reads as before.
- No new key. The ×2 choice is not stored.
- Test (§5): an old project (no spMode / Wcc; two spans made continuous, unequal bays, different skews, girder types) gives the same text through save → load → export and import → export. The list tables give back the same arrays through the page's parser, and `applyEqual` changes nothing. There is no new input error, and every cell's engine inputs are the same.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. Equal spacing only writes the bays the engineer would otherwise type: S = W_cc / (N_b − 1), the Steel Bridge app's definition. No formula of a result changed.
### Check case
- N_b = 5, W_cc = 38 ft: S = 38 / 4 = 9.500 ft, so bays [9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5]. With overhangs 3.5 / 3.0 ft, the deck is 44.50 ft out to out. N_b = 4, W_cc = 40 ft: S = 13.333 ft.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- LAY-D1. Plan diaphragms: drawn as the 3D view places them (at the entered a from each line's left ℄ bearing, parallel to the supports, across the bays next to a line whose type has one; none between adjacent boxes, slabs or NEXT beams). End diaphragms at the bearings are not drawn, because the project has no input for them.
- LAY-D2. "Width ×2" is always offered (Steel offers its exaggeration only for a long, thin plan). The choice is not saved, as Steel's.
- LAY-D3. Girder type of each line: a line that has a type can only be moved to another type of its span, not left without one, as the Girders & strands line boxes.
- LAY-D4. Equal spacing: back to individual keeps the bays as written. A change of N_b in equal mode rewrites every bay to the new S, as Steel.
### Other copies
- `ui/lists.js` and `engine/model.js` `equalSpacing` are copies of the Steel Bridge app's, to move to shared/ later (CLAUDE.md §3). The focusout fix in `ui/lists.js` is not in the steel copy, which has the same race; that tool was not changed.

Engineer's decision: the new app syncs under its own tool id `'ps-bridge-app'` (not the old app's `'bridge-suite'`).
### Problem
- The Project tab's "Save and open" card had Export JSON, Import JSON and New only; no saved-project list, no header project chip, no Save / Ctrl+S, no Cloud sync. The keys `psb2.lib.index`, `psb2.lib.p.`, `psb2.lib.current` were reserved in `engine/model.js` KEYS (PR 1) and unused.
### What changed
- New `engine/library.js` (`window.PSBLibrary`): an adapted copy of `apps/steel-bridge/engine/library.js` (112 lines): the same functions (`list, save, open, rename, duplicate, remove, rebuild, getCur, setCur, text, usage, etTime`) and behaviour, with `window.SBDModel` → `window.PSBModel`, the keys `sbd2.lib.*` → `psb2.lib.*` (through `PSBModel.KEYS`) and the index schema `'sbd2.library'` → `'psb2.library'`. A stored item is `PSBModel.exportJSON(project)`; open is `PSBModel.importJSON(text)`.
- `engine/model.js`: the comment of the three `lib*` KEYS only (Before: `// reserved for the saved-project list (a later PR)` After: `// the saved-project list (engine/library.js, PR 5; reserved in PR 1)`). No key value changed.
- `index.html`:
  - Script list: after `'../../shared/report.js',` new `'engine/library.js'`, `'../../shared/projects.js'`, `'../../shared/projects-ui.js'`, `'../../shared/github-sync.js'` (classic scripts, relative paths, in the CBUST `document.write` list; the shared files unchanged).
  - `panes()` `proj:` Before: `card('Save and open', '<div class="fRow"><button … id="bExport">Export JSON</button><button … id="bImport">Import JSON</button><button … id="bNew">New</button></div><p class="note">The open project is kept in this browser automatically. The saved-projects list (Save, Save as…, Saved projects…) comes in a later PR. Import JSON also opens …</p>')` After: `card('Save and open', '<div id="pbHost"></div><p class="note">Import JSON also opens an old-app Export JSON file (as "From the old app" below).</p>')`; `drawInputs()` mounts the standard card there (`if (pb && $('pbHost')) pb.mount($('pbHost'));`).
  - The `#inPanes` click handler's `bExport` / `bImport` / `bNew` branch removed (the card's buttons; New is projectBar's New).
  - After `saveUi`: `const LIB = window.PSBLibrary, norm = Q => M.exportJSON(Q); let pb = null, cur = { id: null, text: null };`.
  - `syncBar()`: + `if (pb) { pb.refresh(); pb.dialog.refresh(); }`.
  - `lgCtx` ("From the old app"): `pickFile: () => pb.importJSON()` (asks first on unsaved changes); `replace` ends in `loadAs(Q, null)` (Before: `P = Q; autosave = true; ui.itab = 'proj'; ui.scope = ''; saveUi(); changed();`). Its own confirm (ui/legacy.js) unchanged.
  - `#fImport` change handler: Before: `if (!confirm('Open this project? It replaces the open project here (export it first to keep it).')) return; P = r.project; autosave = true; changed();` After: `loadAs(r.project, null);` (asked first by `pb.importJSON`, as the steel app).
  - New block "saved projects (PR 5 …)" before the start-up `drawInputs(); drawOut(); syncBar();`: `loadAs`, `loadNotes`, `ghStore`, `view` / `vStore` (the by-name view), `pbSave`, the start-up link (`LIB.getCur`), `SharedProjectsUI.projectBar({ store: vStore, storage: LS, label: 'Prestressed Bridge Design (new app)', id: 'psbLibDlg', askUnsaved: 'always', …, fileButtons: [B_EX, B_IM], header: $('hdrBtns'), card: true, headerSave: false, chipClick, …, cloud: { tool: 'ps-bridge-app', label: 'Prestressed Bridge Design (new app)', toFile: t => t, store: ghStore, fromFile } })`: the steel app's wiring (apps/steel-bridge/index.html, STDS-B) adapted: no undo bookkeeping in `pbSave` / `loadAs` (Undo/Redo: PR 6), `.psb2.json` file names, PS's `changed()` / `toast()`.
- Tests: new `tests/engine/psbridge-library.test.mjs` (9 tests); `tests/engine/psbridge-model.test.mjs` (the page's script list; the three shared save files left out of the app-code key check, as the moved engine files); new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-library.mjs` (11 checks).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- The open project's autosave `psb2.project.current` is unchanged (key, format, when it is written): an existing user's project opens exactly as before (smoke 1: the text byte-identical after the page opens; the chip says "not saved" until it is saved to the list). `psb2.ui` unchanged.
- New keys, written only on Save / Save as / Rename / Duplicate / Delete / Open: `psb2.lib.index` (`{ schema: 'psb2.library', version: 1, items: [{ id, name, number, saved, size }] }`), `psb2.lib.p.<id>` (the Export JSON text), `psb2.lib.current` (`{ id }`), and `psb2.lib.index.unreadable.<ISO time>` (only if the index cannot be read: its text kept). All `psb2.`-prefixed (Chromium's shared file:// origin).
- Only once Cloud sync is set up by the user (shared/github-sync.js, unchanged): `bridgeSuite.v1.githubSync` (the one setup of every tool in this browser, with the token), `bridgeSuite.v1.githubSync.tool.ps-bridge-app`, `bridgeSuite.v1.githubSync.presence.ps-bridge-app`, `.live`, `.deviceId`. Named per tool by the shared file; nothing is written while sync is off.
- The JSON export format is unchanged: the Export JSON text = the stored item text = `M.exportJSON(P)`; export → import → export is byte-identical for the 19 result-tab designs, `newProject`, `defaultProject` and an old-app import (Node test).
- The token: typed only in the Cloud sync dialog, kept and sent only by shared/github-sync.js (Authorization header to api.github.com). This page never reads it; it is not in a project, an exported file, a URL, the page text or the console (smoke 7).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None: no formula, factor, unit or reference changed; no result changes (harness B 0 differences).
### Check case
- Fresh browser with only `psb2.project.current` of "Existing bridge" (B-77, one 96 ft span, 6 girders): the page opens it unchanged, chip "Project: Existing bridge · not saved". Change the name to "Route 2 over the Pawcatuck", Ctrl+S → Save as with that name → `psb2.lib.index` has 1 item (number B-77), `psb2.lib.p.<id>` = `psb2.project.current`, chip "saved". Change Checker → "unsaved changes"; Ctrl+S → "saved", no question. Export JSON → `Route_2_over_the_Pawcatuck.psb2.json` = the stored item text.
### How verified
- See the PR: `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`; `node tests/engine/run.mjs psbridge tex project-registry`; smokes ps-bridge-skeleton, ps-bridge-types, ps-bridge-3d, ps-bridge-library; harness B normal run.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- PS5-D1. The steel app's behaviour is copied as it is: header chip only (Save and Saved projects… in the card, Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S anywhere), `askUnsaved: 'always'`, duplicate names listed as "(older, saved …)", Import JSON asks only when there are unsaved changes (the old "Open this project?" confirm is replaced by the standard unsaved-changes question).
- PS5-D2. "Unsaved changes" compares the whole project text (M.exportJSON), so choosing the girder type and line shown (P.design, stored in the project) also marks the project changed: nothing that is saved is left out of the comparison.
- PS5-D3. `shared/project-registry.js` (the home page's list of tools' saved projects) is not changed: the home page does not list this app's saved projects yet (a shared-file change of its own, §3).
- PS5-D4. The GitHub sync keys are the shared file's per-tool keys (`bridgeSuite.v1.githubSync.tool.ps-bridge-app`, …), not `psb2.`: they are named by shared/github-sync.js for every tool, written only once the user sets up sync, and carry the tool id; changing them would change a shared file used by every tool.
- PS5-D5. "From the old app" keeps its own card and confirm (ui/legacy.js unchanged); its file button now asks first on unsaved changes (pb.importJSON). An import is not a saved project (chip "not saved").
### Other copies
- `apps/steel-bridge/engine/library.js` and the STDS-B wiring of `apps/steel-bridge/index.html`: the originals of this adapted copy (not changed). Keep a fix to one in step with the other where it applies.
## 2026-11-14 — Loads & LLDF: lanes, wheels and the lever-rule influence line, with an LLDF case switch (display only)
PR #1550: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1550
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up to the Steel Bridge app, item 7:
  - on the Loads & LLDF sketch, a case switch like Steel's (lever rule one lane / multi-lane / rigid section, where the engine uses each);
  - the wheels placed by the lever-rule placement the engine uses;
  - a required Node test that the drawn ordinates and wheel positions reproduce the engine's lever value (with m as the engine applies it) for several layouts;
  - types (f) / (g): no wheels, with a note.
### What the engine does (read from engine/pbd-lldf-flexure.js distFactors, frozen; not edited)
- Exterior I-girder (`ld.pos === 'exterior'`), one lane:
  - `[de-2, de-8].forEach(x => { if (x > -S) R += 0.5*(S+x)/S; }); lever = 1.2*R`;
  - x is the wheel's distance outboard of the exterior girder ℄; the wheels are 2 ft and 8 ft inboard of the traffic face; S = the line's S (the adjacent bay).
- Rigid section: `e_j = Xext + de − 5 − 12 j`, `R = mpf[NL−1] (NL/Nb + Xext Σe/Σx²)`, the largest over NL = 1 … ld.NL. With unequal bays, PS-19 `engine/rigid.js` uses the real lines.
- Two or more lanes: `e_M g_M2` / `e_V g_V2` (equations: no wheel placement).
- Not used: interior lines (equations), NEXT (`isNext`: no lever, no rigid), box beams and slabs (`df.fg`, PS-35: neither).
### What changed
- `ui/xsfig.js`:
  - New `lldf(P, s, g, inp, df)`: the model of line g's cases from the engine's own inputs (`inp.S`, `inp.loads.de`) and results (`df.rigidNL`, `df.rigidX`):
    - lever case: the traffic face d_e outboard of the girder; wheels at 2 and 8 ft inboard of it; terms `{ xo, ord = (S + xo)/S if xo > −S else 0 }`; value = 1.2 Σ 0.5 ord;
    - rigid case: N_L = df.rigidNL lanes of 12 ft from the face; resultants 5 ft inside each lane; e_j from the girder centroid (the lines, or df.rigidX); value = m (N_L/N_b + X_ext Σe/Σx²);
    - kind 'int' / 'next' / 'fg' with a note and no case.
  - `svg(…, { ll })` + `drawLL()`: the lanes and wheels (arrows to the deck) above the barriers, with the d_e and deck dimensions moved up. For the lever case, the exterior girder's influence line under the chain (1.0 at the girder, 0 at the next girder, the ordinates at the wheels, a hover read-out each). For the rigid case, the lane resultants (brown ticks) and e in the lane labels. The Steel Bridge app's lldfSvg layout.
- `ui/loads.js`:
  - `after()`: the detail card gets the "LLDF case" switch (Lever rule, one lane / Rigid section, N lanes) for an exterior I-girder line. The choice is kept for the page session, not saved.
  - Caption `#ldLLNote`: the worked comparison, e.g. "g_lever = 1.2 × 0.5 × (1.0000 + 0.2941) = 0.7765 = the engine's 0.7765 §ld.lever"; for the rigid case, R with e, X_ext, Σx² against `df.rigid` §ld.rigid. For other lines, the note why there are no wheels.
- `ui/report.js`: `ALLSEG` adds `gfx_ld`. For an exterior unit the Report's Loads & LLDF section draws the cross-section in each case (Figure 4.1 lever rule, 4.2 rigid section). Interior units are unchanged.
- Tests:
  - New `tests/engine/psbridge-lldffig.test.mjs` (5 tests), checked against `PSBHoldDown.compute` of each line:
    - the face, the wheels (2 / 8 ft, 6 ft apart) and the next girder at S;
    - each ordinate, and m Σ 0.5 ord = df.lever with m = 1.2;
    - N_L = df.rigidNL, the resultants, and R from the drawn resultants = df.rigid.
  - Layouts: equal bays G1 and G5; unequal bays (PS-19) on both sides with N_L up to 3; a 6 ft × 12 in sidewalk (d_e = −3, the second wheel not counted); a 2.5 ft barrier; no cross-section barriers (the entered d_e) with N_L = 1; interior lines, NEXT and box beams (no case).
  - `ps-bridge-figures.mjs`: the switch, the wheels and influence line, the caption value = the engine's, the rigid lanes, G5 on the sidewalk side, interior G3 (no case), and Report §4 holding both cases.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. The figure draws the engine's own placement (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 4.6.2.2.2d lever rule, m = 1.2 of Table 3.6.1.1.2-1; C4.6.2.2.2d rigid section). Its values are recomputed only to show that they equal the engine's, which the test checks.
### Check case (new project, 5 BT-72, bays 8.5 / 9.5 / 9.5 / 8.5 ft, overhang 3.5 ft, d_e = 2.00 ft, G1)
- Lever: x_w = 0.00 and −6.00 ft; ordinates (8.5 + 0)/8.5 = 1.0000 and (8.5 − 6)/8.5 = 0.2941; g_lever = 1.2 × 0.5 × 1.2941 = 0.7765 (the engine's 0.7765).
- Rigid, 2 lanes: e = 18 + 2 − 5 = 15.000 and 3.000 ft; Σx² = 2 × 18² + 2 × 9.5² = 828.50 ft²; R = 1.00 (2/5 + 18 × 18 / 828.5) = 0.7911 (the engine's 0.7911).
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- LL-D1. No "multi-lane" lever case: the engine's two-or-more-lane exterior factor is e × g_interior (equations, Table 4.6.2.2.2d-1), with no wheel placement to draw. The switch offers only the cases the engine uses: lever (one lane) and rigid section (its governing N_L).
- LL-D2. In the rigid case the lanes are drawn from the traffic face with each lane resultant 5 ft inside its lane edge. This is the engine's e_j = X_ext + d_e − 5 − 12 j: the wheel pair 2 ft and 8 ft inside each lane. The engine places no wheels for it; the wheels drawn are those the resultant implies.
- LL-D3. The case choice is per page session (not saved). The Report shows both cases for an exterior unit.
- LL-D4. DXF download of the figure: not done (optional in the request). shared/dxf.js would need a second drawing of the same figure in CAD primitives.

## 2026-11-14 — PR 6: Undo / Redo in the header (100 steps, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z, as the Steel Bridge app); the girder count notice's Undo is a step of it (no calculation change)
PR #1551: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1551
### Request
- Catch-up to the Steel Bridge app (apps/steel-bridge/index.html, "undo / redo"): header Undo / Redo with a 100-step history and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z; typing in a field keeps its own undo; integrated with the girder count change notice's Undo (PR 3a-1); results follow an Undo.
### Problem
- No Undo / Redo except the girder count notice's own Undo, which put back a stored project text (`P = JSON.parse(undo); changed();`): that "undo" was itself a new change and could not be redone.
### What changed (`apps/ps-bridge/index.html` only)
- Header: in `#hdrBtns` before `#fImport`, `<span id="hdrUR"><button id="bUndo" title="Undo the last input change (Ctrl+Z)" disabled>Undo</button><button id="bRedo" title="Redo (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z)" disabled>Redo</button></span>` (the steel app's markup); CSS `#hdrUR{display:inline-flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;white-space:nowrap;} #hdrBtns button:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:default;}` (the steel app's rules); projectBar `chipBefore: $('hdrUR')` (order chip · Undo · Redo).
- State after `let pb = null, cur = …`: `let snap = '', undoS = [], redoS = [], stepNo = 0; const UNDO_MAX = 100;` (memory only).
- `changed()` → `changed(restoring)`: `if (!restoring) record();` after the autosave. New `record()`: `t = JSON.stringify(P)`; unchanged → nothing; only `P.design` differs (the girder type / line shown) → `snap = t` (no step); else `undoS.push(snap)` (oldest dropped past 100), `redoS.length = 0`, `snap = t`, `stepNo++`, the notices' Undo buttons removed. New `restore(from, to)`, `undo`, `redo` (the steel app's: `to.push(snap); snap = from.pop(); P = JSON.parse(snap); changed(true)`).
- `syncBar()`: `$('bUndo').disabled = !undoS.length; $('bRedo').disabled = !redoS.length;` first.
- `pick()` and the `[data-tycell]` click: `record()` after their autosave (P.design only: snap follows).
- `toast(text, undo)`: `undo` is now `true` (not the project text). Before: `n.querySelector('.nUndo').onclick = () => { n.remove(); P = JSON.parse(undo); changed(); };` After: `const at = stepNo; … onclick = () => { n.remove(); if (stepNo === at && undoS.length) restore(undoS, redoS); };` (the history's Undo; `restore` because the parameter `undo` hides the function `undo` there). The `#inPanes` change handler: `undo = JSON.stringify(P)` removed; `toast(tyNote, undo)` → `toast(tyNote, true)`.
- `loadAs` (open, New, Import, From the old app): the history starts again (`undoS = []; redoS = []; snap = JSON.stringify(P); stepNo++`, notices' Undo removed, `changed(true)`).
- `pbSave`: `record()` after the save (a Save as name change is a step, as the steel app).
- Keys (the steel app's handlers): `#bUndo` / `#bRedo` clicks; `input` / `change` / `blur` (capture) set / clear `data-typing` on the field; `keydown`: Ctrl/⌘+Z undo, Ctrl/⌘+Y or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z redo, not while a field has `data-typing` or a dialog is open. At start-up `snap = JSON.stringify(P)`.
- Tests: new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-undo.mjs`.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: the history is in the page's memory only (the steel app stores none either); no key, no format changed. Every Undo / Redo writes the restored project to the autosave `psb2.project.current` as any change does.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None: no formula, factor, unit or reference changed. Results follow the project on screen (`result()` keyed by the design's engine inputs, `allResults()` by the project text): an Undo shows exactly the results before the change (smoke 2: the Analysis tab's text identical).
### Check case
- New project; Analysis tab; Span lengths 120 → 100: the tab's results change. Undo (or Ctrl+Z): span 120 and the tab's text identical to before; Redo (Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z): span 100 and the changed text. Number of girders 5 → 6: notice "Girder count 5 → 6: … re-assigned" with Undo; its Undo gives the project text before the change byte for byte, and Redo puts the change back.
### How verified
- See the PR.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- PS6-D1. As the steel app: the history is not stored (memory only; a reload starts with none), 100 steps, one step per project change, Save as's name change a step, opening a project / New / Import starts a new history.
- PS6-D2. A change of the girder type and line shown only (P.design, the output tabs' choice; stored in the project) is not an undo step (as the steel app's girder shown, ui.g); an Undo restores the snapshot as it was, with the line shown then.
- PS6-D3. The girder count notice's Undo is the header's Undo of that one step (so it can be redone); it is removed once another step is made or the history moves (Undo / Redo, open, New), where before it stayed on the newest notice.
## 2026-11-14 — PR 8a: Summary girder elevation, one per girder type (picker), with the strand profile, ℓ_t / ℓ_d and the governing checks where they govern (display only)
PR #1552: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1552
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up to the Steel Bridge app, item 8, Summary elevation. Engineer's choice, corrected on 2026-11-14: one elevation per girder type, chosen with a picker, not one per span.
- Each elevation is drawn for that type's governing line and span. It shows the girder elevation, the strand profile (draped, debonded, hold-down points), the transfer and development lengths, and the governing check of each kind marked where it governs, each linking to its check's tab. Steel's `SBDAlongGfx.summarySvg` is the reference.
### What changed
- New `ui/sumelev.js` (`window.PSBSumElev`):
  - `model(M, P, k)` reads girder type k of the Summary model (`ui/summary.js model()`). Its governing line is the line of its largest group ratio, in its span. All values are that cell's engine values: L, h; the strand rows (y, n, debonded count and length); the draped strands (y_end, y_mid, hold-down points at frac × L); ℓ_t = R.ss.lt; ℓ_d = R.ldBonded (κ 1.6) and R.ldDebond (κ 2.0).
  - Each group's governing check (`T.groups`, the worst over the type's lines, the line named) is placed at its station `q.loc`. Groups with no station (the owner's input limits) are listed only.
  - `svg(m, W)`:
    - the girder (vertical scale exaggerated) and the strands (debonded lengths dashed; draped strands and hold-down points);
    - ℓ_t and ℓ_d bars under the girder from each end, and from each debond point;
    - the checks as flags above the girder in rows that do not overlap, coloured by ratio (< 0.90, 0.90 to 1.00, > 1.00), the type's governing check outlined; each flag is a `data-sumgo` link (its tab and worked step with that type and line, the Summary's own link handling);
    - dimensions: the hold-down distance, L, h.
  - `html(M, o)` is the card "Girder elevation of each girder type" with the picker `#sumElevK`. It defaults to the type of the Summary's governing check; the choice is kept for the page session and not saved. `after(el, M, o)` draws the detail card and lists every group's check with its link.
- `ui/summary.js`: `html()` adds the card after "Governing check of each group, per girder type" and keeps the model (`LAST.M`); `after()` draws it. CSS `.se-*`.
- `index.html`: `ui/sumelev.js` is loaded before `ui/summary.js`. In the output change handler, the picker redraws the tab.
- Tests:
  - `tests/engine/psbridge-sumelev.test.mjs` (3 tests) covers every type of: a new project; three spans made continuous with pier checks, debonded rows and a third type; CTDOT owner limits (listed, no station); and box beams with no draped strands. It checks the governing line and span; L, h, ℓ_t, ℓ_d, the rows and the draped strands = the engine's; each group's ratio, line, station and link = the Summary model's; and one marker per check with a station.
  - `psbridge-model.test.mjs`: the script list.
  - `ps-bridge-figures.mjs`: the picker lists every type; the markers and the list; the title names the governing line; ℓ, L and h are drawn; the picker draws another type; a marker opens its tab; 1400 and 390 px.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None. The picker's choice is not stored.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. Shown as the engine computes them: transfer length 5.9.4.3.1; development length 5.9.4.3.2 (κ = 1.6) and of debonded strands 5.9.4.3.3 (κ = 2.0).
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- SE-D1. The type's governing line is the line of its largest group ratio. The checks of the other groups may govern on another line of the same type, and each marker names its line.
- SE-D2. ℓ_t and ℓ_d are drawn from each girder end for the bonded strands and from each debond point for the debonded ones. The engine reports one ℓ_t (R.ss.lt) for all strands.
- SE-D3. The groups with no station along the girder (the owner's input limits, e.g. f′ci) are listed under the figure, not marked on it.

## 2026-11-14 — PR 8b: 3D view: View (whole bridge / girder line close-up, Zoom to), diagram overlays, Scale (display only)
PR #1553: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1553
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up to the Steel Bridge app, item 8, 3D view:
  - Steel's View choices (close-up per girder);
  - the diagram overlays (moment / shear envelopes from the results);
  - the Scale control;
  - readable labels.
### What changed (`ui/view3d.js`, the Steel Bridge app's apps/steel-bridge/ui/view3d.js pattern: DG, V3B_DG, the close-up and V3B.focus)
- New bar: View (Whole bridge / Girder line G1 … Gn close-up), Zoom to (close-up only), Diagram, Scale (0.25 to 4), + moment down. The choices are kept in `ui.v3d` (psb2.ui, the key the layers and the camera already use; nothing new in the project).
- Close-up of line g:
  - its girders in every span; its tributary deck strip (half the bays beside it, to the deck edge on an exterior line) with its barrier or sidewalk; its haunch and bearings; the diaphragms in the bays beside it; the continuity diaphragm cut to the strip;
  - every strand of its girders: `geom(P, { strLine: g })`. The default `geom(P)` is unchanged: the strands of the type shown.
  - Zoom to: the whole line; each span's left end, hold-down point (when draped), midspan and right end. The home view is closer.
- Diagrams (`DG`, `series(R, d)`): Strength I and Service I moment envelopes, LL+IM moment envelope, DC moment, DW moment, Strength I shear envelope, LL+IM shear envelope, DC shear.
  - The values are each girder type × line's engine result (`R.diagrams`, k-ft / kip at the engine's stations, x from the left ℄ bearing), through `ctx.res(k, g)`, which is the page's cached `cellR`.
  - Each is drawn as a fence beside each girder drawn (+ moment down by default), with the peak values labelled (larger in the close-up, 1.2 × the label size in the whole view) and a pointer read-out.
  - The `dg` layer toggle is added to the layer list.

## 2026-11-14 — Smoke ps-bridge-library: the intermittent `'unsaved' !== 'saved'` after the reload (test fix; no app change)
PR #1555: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1555
### Problem
- `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-library.mjs` failed about one run in two (5 of 10 runs here, also on clean origin/main) at step 4, the check after `p.reload()`: `assert.equal(await state(), 'saved')` got `'unsaved'`.
- Root cause (found, not guessed): the page was opened with `openPage(FILE, { ls: … })` (tests/lib.mjs), whose init script seeds localStorage on every navigation unless `sessionStorage.__seeded` is set. Chromium does not always keep a tab's sessionStorage across a `file://` reload. Shown in a debug run: a marker put in sessionStorage before the reload was `null` after it in exactly the failing runs. The init script then wrote the seed again, so `psb2.project.current` went back to the seeded "Existing bridge" (checker "") while `psb2.lib.current` still named "Route 2 alt (renamed)". The chip then correctly said "unsaved changes": the inputs on screen were not the saved project.
- So the app was right and the test was wrong: no race in the save or the autosave (both are synchronous; the chip compares `M.exportJSON(P)` with the saved item's text).
### What changed (`tests/smoke/ps-bridge-library.mjs` only)
- Anchor: `const { b, p, errs } = await openPage(FILE, { vw: 1280, vh: 900`.
- Before: `const { b, p, errs } = await openPage(FILE, { vw: 1280, vh: 900, ls: { ...OLD, 'psb2.project.current': seeded } });`
- After: `const SEED = { ...OLD, 'psb2.project.current': seeded }; const { b, p, errs } = await openPage(FILE, { vw: 1280, vh: 900 }); await p.waitForSelector('#inTabs [data-itab]'); await p.evaluate(o => { localStorage.clear(); for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)) localStorage.setItem(k, v); }, SEED); await p.reload();` (with a comment giving the reason). The seed is written once; no init script re-seeds on the later reload. Step 1 still checks what it checked: the first page load with the seed keeps `psb2.project.current` byte-identical and shows "not saved".
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5) / Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None: test only; no app file changed.
### Check case
- Before: 10 runs, 5 failed at line 129 (`'unsaved' !== 'saved'`). After: 10 runs, 10 passed (11 checks each).
### Open items
- `tests/lib.mjs` `openPage`'s `ls` seed has the same weakness for every smoke that seeds and then reloads, expecting the page's own later writes to survive (the list in the PR). It is not changed here: it is shared test tooling used by every smoke. A fix there (for example, seed then reload, as here) is a separate change.

- PS37-D4. NEDBT and NEBT use the engine's I-girder handling (type (k)). An NEDBT with no cast-in-place topping (t_s = 0) gets the engine's guarded K_g / (12 L t_s³) term: DF_M about 4.4–5.2 (S 8 ft, L 80 ft): very conservative, not changed (existing engine behaviour); a refined analysis or entered factors are expected for an NEDBT deck.
- PS37-D5. NEXT D and NEXT F use the engine's NEXT handling (types (i)/(j) per beam, S = b_f / 12; no topping: K_g term omitted). NEXT D width b_f = 12 S − 13 in (dwg 11.2.3 note 2), within 96–120 in; the 13 in closure pour's weight is not added automatically (enter it as a non-composite load).

## 2026-11-14 — PS-42: a MassDOT NEDBT with no cast-in-place topping flagged next to its distribution factor (Loads & LLDF tab, Girders & strands shape card, Report Loads & LLDF section) (DISPLAY ONLY; no calculation change)
PR #1559: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1559
### Request
- Engineer decision 2026-11-14 (PS-42, follows PS37-D4): an NEDBT with no topping keeps the current behaviour (the engine's type (k) LLDF evaluated with t_s = 0, a very conservative moment DF, about 4.4–5.2) but is flagged: a clear warning next to the DF on the Loads & LLDF tab, on the girder card, and a matching line in the Report's Loads & LLDF section with a "see §" reference (CLAUDE.md §6). Paraphrased wording, no "pending review" wording; for every girder type / line on an NEDBT with zero topping, none otherwise.
### What changed
- `apps/ps-bridge/engine/sections.js` (anchor `function noTop(inp)`, before `install(); wrapVoids(); wrapMD();`): new
  `noTop(inp)` = the girder is a MassDOT NEDBT (`MD[inp.girder].src.fam === 'nedbt'`) and `!(+inp.ts > 0)` and `inp.loads.llAuto && inp.loads.dfAuto` (the DF is computed); `noTopText(inp)` the warning (HTML, '' otherwise): "No cast-in-place topping is entered for this <girder> (deck thickness t_s = 0, PS-42): the type (k) distribution factor equations are evaluated with t_s = 0 in their deck-slab term K_g / (12 L t_s³), so the moment distribution factor comes out very large and is likely very conservative. Add the topping (deck thickness t_s, Cross-section tab) or review the distribution factor by hand (for example a refined analysis) and enter it (Loads tab)." Both exported on `window.PSBSections` (after `mdNote`).
- `apps/ps-bridge/ui/loads.js` `output()`: the type (k) / NEXT branch `} else h += k.card(\`Live load distribution factors: …\`, k.kv(dfr) + \`<p class="note">…\`);` becomes a block that adds, after `k.kv(dfr)` (below "DF_M used" / "DF_V used"), when `PSBSections.noTopText(inp)` is not '':
  `<div class="alert" id="nedbtNoTop"><b>NEDBT without a topping: the distribution factor is likely very conservative</b> ${nt} The moment factors g<sub>M1</sub> ${wk('ld.m1')} and g<sub>M2</sub> ${wk('ld.m2')} are worked in the Loads &amp; LLDF steps.</div>`. The Report's Loads & LLDF section is made from this card (report/fromtab.js: an `.alert` is a warning note; each `wk` link prints "(see §x.y)" to the worked g_M1 / g_M2 step), once per worked girder type / line.
- `apps/ps-bridge/ui/inputs.js` `cards()` (anchor `id="secTbcNote"`): the Girders & strands tab's shape card also gets `<div class="alert" id="secNoTopNote">${noTopText(P.base)} Worked on the <a href="#" data-gotab="lds">Loads &amp; LLDF tab</a>.</div>` when the condition holds.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key, field or format read or written.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 4.6.2.2.2b-1 (type (k), K_g / 12 L t_s³ term) and Eq. 4.6.2.2.1-1 (K_g) as the engine already evaluates them; the engine's `ts³ = max(ts³, 1e-6)` guard (engine/pbd-lldf-flexure.js, not edited).

Exterior G1: DF_M 4.8995: shown. NEDBT 40 / 80: DF_M 4.4429 / 5.2202. Same girder with t_s = 8 in: DF_M 0.7421: no warning. Every value the same before and after (display only).

## 2026-11-14 — PR 9: cross-section load items matching the Steel Bridge app (deck edge barrier or curb and railing, edge to traffic face, sidewalk fences, raised median, appurtenance w_c, wearing surface by thickness, overlays, a distribution per added line load, DC1 line loads) (CALCULATION CHANGE, §4, for projects that use them; projects saved before unchanged)
PR #1558: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1558
### Request
- Engineer's choice "Match Steel" (catch-up item 9): the Cross-section tab's DC2 / DW inputs should offer the Steel Bridge app's cross-section load items (apps/steel-bridge/ui/loads.js parts(): Deck edges, Sidewalks and median, Wearing surface, Utilities and other line loads, Distribution) and distribute them the same way.
- Projects saved before must open with identical results (§5): the new fields are optional and default to the current behaviour. A round-trip test is required.
### What changed
- `engine/bridge-dl.js`:
  - New block EDGE: lines 30-114 of apps/steel-bridge/engine/loads.js at 58204ba (the same pin as DEAD-VERBATIM), byte for byte, in a scope of its own (`const EDGE = (function () { … return { edgeIn, bridgeEff, edgeLoads, xsIn, llFaces, CATS }; })();`). These are the steel app's deck edge, cross-section input and traffic face functions.
  - New `edgesOf(q)`, `xsInOf(q, sw)`: P.xs.dl → the steel module's inputs.
  - New `edgeFace(P, s)` (Ed[s].f, the steel edgeIn rule) and `llFace(P, s)` = max(edge face, a sidewalk ≥ 12 in, a fence on the sidewalk) (the steel llFaces rule).
  - `checks(P)`: path-named checks of the new fields.
  - `distribute(P)` anchor `const Wd = deckWidth(P)`.
    - Before: the barrier edge loads built by hand (`if (+bL.w > 0) edges.push({ id: 'barL', … x: +bL.bw / 2, plf: +bL.w })`), `fL: +bL.bw || 0`, `medW: 0`, `uwcA: null`, `ovl: []`, `dist: 'auto'`.
    - After: `Ed = EDGE.edgeIn(edgesOf(q), err)`, `xi = EDGE.xsIn(xsInOf(q, sw), err)`, `edges = EDGE.edgeLoads(EDGE.bridgeEff({ wc }, Ed), xi.wcA)`, `fL: Ed.L.f`, `fR: Ed.R.f`, the median / fences / wsThk / wsGam / ovl / wcA passed, `fws: xi.fws !== null ? xi.fws : +q.fws || 0`, `dist: r.dist || 'auto'`.
    - A barrier with none of the new fields gives the same objects as before (`edgeLoads` builds `{ id, desc, cat, side, x: bw / 2, plf: w }` in the same key order).
  - `line(P, g)`: + `DC1` (the line's share of the added DC1 line loads) when there are any.
  - `withSteps`: a new step `dl.G<g>.DC1x` and a note on `ld.wDC1` when there are DC1 line loads.
- `engine/design.js`:
  - `deOf` anchor `const face = `. Before: `Math.max(b, +sw.w > 0 && +sw.t >= 12 - 1e-9 ? +sw.w : 0)`. After: `DL.llFace(P, s)` (same value without the new fields).
  - `one()` after `wBar: q.DC2, wDW: q.DW`: `if (q && q.DC1 != null) o.loads.wNC = +o.loads.wNC + q.DC1`.
- `ui/bridgedl.js`: the card gets the steel app's groups. The new kinds are `type`, `opt` (blank = null) and `bool`. Overlays and line loads can be added and deleted. `lineTable` gets a DC1 total row.
- `ui/loads.js`: the "DC1 additional" row names the line's DC1 share and links to `§dl.G<g>.DC1x`.
- `ui/xsfig.js`, `ui/view3d.js` (display): the curb, railing and fence posts and the median are drawn.
  - XS-D3 resolved: the 3D sidewalk now runs from the deck edge, with the barrier on it, as dead() loads it and the cross-section figure draws it.
- `engine/fields.js`: the d_e note says "traffic face". `engine/model.js`: comment only.
- Tests: new `tests/engine/psbridge-xsloads.test.mjs` (7 tests), with `tests/engine/psbridge-xsloads.before/` (bridge-dl.js and design.js of origin/main 2d61437, the "before" of test 2).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- New optional fields in `P.xs.dl` (psb2.project v1):
  - `barL/barR.type ('barrier' | 'curb'), cw, ch, rw, rp, rf, face`;
  - `swL/swR.fence, fenceX`;
  - `med { w, t, joint }`, `wcA`, `wsMode ('psf' | 'thk'), wsThk, wsGam`;
  - `ovl [{ name, mode, psf, thk, gam }]`;
  - `extra[i].dist`, and category `'DC1'`.
- Absent = as before. No migration; no key changed. A new project writes none of them (byte-identical `xs.dl`).
- Test 2: every girder line's engine inputs are byte-identical to before for the 19 harness B designs (without xs.dl and with the default distribution) and 6 distributed layouts (3 methods × equal / unequal bays, sidewalks, added loads); the worked steps too.
- Test 5: export → import → export is byte-identical with every new field (same engine inputs), and an old project text too.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 3.5.1 (DC and DW); Art. 4.6.2.2.1 (permanent loads distributed equally: the "Typical AASHTO" method; d_e); Art. 4.6.2.2.2d (exterior girder: lever rule, rigid section, through d_e); Art. 3.6.1.1.1 (traffic face).
- MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3 (pile-cap) and RIDOT BDM 3.3.1 (60/40) as before. The formulas are the steel app's (verbatim), unchanged.
- Before / after (only with the new inputs):
  - the curb (c_w/12 × c_h/12 × w_c at c_w/2) and railing (w at its load point) line loads: before there was no curb, only a barrier;
  - the traffic face: the railing face when the curb is < 12 in, else the curb or railing face, or the entered face; before, the barrier width. This moves the start of the wearing surface (dead()'s fL) and d_e (deOf);
  - a fence on the sidewalk: a DC2 line load, and a traffic face candidate;
  - the median, overlays and wearing surface by thickness (q = t/12 × γ × 1000): DC2 / DW line loads;
  - the distribution per added line load (auto / pile-cap / equal / two adjacent): before always 'auto';
  - DC1 line loads: the line's share added to w_NC (before: no DC1 category).
### Check case (new AASHTO project: 5 BT-72 at 9 ft, overhangs 3 ft, deck 42 ft, L = 120 ft, w_c 0.150 kcf, w_NC 0.10 klf; barriers 0.30 klf × 1.5 ft, 25 psf)
- After: the left edge is a 12 × 10 in curb + a 0.05 klf railing at 1.0 ft, plus a 0.05 klf DC1 conduit at 21 ft.
- Before:
  - DC2 = 2 × 0.30 / 5 = 0.120 klf per line;
  - DW = 0.025 × (42 − 1.5 − 1.5) / 5 = 0.975 / 5 = 0.195;
  - d_e G1 = 3 − 1.5 = 1.5 ft.
- After:
  - curb = 12/12 × 10/12 × 0.150 = 0.125 klf at 0.5 ft;
  - ΣDC2 = 0.125 + 0.05 + 0.30 = 0.475, so DC2 = 0.095 per line;
  - the traffic face = the railing face 1.0 ft (the 10 in curb is mountable);
  - DW = 0.025 × (42 − 1.0 − 1.5) / 5 = 0.9875 / 5 = 0.1975;
  - DC1 = 0.05 / 5 = 0.010, so w_NC = 0.110;
  - d_e G1 = 3 − 1.0 = 2.0 ft.
- G2 midspan:
  - M_DC2 = 0.095 × 120² / 8 = 171.0 (before 216.0) kip-ft;
  - M_DW = 355.5 (before 351.0);
  - M_DC1 = 1975.5 (before 1957.5);
  - Strength I M_u = 9697.49 + 1.25 (−45.0 + 18.0) + 1.50 (4.5) = 9670.49 kip-ft (before 9697.49).
- G1:
  - lever rule: before 1.2 × 0.5 × (8.5/9 + 2.5/9) = 0.7333; after 1.2 × 0.5 × (9/9 + 3/9) = 0.8000;
  - rigid section (2 lanes): before 2/5 + 18 × (14.5 + 2.5)/810 = 0.7778; after 2/5 + 18 × (15 + 3)/810 = 0.8000;
  - g_M 0.7778 → 0.8000; Strength I midspan 9734.78 → 9849.81 kip-ft.
- All of these are asserted in `psbridge-xsloads.test.mjs`.
### How verified
- See the PR: `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`; `node tests/engine/run.mjs psbridge tex project-registry`; harness B normal, `--import` and `--control`; smokes ps-bridge-skeleton, -types, -3d, -figures, -library, -undo.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- XS9-D1. Not offered, because the moved engine has no input for them: the steel app's pedestrian live load (PL), utilities on the noncomposite section with DW factors (UT), the future utility allowance (UF), stay-in-place forms by area, the steel detail allowance. The steel engine's load overrides and beam classes are not offered either; the steel app has no inputs for them.
- XS9-D2. A DC1 line load goes on the bare girder: each line's share is added to its w_NC (the "DC1 additional" input, DC factors), the closest input of the moved engine.
- XS9-D3. A curb's sizes start blank (a blocking input error names them until entered); no value is assumed. New projects keep the barrier defaults (no new field written).
- XS9-D4. Railing and fence posts are drawn 42 in high (schematic), as the barrier height is (XS-D1).
- XS9-D5. An entered edge to traffic face also moves the start of the wearing surface (dead()'s fL), as in the steel app. The deck design (Diaphragms / deck tab) keeps its own barrier weight and wearing surface (unchanged).
### Other copies
- apps/steel-bridge/engine/loads.js lines 30-114 (EDGE-VERBATIM) and 116-217 (DEAD-VERBATIM): keep in step. The pin test checks both.

## 2026-11-14 — Item 12: the old app's cross-tool hand-offs (bridgeSuite.v1.*) in the new app — same keys, schemas and payloads; Project tab "Hand-offs" card (no calculation change)
PR #1566: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1566
### Request
- Planned item 12: the new app sends and receives the same `bridgeSuite.v1.*` hand-offs as the old app (`Prestressed Bridge Design.html`), with identical key names and payload formats (CLAUDE.md §5; HANDOFF.md). Prefer changing only apps/ps-bridge. Node tests of every payload round trip. Not the switch-over itself.
### Inventory: the old app's channels (sender → receiver, key) and what the new app does
| Channel / key | Old app | New app (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `superReactions`, `.updatedAt`, copy `.by.psbeam` (bridge-super-reactions) | sends (button) → Bridge Substructure Loading | **sends** (button), the old app's `bxSuperRxPayload` (moved engine, verbatim), producer `PS-Beam`, same copy key |
| `lldfGeom` (bridge-lldf-geometry) | sends (button; auto while the geometry lock is on) → LL & DL | **sends** (button), port of `sendLLDF` |
| `psSection`, `.updatedAt` (bridge-ps-section) | sends on every recompute → MCT generator, LL & DL | **sends** (button), port of its publisher |
| `capacity`, `.updatedAt` (bridge-design-capacity) | sends (button; auto while locked) → MCT rating | **sends** (button), port of `publishCapacity` |
| `projectMeta`, `.updatedAt` (bridge-project-meta) | Share / Use (buttons) ↔ every tool | **Share / Use** (buttons) |
| `lldf` (bridge-lldf-factors) | receives (Pull; lock auto-follow) ← LL & DL | **receives** (Pull, confirm), port of `lldfResolveFor` / `lldfTheirsFor` / `applyLLDFTo` |
| `dlLoads` (bridge-dl-loads) | receives (Pull; lock) ← LL & DL | **receives** (Pull, confirm), port of `dlResolveFor` / `dlTheirsFor` / `applyDLTo` |
| `handoffs`, `latestId`, `updatedAt`, `adopted.psbeam` (MCT demands, psbeam-external-demands) | receives ← MCT generator | not yet (open item: the new app has no imported MIDAS demands in its design; `P.legacy` keeps them unused) |
| `designBeam`, `beamRoster` | reads / writes ↔ LL & DL, MCT | not yet (open item); the lldf pull takes the line shown as the design beam (HO-D5) |
| `geometryChanges`, `.adopted.psbeam` | receives (notice) ← MCT | not yet (open item; a notice for the MCT demands) |
| `locks`, `syncLog.*`, `lockSnap.*` (BridgeLocks) | auto-follow / auto-publish | not in the new app (HANDOFF.md §3.1, §3.7: pull and send on click) |
| `appPaths` | records its file | not written (switch-over) |
| `projects`, `currentProjectId`, `migrated.psbeam` | its slice of the shared project list | read only ("From the old app", PR 2f); switch-over |

## 2026-11-14 — Item A: Auto design (engine/autodesign.js, ui/autodesign.js): a search over each girder type's section, strands, draping and f′c / f′ci, judged by the page's own engine call; candidates per span, Apply as one Undo step (inputs only; no calculation change)
PR #1562: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1562
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up to the Steel Bridge app, item A: Auto design (the steel app's apps/steel-bridge/engine/autodesign.js, ui/autodesign.js are the pattern: settings with Auto / Lock variables and Run on the input tab; ranked candidates with the governing check, Apply as one change, on the output tab).
- For each girder type: the library sections of the owner, strand counts and rows, draping, f′c / f′ci within the allowed ranges; the lightest / shallowest section and the fewest strands that pass every engine check; every candidate computed by the existing engine; no new design formula. docs/ps-bridge-plan.md §4 (PS-1, PS-5, PS-10 to PS-12).
### What changed
- New `engine/autodesign.js` (`window.PSBAutoDesign`; classic script, no DOM): `settings`, `family`, `sections`, `conc`, `rowsOf`, `fill`, `drapes`, `lineInputs`, `fitErrors`, `evalCand`, `search` (generator), `run` (generator), `runSync`, `apply`.
  - A candidate's engine inputs on line g: `PSBDesign.one(Object.assign({}, P, { base: eff, design: { g, s: span }, types: undefined }))` — the body of `PSBDesign.cellInputs` with the candidate's inputs `eff` in place of `PSBBridge.effBase(P, k)` (test: equal for the type's own inputs); result `PSBHoldDown.compute` (computeAll + PS-10 + the app's additions, as the tabs and the check summary).
  - PASS: no engine error, every `R.checks` entry `pass` on every line of the type, and no `PSBInputCheck.collect` error on `base.rows.*` / `base.harp.*` (the strand fit PS-28 / PS-39 on the type's first line, as the page checks a type).
  - Sections (`sections`): MassDOT projects the MassDOT sections; other owners every other library section; of the current shape's family (I-girders and bulb tees incl. NEBT; NEDBT; NEXT F; NEXT D; spread boxes; adjacent boxes; deck slabs) and, for adjacent members, the same nominal width; sorted by gross A then h (lightest) or h then A (shallowest), A and h from the engine's `girderGross`. Locked, Custom or a section property override: the current shape only. One section per span (PS-8): a section is a candidate when every girder type of the span passes on it; the first `topN` (default 3) are listed.
  - Strands: straight rows on the row grid (`PSBSections.rowGrid`, PS-41, else 2 in + 2 in), each filled bottom-up to its capacity = the largest even count that fits (the input check's fit); rows with a capacity below 4 not used; entered rows in the upper half (top strands) kept as entered at the same distance below the top; entered debonding kept row by row (PS-12, never added).
  - Drapes: n_h = 0, 2, …; rows of two at x = ±1 in (the drawn positions); y_mid = top straight row + 2 + (rows of two − 1) in; y_end = y_mid + 2j; the bundle must fit at every height 1 in apart between them (no drape through a void); frac 0.33 … 0.45 by 0.01 (PS-5).
  - Strengths: f′c grid 0.5 ksi through the entered f′c, from the owner's minimum (AASHTO 4.0 ksi, 10th Ed. 5.4.2.1; RIDOT 5.0, 5.2.1; CTDOT 6.0, V2 5.9.1.2; MassDOT 6.5, 3.7.2.1 standard) to the owner's maximum (AASHTO 10.0, C5.4.2.1 basis; CTDOT 10.0; RIDOT 8.0; MassDOT 8.0), read from `PBD.ownRule`; f′ci grid 0.5 ksi through the entered f′ci, from 4.0 ksi, ≤ f′c, within MassDOT ≤ 0.80 f′c, CTDOT 0.70–0.80 f′c and ≤ 6.5, RIDOT ≤ 0.70 f′c, and ≤ the plant value (setting, blank = none). Each limit editable.
  - Search per type and section: a quick reject at the highest strengths with every row full (LL deflection, Strength I flexure or Service III tension failing); then at the entered f′c / f′ci, else the entered f′c with its highest f′ci, else the highest f′c and f′ci: (1) the fewest straight strands N1 passing flexure and Service III tension with no drape (bisection); (2) N = N1, N1 + 2, …, n_h = 0, 2, …, for each frac from 0.45 down the lowest y_end at which every check but the hold-down force passes (bisection), only drapes flatter than the best found; the first (N, n_h) with a passing drape; N grows only while a trial failed only on checks in GROW (Flexure, Srv III tens, Min reinf, Shear, Long. reinf, Fatigue I strand); (3) the lowest f′c with its highest f′ci, then the lowest f′ci.
  - Choice (lexicographic): section (A, h; or h, A), N, n_h, drape slope (y_end − y_mid)/frac (orders F_hd exactly for one n_h), |frac − 0.40|, f′c, f′ci; deterministic.
  - No candidate for a span: `blocked` = the checks failing on the current design and on the closest trial of every section tried.
  - `apply(P, Res, choice)`: each type of each span: `effBase` with girder, rows, harp, mat.fc, mat.fci of its candidate → `PSBBridge.setOvr` (one call per type; the shape for every type of the span).
- New `ui/autodesign.js` (`window.PSBAutoDesignUI`): the input tab (objective, sections to list, the four variables Auto / Lock, f′c / f′ci limits with the owner's values as placeholders, Run / Stop with progress; the run steps the generator ≈ 40 ms per timer tick on a copy of the project) and the output tab (per span: every section tried with each type's strands, f′c / f′ci and governing check (ratio, line) or the reason it has none; the current design and its failing checks; the selected candidate's rows, drape, F_hd / limit, weight and every check (worst line) linked to its tab and worked step (ui/dash.js GROUPS); the assumptions; the trial log; "The project changed since this run" disables Apply). Apply: `PSBAutoDesign.apply`, then the page's `changed()` (one undo step, PR 6) and a notice whose Undo is that step.
- `index.html`: `'engine/autodesign.js'` after `'engine/legacy.js'`, `'ui/autodesign.js'` before `'ui/summary.js'`; the Auto design input pane `PSBAutoDesignUI.inputs(P)` (was a placeholder); `#inPanes` change: `data-ad` → `onChange` + `changed()`; click: `onClick(e, adCtx())`; `OUT = {}` (the Auto design placeholder removed); `drawOut`: `ui.otab === 'ad'` → `#adHost` + `render`; `adCtx()`.
- `ui/summary.js`: the "Not in the Summary" note names Auto design as its own tabs.
- Tests: new `tests/engine/psbridge-autodesign.test.mjs` (5 tests), new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-autodesign.mjs` (7 checks); `psbridge-model.test.mjs` (the script list).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- New optional `P.autodesign = { objective, topN, vars: { section, strands, drape, conc }, fcLo, fcHi, fciLo, fciHi }` (absent = the defaults; nothing reads it for a calculation). No key added or changed (psb2.project.current as before). Apply writes the girder types' existing `ovr` (the same fields the Girders & strands / Materials tabs write).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed: no formula, factor, unit or reference; harness B 0 differences. The search's limits cite AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.4.2.1 and the owner rules already in the engine (RIDOT 5.2.1 / 5.6.1, CTDOT V2 5.9.1.2, MassDOT 3.7.2.1).
### Check case
- New project (BT-72, 120 ft, 5 girders; Interior S1 and Exterior S1, both 40 strands with 12 draped, f′c 8.5 / f′ci 6.8, failing Hold-down force (PS-10) 1.276): Type I–III, BT-54 and Type IV fail the LL deflection at 10 ksi (rejected); #1 PCI BT-63: Interior 36 strands (6 draped), f′c 8.5 / f′ci 7.8; Exterior 34 (6 draped), 9.5 / 9.3; #2 PCI BT-72: 32 (6) 6.5 / 6.3 and 30 (6) 7.5 / 7.3; #3 AASHTO Type V. After Apply of #1 the Summary shows PASS, 0 FAIL (smoke).
### How verified
- See the PR (Node exhaustive cases, 19 harness designs, smoke, harness B).
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- AD-D1. The sections are searched (the parent request); docs/ps-bridge-plan.md §4 had "section fixed". Lock "Girder section" keeps it fixed.
- AD-D2. The owner's library: MassDOT → MassDOT sections only; any other owner → every non-MassDOT section; the same family; adjacent members (boxes, slabs) the same width (their width sets the girder lines; the cross-section is not changed).
- AD-D3. The strand count is searched at the entered f′c / f′ci first (plan §4 step 1), then the entered f′c with its highest f′ci, then the highest f′c and f′ci; the fewest strands at the first of these that has a passing pattern, then the lowest f′c and f′ci at that pattern (so fewer strands needing a stronger concrete are not preferred while a pattern passes at the entered strengths).
- AD-D4. Symmetric pairs: every straight row and the drape hold even counts (a row of odd capacity holds one less).
- AD-D5. Draped strands at midspan sit directly above the top straight row (the drawn bundle never overlaps a straight row); y_end on the 2 in grid; frac by 0.01.
- AD-D6. Rows with a capacity below 4 strands are not used (no straight strands up the web); entered top strands (rows in the upper half) are kept as entered.
- AD-D7. No plant f′ci limit by default (the setting is blank); RIDOT's f′ci ≈ 0.70 f′c (a warning in the engine) is applied as a limit; f′ci not below 4.0 ksi.
- AD-D8. Assumed monotone (pending review): a higher f′c / f′ci is not worse for any check; a higher y_end relieves the end (the bisection); more strands improve only GROW. The Node exhaustive cases confirm the result on two small cases.
- AD-D9. A span with no passing section has no Apply; its blocked checks are listed. The Report has no "Auto design basis" section yet (plan §4): a later PR.

## 2026-11-14 — Item B: the Drawings tab, part 2 — each girder type's elevation and strand pattern sheets and the strand and girder schedule, DXF and print as part 1 (display and export only)
PR #1563: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1563
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up item B (Drawings part 2, after the auto design): strand pattern and girder elevation sheets and a strand / girder schedule.
  - Strand pattern sheets: the sections at midspan and at the end, with the strand grid and the debonded and draped strands.
  - Girder elevation sheets: the hold-down points, the debond lengths and the camber.
  - The sheets are modelled on the Steel Bridge app's girder sheets. They reuse the app's figure code and the part 1 sheet frame (PR #1560) and load shared/dxf.js unchanged.
- Every dimension comes from the existing model and figure data. DXF download and print work as in part 1. The "Not in this set" part-2 line is removed. No calculation change.
### What changed
- `ui/sheets.js` (`PSBSheets`): new `typeModels(P, opt)`, `elevation(D, C)`, `strands(D, C)`, `schedule(D, C)`. In `build()`, the line `miss.push(['GIRDER, STRAND AND ELEVATION SHEETS', 'PART 2 (AFTER THE AUTO DESIGN), NOT YET'])` is replaced by:
  - for each girder type with lines, the sheets `elev<k>` "GIRDER <LABEL>: ELEVATION" (kmin 12) and `strd<k>` "GIRDER <LABEL>: STRAND PATTERN" (kmin 2);
  - then `sched` "STRAND AND GIRDER SCHEDULE" (kmin 1; the table is fitted to the paper's width).
  - New `opt.res(k, g)`: the page's cached result. Without it, the sheets compute the same call (`PSBHoldDown.compute` of `PSBDesign.cellInputs`).
  - Data, for each type on its first line:
    - outline `halfPolygon(R.g)`, mirrored, and voids `sectionVoids(R.g)`;
    - strand positions `PSBStrandGfx.pattern(R, end)`;
    - rows, draped strands and hold-down points from `R.ss`, as in ui/sumelev.js;
    - L = `R.L`; e_end = `opt.endOh`;
    - camber `R.cam` (rel, erect, afterDeck, seat, final);
    - weight w_sw (L + 2 e_end / 12), as `PSBBridge.results`.
  - Elevation:
    - true length, with the depth exaggerated × round(L_g / 5h) (noted on the sheet);
    - ℄ bearings and midspan;
    - a line per strand row, with the debonded lengths dashed (as ui/sumelev.js draws them);
    - the draped profile and the hold-down points;
    - DIMENSIONs: hold-down from ℄ bearing (frac L) and from the girder end (frac L + e_end, PS-13); ℄ bearing to ℄ bearing; the girder length;
    - notes: the camber at release, at erection, after the deck, at the beam seat and final, and the weight.
  - Strand pattern:
    - sections at ℄ bearing (the girder end) and at midspan, true scale;
    - symbols: bonded strand (double circle), debonded at the end (circle with X), draped strand (circle with a dot);
    - DIMENSIONs: the row chain from the soffit, Y END / Y MID, H and the bottom width;
    - the counts.
  - Schedule: one row per type with:
    - type, span, lines, section, L, strands and size;
    - straight rows, debonded rows, draped strands (n, y_end / y_mid);
    - hold-down from ℄ bearing / from the end;
    - f′c / f′ci, camber at release / erection, weight.
  - New layers: S-STRD, S-STRD-DEBOND, S-STRD-DRAPE, S-TBL.
- `ui/drawings.js`:
  - builds with `res: ctx.res` (and the half-size print the same);
  - the heading no longer says "part 1";
  - index links for elev (Girders & strands, Camber & deflection, End zone & hold-down), strd (Girders & strands, Losses, Stresses) and sched (Girders & strands, Materials, Camber & deflection);
  - the layer and source note.
- `index.html`: the part-2 note under the tab is removed; `PSBDrawingsUI.render(…, { …, res: (k, g) => cellR(PSBDesign.cellInputs(P, k, g)) })`; the script comment.
- `ui/summary.js`: the note names the Drawings' sheets.
- Tests:
  - `psbridge-drawings.test.mjs`: the sheet list includes part 2 and nothing is left out. New test "part 2": every dimension equals its engine value, as does the strand count per section and the schedule row of each type.
  - New smoke `ps-bridge-drawings2.mjs` (7 checks).
  - `ps-bridge-drawings.mjs`: the sheet lists and "Not in this set" updated.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key or field. `ui.dwg` as in part 1.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed: display and export only. Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- New project (BT-72, 120 ft, Interior S1 and Exterior S1, 40 strands with 12 draped, y_end 60 in, y_mid 8 in, frac 0.40, e_end 0):
  - elevation: CL BRG TO CL BRG 120'-0"; HOLD-DOWN 48'-0" FROM CL BRG; 48'-0" FROM GIRDER END; vertical scale × 4 (L_g / 5h = 1440 / (5 × 72) = 4);
  - strand pattern: 28 bonded and 12 draped (40 strands); H = 6'-0";
  - schedule: INTERIOR S1 | 1 | G2 G3 G4 | PCI BT-72 | 120.00 | 40 0.6" | 10@2.00, 10@4.00, 8@6.00 | - | 12, 60.00 / 8.00 | 48.00 / 48.00 | 8.50 / 6.80 | camber 2.90 / 5.15 | 99.1 kip.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- DW2-D1. One elevation and one strand pattern sheet per girder type, drawn from the type's first line: the strands, the profile and the release / erection camber do not depend on the line. The camber after the deck, at the beam seat and final are those of that line (named on the sheet).
- DW2-D2. The elevation is drawn at true length with the depth exaggerated (× round(L_g / 5h), noted), so its vertical dimensions are text, not DIMENSION entities.
- DW2-D3. The debonded lengths are drawn as on the Summary elevation (ui/sumelev.js) and labelled with the entered length.
- DW2-D4. The schedule is one row per girder type (the same girder on every line listed); each line's camber after the deck is on the Camber & deflection tab.
### Other copies
- None new: the sheet frame is part 1's adapted copy of the steel app's `sheet()` (unchanged here).

## 2026-11-15 — Batch A: display bugs and stale text — Report References, the Rating tab's RF chips, §1's "99.000", the Flexure Components chart, stale placeholders, the footer (display only; no calculation change)
PR #1569: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1569
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up batch A (review 2026-11-15, ps-vs-steel O16, O19, L15, R7; old-vs-new #109, #134). Display bugs and stale text; no calculation change.
### What changed
- `report/builders.js` `refsOf(B)` (the References table on the Report's cover):
  - before: 'PCI Bridge Design Manual and the Mast method (handling stability screening)'. That contradicted the Handling tab, which says the stability is a screening and not the PCI / Mast method.
  - after: built from what the report works:
    - AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024): every article the worked steps cite (each step's `ref`, every worked unit), sorted. Equation and table suffixes are dropped, e.g. "Eq. 5.9.3.3-1" is listed as 5.9.3.3. This restores the old app's article list.
    - MBE: the articles cited, with the existing note that the labels are the old app's (MBE 4th Ed. labels: their own change).
    - PCI Design Handbook: the long-term camber multipliers ("edition not stated by the old app: verify", as in the old app's References). Listed when the Camber steps cite it.
    - Handling: listed when the handling steps exist. Text: the lateral deflection z_o uses the Mast expression; the factors of safety are a simplified screening, not the PCI (2016) / Mast method.
    - The owner's manual row is unchanged.
  - New helpers: `artKey`, `artCmp`, `citedArts(B, re)`.
- `ui/outkit.js`: new `groups(list, topics)`. It wraps `SharedSteps.group`.
  - A topic with `rf: RegExp` gets a rating-factor status:
    - result step and chip: the lowest RF of the topic's RF steps ("RF 1.737"; 99, the engine's "not applicable", is left out; all 99: "RF —");
    - `cls`: 'ng' when an RF step has ok false, else 'ok'.
  - `steps()` uses it.
  - `report/builders.js` `gsteps` uses `PSBOutKit.groups` too, so the Report's topic chips match the tab.
  - Why: `shared/steps.js` group() reads any unitless step with an ok flag as demand / capacity, so the largest value governs and anything over 1 is red. The flexure topic's operating RF (2.252 on the default project, 2.407 on the reviewed design) was shown red.
  - `shared/steps.js` is unchanged (no other tool affected).
- `ui/rating.js` TOPICS: `rf` regex added to:
  - flex: `/^rt\.RF(inv|opr)$/`;
  - shear: `/^rt\.RFv(Inv|Opr)$/`;
  - s3: `/^rt\.RFs3$/`;
  - veh: `/^rt\.veh\d+\.RF$/`.
- `report/builders.js` `summary()`, the §1 rating table:
  - an RF ≥ 99 (the engine's "not applicable") is shown "—", as on the Rating tab (before: "99.000");
  - the note now says "— = not applicable" (before: "99 = not applicable").
- `ui/flexure.js`: `HIDE = {}`. Every series of both charts is shown at first, as in the steel app's charts (`S.hide {}`). Before, every Components series was hidden, so the chart was drawn empty. The label's "select them below" is removed.
- `index.html`:
  - the "Girder library … PR 4, waits for the sheets (PS-2)" placeholder card is removed: the library has been merged (PS-37);
  - new footer `#appFoot`, as the old app's `.footer`: "Prestressed Bridge Design v3.0-dev (new, in development) · AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) · units: kip, in, ksi" and "Design aid — independent verification by a licensed engineer required". It is hidden when the Report is printed alone.
- `engine/fields.js` (not a pbd-* file): the Girder shape card's subtitle. Before: "PCI / AASHTO shapes (the old app's library)". After: "girder library by owner: AASHTO / PCI, PCI Northeast NEXT, MassDOT, CTDOT; or Custom".
- New test `tests/engine/psbridge-display-a.test.mjs` (20 cases).

- None changed: display only; no formula, factor or value. Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- New project (PCI BT-72, 120 ft, Interior S1 on G2):
  - Rating tab topic chips, before: Flexure "2.252" red (the operating RF read as a ratio), Shear "2.120" red, Service III "1.430" red.
  - After: Flexure "RF 1.737" green (RF_inv 1.737 < RF_opr 2.252), Shear "RF 1.635" green, Service III "RF 1.430" green.
  - Hand check: the lowest of the topic's RFs (1.737, 2.252) is 1.737 ≥ 1.0, so green.
- Box BIII-36 with a 6 in topping (test case): Service III RF = 99 (net compression). §1's table, before "99.000", after "—"; the Rating tab already shows "—".
- References of the new project:

### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- A-D1. The footer's version text "v3.0-dev" (the old app is v2.65). It is a name for the new app until a numbering is chosen.
- A-D2. The References list the articles the worked steps cite, not a hand-kept list, so the list always matches what is worked. An article cited only in a tab's prose (not in a step) is not listed.
- A-D3. A rating topic's chip shows the lowest RF of the topic ("RF x.xxx"). It is red only when an RF is < 1.0. The steel app shows no chip on its RF topic (its RF steps have no ok flag).

- None.

## 2026-11-15 — Batch B: the Steel Bridge app's formats — amber / REVIEW statuses, stat tiles 3 across with § links, graphics in titled cards, plain type / line picker, Download DXF on each result graphic, girder elevation coloured by governing ratio (Flexure, Shear), the 390 px section figure (display and export only)
PR #1570: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1570
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up batch B (review 2026-11-15, ps-vs-steel L4, L5, L9, L13, L14, L17, O8, O15). Format the result tabs as the Steel Bridge app does. Display and export only.
### What changed
- `ui/summary.js`: each check cell's class comes from the engine's own pass and ratio, through `stOf(q)`:
  - s-fail: the engine's FAIL;
  - s-review: the engine passes the check but its ratio is not finite (REVIEW, the steel Summary's rule for a ratio that is not finite);
  - s-hi: PASS with a ratio from 0.90 to 1.00 (amber; the 0.90 threshold of the steel app's ratio colours, of this app's Report 'hi' and of the step chips);
  - s-pass.
  - The grid, the type × group table and the governing-check tables use it. CSS s-review / s-hi as the steel s-review.
  - The verdict: FAIL / REVIEW / PASS badge and counts. `model()` returns `nR`; `nP` counts PASS with a finite ratio.
- `ui/dash.js`:
  - `stG(all)`: a group is FAIL / REVIEW / PASS as above;
  - `stC(c)`: the class of each listed check;
  - a PASS chip with a governing ratio ≥ 0.90 gets `sd-hi` (amber border and value);
  - REVIEW is counted (`sdW`); the verdict is FAIL / REVIEW / PASS.
  - The CSS of `sd-hi` is in `index.html`.
  - No engine check changes status: a check the engine fails stays FAIL whatever its ratio.
- `ui/vizkit.js` `tiles()`:
  - 3 across (`.vk-tiles` repeat(3); before 6);
  - the value and its unit on one line in `.vk-tv` (white-space: nowrap);
  - the label rule is now `.vk-tile>span:first-child`. Before, `.vk-tile span{display:block}` also hit the value's own data-ev span, which put the unit on the next line;
  - value font 12.5 pt;
  - a § link: `t.link`, else `PSBVizKit.tileLink(path)`. The page sets it around each tab's `after()` to `PSBOutKit.tileLinker($('out'), ctx)`, which finds, in order:
    - the § the tab writes next to the same value (a data-ev span outside the graphics followed by a.wk);
    - else the step whose engine path it is (`ctx.W[*].paths`);
    - else, for a check ratio `checks.<i>.r`, that check's step (ui/dash.js GROUPS).
- `ui/outkit.js`:
  - `tileLinker`, as above;
  - `gcard(title, id)`: a result graphic's slot in a titled card (`section.sec.gfxCard`).
  - Every result tab's top-level graphic slot is now in one, e.g. "Section graphic", "Load rating: rating factors" (ui/section, loads, analysis, losses, stresses, flexure, shear, endzone, camber, handling, deck, rating).
  - `report/fromtab.js` reads a `gfxCard` as its slot alone, so the Report is unchanged. The page hides a gfxCard left empty.
- `ui/types.js` `outBar`:
  - the girder type / line picker is a plain line, as the steel `#gBar`: "Girder type … on line … checked on G2, G3, G4; every line in the Summary · Girder types";
  - `.tyOut` CSS without the box (`index.html`);
  - ids `tyOutT` / `tyOutL` unchanged.
- New `ui/svgdxf.js` (`window.PSBGraphics`): Download DXF of a graphic as drawn.
  - Every line, polyline, polygon, rect, circle, path and text of its SVG becomes a DXF R12 entity through `shared/dxf.js` (unchanged).
  - Units: the graphic's own units, y up. Layers PSB-<kind>-<class>.
  - `download()` validates first (`SharedDxf.validate`), as the steel `SBDGraphics.download`.
  - No `textW`: the charts' text widths are unchanged.
- `ui/vizkit.js` `detCard` and `ui/vizalong.js` `mount`: Download DXF on every graphic. It uses `o.dxf` when given, else the graphic as drawn (`PSBGraphics.fromFig`), with the note `PSBGraphics.NOTE`. The "DXF comes with PR 7" comments are removed.
- New `ui/ratioelev.js` (`window.PSBRatioElev`): the girder elevation coloured by governing ratio, as the steel Flexure / Shear elevation:
  - one band per station: the stretch to the mid-points of its neighbours;
  - neighbours of one class merged and labelled with their largest ratio;
  - green below 0.90, amber 0.90 to 1.00, red above 1.00;
  - the engine's governing check flagged.
  - Flexure (`#gfxr_fx`): M_u / φM_n at the chart's stations (the ratio its read-out shows), flag = the Flexure check, § fx.gov.
  - Shear (`#gfxr_sh`): the engine's d/c of each design station, flag = the Shear check, § sh.gov.
  - Slots `gfxr_*` are screen only (not Report figures).
- `ui/section.js` `figure()`: on a narrow card (W < 560) the y_b / y_bc / y_ps labels go above each line at its right end (short text, halo), and maxH = max(300, 1.1 W). At 390 px the section is drawn at the card's width (before about 120 px).
- `index.html`: the scripts ui/ratioelev.js and ui/svgdxf.js; `VK.tileLink` set around `after()`; empty gfxCards hidden; CSS.
- Tests:
  - new `tests/engine/psbridge-display-b.test.mjs` (22): the Summary classes and counts vs the engine and the column, the gfxCard in the Report, the tiles;
  - new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-display.mjs`.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key or field.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. Display and export only.
- Every ratio shown is the engine's. The flexure elevation's band ratio is M_u / φM_n of the engine's stations, the quotient the chart's read-out already shows.
- Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- New project:
  - Summary: Release stresses 0.944 (Release comp at x = 48 ft) PASS, now amber (s-hi; before green); its column chip is amber (sd-hi). Counts 2 FAIL / 38 PASS, unchanged.
  - Flexure elevation: governs 0.752 at x = 60 ft (= the Flexure check).
  - Shear elevation: governs 0.721 at x = 30.01 ft (= the Shear check).
  - Hand check of one band: x = 60 ft, M_u / φM_n = the read-out's ratio at that station.

diff --git a/apps/ps-bridge/ui/ratioelev.js b/apps/ps-bridge/ui/ratioelev.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cb1ab36
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/ps-bridge/ui/ratioelev.js
@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/ratioelev.js — window.PSBRatioElev: "Girder elevation coloured by governing ratio" on a check tab (2026-11-15, batch B;
+   the steel app's elevation of the Flexure / Shear tabs, apps/steel-bridge/ui/alonggfx.js: one band per station of the check's table, the
+   stretch to the mid-points of its neighbours, neighbouring bands of one colour class merged and labelled with their largest ratio; green
+   below 0.90, amber 0.90 to 1.00, red above 1.00; a flag at the governing check). Classic script, display only: the ratios are the tab's
+   own (each tab hands in its stations and the ratio its read-out or table shows, e.g. the engine's shear d/c, M_u / φM_n of the flexure
+   read-out); the governing check is the engine's (R.checks: its x and ratio).
+     svg(W, o) -> { svg, nar }   o = { L (ft), pts: [{ x, r }], gov: { x, r, name }, label (the band's title) }
+     mount(slot, o)              a PSBVizKit.detCard (title, read-out of each band, Download DXF as every graphic) */
+(function () {
+  'use strict';
+  const esc = s => String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' }[c]));
+  const fin = v => typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v);
+  const cls = r => !fin(r) || r > 1 + 1e-9 ? 'ng' : r >= 0.9 ? 'hi' : 'ok';
+  const COL = { ok: ['#E3F4EA', '#2F6E4E'], hi: ['#FEF3C7', '#8A5A0B'], ng: ['#FDE2E1', '#A3322A'] };
+  const f2 = v => (fin(v) ? v.toFixed(2) : v === Infinity ? '∞' : 'NaN'), f3 = v => (fin(v) ? v.toFixed(3) : v === Infinity ? '∞' : 'NaN');
+  const nice = (span, n) => { const r = span / n, p = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(r))), m = r / p; return (m < 1.5 ? 1 : m < 3.5 ? 2 : m < 7.5 ? 5 : 10) * p; };
+  /* the merged bands: [{ x0, x1, c, r (largest), i0, i1 }] */
+  function bands(L, pts) {
+    const P = pts.filter(q => fin(q.x)).slice().sort((a, b) => a.x - b.x), out = [];
+    P.forEach((q, i) => { const x0 = i ? (P[i - 1].x + q.x) / 2 : 0, x1 = i < P.length - 1 ? (q.x + P[i + 1].x) / 2 : L, c = cls(q.r), b = out[out.length - 1];
+      if (b && b.c === c) { b.x1 = x1; if (!fin(b.r) || !fin(q.r) ? !fin(q.r) : q.r > b.r) { b.r = q.r; b.xr = q.x; } b.n++; } else out.push({ x0, x1, c, r: q.r, xr: q.x, n: 1 }); });
+    return out;
+  }
+  function svg(W, o) {
+    const L = o.L, l = 14, r = 14, X = x => l + Math.max(0, Math.min(L, x)) / L * (W - l - r), nar = W < 560;
+    const yG = 34, hG = 22, yB = yG + hG + 34, hB = 22, yA = yB + hB + 30, H = yA + 30;
+    let s = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" width="${W}" height="${H}" role="img" aria-label="${esc(o.label || 'Girder elevation coloured by governing ratio')}" font-family="Arial,sans-serif">`;
+    // the girder and its bearings
+    s += `<rect class="re-g" x="${X(0)}" y="${yG}" width="${X(L) - X(0)}" height="${hG}" fill="#E2E8F0" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="1" data-dtr="Girder, ℄ bearing to ℄ bearing L = ${f2(L)} ft"/>`;
+    [0, L].forEach(x => { s += `<path class="re-s" d="M${X(x)} ${yG + hG} l-6 10 h12 z" fill="#64748B"/>`; });
+    s += `<text x="${(X(0) + X(L)) / 2}" y="${yG - 8}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Span L = ${f2(L)} ft (℄ bearing to ℄ bearing)</text>`;
+    // the band
+    s += `<text x="${X(0)}" y="${yB - 8}" font-size="11" fill="#0F172A">${esc(o.label || 'Governing ratio')}</text>`;
+    bands(L, o.pts).forEach(b => { const [fl, st] = COL[b.c], x0 = X(b.x0), w = Math.max(1, X(b.x1) - x0);
+      s += `<rect class="re-${b.c}" x="${x0.toFixed(1)}" y="${yB}" width="${w.toFixed(1)}" height="${hB}" fill="${fl}" stroke="${st}" stroke-width="0.8" data-dtr="x = ${f2(b.x0)} to ${f2(b.x1)} ft: largest ratio ${f3(b.r)} at x = ${f2(b.xr)} ft (${b.n} station${b.n === 1 ? '' : 's'}; ${b.c === 'ok' ? 'below 0.90' : b.c === 'hi' ? '0.90 to 1.00' : 'above 1.00'})"/>`;
+      if (w > (nar ? 28 : 34)) s += `<text x="${(x0 + w / 2).toFixed(1)}" y="${yB + 15}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="600" fill="${st}" pointer-events="none">${f2(b.r)}</text>`;
+      // the same colour on the girder
+      s += `<rect x="${x0.toFixed(1)}" y="${yG + 2}" width="${w.toFixed(1)}" height="${hG - 4}" fill="${fl}" opacity="0.85" pointer-events="none"/>`; });
+    // the governing check
+    if (o.gov && fin(o.gov.x)) { const gx = X(o.gov.x), gc = COL[cls(o.gov.r)][1], lab = `Governs: ${o.gov.name ? o.gov.name + ' ' : ''}${f3(o.gov.r)} at x = ${f2(o.gov.x)} ft`;
+      s += `<line x1="${gx}" x2="${gx}" y1="${yG - 4}" y2="${yB + hB + 4}" stroke="${gc}" stroke-width="1.6"/>`;
+      s += `<text x="${Math.min(Math.max(gx, l + 4), W - r - 4)}" y="${yB + hB + 18}" text-anchor="${gx > W * 0.6 ? 'end' : gx < W * 0.3 ? 'start' : 'middle'}" font-size="11" font-weight="600" fill="${gc}">${esc(lab)}</text>`; }
+    // the axis
+    const st = nice(L, nar ? 4 : 8); s += `<line x1="${X(0)}" x2="${X(L)}" y1="${yA}" y2="${yA}" stroke="#94A3B8"/>`;
+    for (let x = 0; x <= L + 1e-9; x += st) s += `<line x1="${X(x)}" x2="${X(x)}" y1="${yA}" y2="${yA + 4}" stroke="#94A3B8"/><text x="${X(x)}" y="${yA + 15}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#475569">${+x.toFixed(2)}</text>`;
+    s += `<text x="${X(L)}" y="${yA + 27}" text-anchor="end" font-size="10" fill="#475569">Station x, ft (from ℄ bearing, left)</text></svg>`;
+    return { svg: s, nar };
+  }
+  const LEG = '<p class="vk-cap"><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:9px;background:#E3F4EA;border:1px solid #2F6E4E"></span> below 0.90 &nbsp; <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:9px;background:#FEF3C7;border:1px solid #8A5A0B"></span> 0.90 to 1.00 &nbsp; <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:9px;background:#FDE2E1;border:1px solid #A3322A"></span> above 1.00</p>';
+  function mount(slot, o) {
+    const VK = window.PSBVizKit; if (!slot || !VK || !VK.detCard) return null;
+    return VK.detCard(slot, { id: o.id, title: o.title || 'Girder elevation coloured by governing ratio', sub: o.sub || '', draw: W => { const q = svg(W, o); return { html: q.svg, nar: q.nar }; },
+      hint: 'Point at (or tap) a band to read its stations and ratio.', cap: LEG + (o.cap || ''), file: o.file });
+  }
+  window.PSBRatioElev = { svg, mount, bands, cls };
+})();

+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/svgdxf.js — window.PSBGraphics: "Download DXF" of the result tabs' graphics (2026-11-15, batch B; the steel app's
