```diff
+     PSBGraphics.fromSvg(svg, o) -> { D, file, title }   svg: an <svg> element on the page (or a container: its first svg); o = { title, file }

+  const SKIP = new Set(['defs', 'clippath', 'mask', 'pattern', 'marker', 'title', 'desc', 'style', 'script', 'lineargradient', 'radialgradient', 'filter', 'symbol']);
+  const num = v => { const n = parseFloat(v); return isFinite(n) ? n : 0; };

+    return D.layer('PSB-' + kind + (c ? '-' + c : ''), kind === 'TEXT' ? 7 : kind === 'FILL' ? 8 : 7); };

+  function pathPolys(d) {
```

### Tests
- check-syntax: all pass.
- `node tests/engine/run.mjs psbridge tex project-registry`: 40 files, 415 passed (the new psbridge-display-b 22; psbridge-model's script list gets ui/ratioelev.js and ui/svgdxf.js).
- Harness B: 48,347 shown and 8,392 step values, 0 differences (normal and --import); --control exits 1.
- Smokes: skeleton 271, types 106, 3d 101, figures 225, library 11, undo 7, drawings 6, drawings2 7, autodesign 7, handoffs 12, display 8; 0 console errors.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- B-D1. Amber on PASS ratios 0.90 to 1.00 in the Summary table and the check summary column, as the review asked. The steel app colours 0.90–1.00 amber in its elevations and step chips. Its Summary cells are amber only for REVIEW: there a 0.997 is green.
- B-D2. REVIEW is given only to a check the engine passes whose ratio is not finite. A check the engine fails stays FAIL even when its ratio is NaN; the steel app would count that REVIEW. This is the conservative choice.
- B-D3. Download DXF writes the graphic as drawn (screen units, not a drawing scale), not a hand-built CAD drawing as in the steel app. The scaled sheets are on the Drawings tab.
- B-D4. The ratio elevation is on Flexure (M_u / φM_n at the chart's stations) and Shear (the engine's d/c at the design stations) only. The Stresses tab has no per-station ratio from the engine; its checks are worked at their governing stations.
- B-D5. A tile whose value is not worked by a step (e.g. the library's A, I, y_b on Section properties) has no § link.
### Other copies
- `ui/vizkit.js` and `ui/vizalong.js` are adapted copies of the steel app's files. The tile layout (3 across, `.vk-tv`) and the Download DXF of the graphic as drawn differ from the steel copies; the steel files are unchanged.
## 2026-11-15 — PSLT: a list edit is committed before another click or change acts (the Steel Bridge app's fix, PR #1568; input only, no calculation change)
PR #1571: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1571
### Request
- The PS Bridge app's copy of `ui/lists.js` should get the same fix as Steel's (PR #1568, its open item of PR #1561): a pending list-table edit should always be committed, including for the lists drawn only in some states.
- Reproduce in a smoke first.
### Problem
- The table edit is committed in a `focusout` handler deferred by `setTimeout(…, 0)`.
- A click or change elsewhere that is handled before that commit runs acts on the project without the edit. Two cases reproduce on origin/main (new smoke, below):
  - **Lost edit.** Cross-section tab, a girder spacing typed, then Girder spacing changed to Equal. The bay list is not drawn in Equal mode, so after the redraw no input of the same id exists for the commit. W_cc was taken as Σ of the old bays, and the edit was lost.
  - **Undo in the wrong order.** Bridge layout tab, a skew typed, then the Undo button clicked. Undo took back the step before, and the deferred commit then wrote the skew after it, as a step that Redo could not reach.
- The PS app has no list drawn only while its own tab is open: spans, skews and bays are on panes that are always drawn. The cases above are the lists drawn only in some states.
### Where
- `apps/ps-bridge/ui/lists.js`, `bind()` (anchor `ctl.el.addEventListener('focusout', () => setTimeout(() => {`) and `start()` (anchor `upgrade(document);`).
- Before (`bind`):
  ```js
      ctl.el.addEventListener('focusout', () => setTimeout(() => {   // after the event: a redraw (Enter, ×) moves the focus within the table
        if (ctl.el.isConnected && ctl.el.contains(document.activeElement)) return;
        if (el.value === was) return; was = el.value;
        // one change from the steel copy: …
        let t = el; if (!el.isConnected) { t = document.getElementById(el.id); if (!t) return; t.value = el.value; }
        t.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
      }, 0));
      el._sli = ctl;
  ```
- After:
  - the commit body moved unchanged into `const commit = () => { … }`;
  - the focusout handler calls `commit()`;
  - `BOUND.add({ el, ctl, commit })` follows `el._sli = ctl;`;
  - new, above `bind`: `const BOUND = new Set(); let flushing = false;`;
  - new, after `bind`:
  ```js
    function flush(target) {
      if (flushing) return;
      flushing = true;
      try {
        BOUND.forEach(b => {
          if (!b.el.isConnected) { BOUND.delete(b); return; }   // redrawn: its deferred focusout (above) still commits a pending edit
          if (target && target.nodeType === 1 && (target === b.el || b.ctl.el.contains(target))) return;
          b.commit();
        });
      } finally { flushing = false; }
    }
  ```
  - in `start()`, after `upgrade(document);`:
  ```js
      ['click', 'change'].forEach(t => document.addEventListener(t, e => flush(e.target), true));   // PSLT: before the page's handlers
  ```
  - `W.PSBListsUI = { LISTS, upgrade, flush };`
- How it works: a click or change anywhere outside a table commits that table's pending edit first. The listener is in the capture phase on the document, so it runs before the page's own handlers. The page's own handler then reads the edit before that click or change acts.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None. The page's own change handler writes the same fields in the same formats.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. Input handling only; no formula, factor or value changed. Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case (new project, `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-list-commit.mjs`)
- **Bays then Equal.** Bays 9, 9, 9, 9; bay 1 typed 9.5, then Girder spacing → Equal.
  - Saved `xs.Wcc` before: **36** (the edit lost).
  - After: **36.5** = 9.5 + 9 + 9 + 9.
- **Skew then Undo.** Skews 0, 0; skew 1 typed 12, then Undo.
  - Before: the skews stayed "12, 0" and Redo was disabled. Undo took back the step before, and the skew was written after it.
  - After: "0, 0", and Redo gives [12, 0].
- **Span then input tab.** Span 120 → 121, then an input-tab click: saved [121] before and after (PR #1548's case).
### How verified
- `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-list-commit.mjs`: 5 checks. On origin/main 3 fail; with the fix 5 of 5 pass, 0 console errors.
- PS checks: see the PR.
### Other copies
- `apps/steel-bridge/ui/lists.js` (PR #1568): the same code. The two copies differ only in comments, the selector list and the namespace.

## 2026-11-15 — Batch C: the tables the Steel Bridge app has — dead loads and LLDF of every girder line, Analysis reactions / loads and factors used / girder elevation, Report "every station" detail and §1 girder elevations (display only)
PR #1572: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1572
### Request
- PS Bridge catch-up batch C (review 2026-11-15, ps-vs-steel O10, O12, O13, O14, R4, R6).
- Add the steel app's tables from existing engine results; no new formula. Display only.
### What changed
- `ui/loads.js`: new `everyLine(ctx)`, a card "Dead loads and distribution factors of every girder line".
  - One row per girder type × line of every span, from `ctx.all`. That is engine/bridge.js results, the page's cached results of every type × line; each line has its own computeAll, the same objects the Summary uses.
  - Columns: w_g, w_DC1 (`R.wDk`), DC2 (`R.wBar`), DW (`R.wDW`), DF_M, DF_V, fatigue DF (`R.fat.dfFat`), and the LLDF method (interior equations / exterior lever rule, e, rigid / type (f)/(g) / entered).
  - Each value has a § (`data-sumgo` k|g|tab|step) that opens its tab with that type and line at the step that works it: `sec.g.wsw`, `ld.wDC1`, `ld.wDC2` or `dl.G<g>.DC2`, `ld.wDW` or `dl.G<g>.DW`, `ld.dfm`, `ld.dfv`, `st.fat.df`.
  - Not in the Report: the report's tab sections have no `ctx.all`; §1 lists every type and line.
- `index.html`: `ctxOut.all = rc.all`.
- `ui/analysis.js`:
  - `usedCard(ctx)`, "Loads and factors used": w_g, w_DC1, P_dia, DC2, DW, DF_M / DF_V, η / m, as engine values (data-ev), each with its §; and the load combinations' steps (an.MuS, an.MsI, an.MsIII).
  - `reactions(ctx)`, "Reactions (unfactored, kip)":
    - the engine's own `bxSuperRxPayload` (engine/handoffs.js `srPayload`), the numbers "Send reactions to Substructure Loading" sends: DC1, DC2, DW per support and, simple span, the LL per lane for information;
    - worked in the note with the same numbers: DC1 = (w_g + w_DC1) L / 2 + Σ P (L − a) / L; DC2 = w L / 2, or on a continuous unit w × V_w(0); LL = max(V_tr, V_td) + V_ln; each term linked.
  - `elevSvg` / the "Girder elevation" card (slot `gfxr_anel`, screen only): the span, bearings, diaphragm point loads, continuous ends.
- `report/builders.js`:
  - `tabSec` passes `ui: { every: true }` when `opt.every`;
  - `elevSub(X)` puts the figures of `opt.sumFig` in §1 ("Girder elevations: where each check governs"), with the list of the checks drawn;
  - X gets `sumFig` and `every`.
- `ui/report.js`:
  - the Detail choice ("the stations the tabs tabulate" / "every station"), kept in `ui.rpt.detail` (psb2.ui; a new field of the existing UI object, default the tabulated stations);
  - `sumFig(B, wScr)`: the Summary's girder elevation of each type on its governing line (ui/sumelev.js model + svg, links removed) at the printed width.
- `ui/analysis.js`, `ui/stresses.js`, `ui/flexure.js`: with `ui.every` the station tables list every engine station. Before / default: analysis every 6th station; stresses the tenth points; flexure the twentieth points to midspan.
- Tests:
  - new `tests/engine/psbridge-display-c.test.mjs` (20): every value of the line table vs each cell's engine result and its link; the reactions vs bxSuperRxPayload with the DC2 = w L / 2 hand check; "every station" lists every station with each recorded value equal to the engine's; the default is unchanged; §1's figure;
  - new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-tables.mjs`.
- `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-skeleton.mjs`: the Report-figures check now expects the §1 girder elevations (before it required none in §1; test only).

### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- No key added or renamed. `psb2.ui` (the page's UI object, per browser) gets the optional `rpt.detail` ('all' or absent). An older psb2.ui without it opens with the default detail.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. Every value is an engine value. The reactions are the engine's hand-off function (AASHTO statics as the old app's BXSuperRx), shown with their working.
- Harness B: 0 differences. The Report now records more values in its Analysis section (Loads and factors used), each compared equal.
### Check case
- New project, Interior S1 on G2, simple span L = 120.00 ft:
  - Support 1 DC1 = (w_g + w_DC1) L / 2 = (0.8256 + w_DC1)(120.00) / 2, as the table shows;
  - DC2 = w_DC2 (120.00) / 2;
  - the test checks |DC2 − w_DC2 L / 2| < 0.001 kip on every design.
- Loads & LLDF line table: 5 rows (G1–G5), G2 marked shown. A § on G5's DF_M opens Exterior S1 on G5 at step ld.dfm.
- Report Detail "every station": the Analysis table 12 → 63 rows (every 6th station + midspan → every station); Stresses → every grid station; Flexure → every flexFull station.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- C-D1. The line table is on the tab only, not in the Report (the Report's §1 already lists every type and line).
- C-D2. Reactions: those of the girder line shown (as the hand-off sends), not of every line. V_w of a continuous unit is the engine's FE end shear per klf (not a worked step; its M_w is).
- C-D3. "Every station" widens the Analysis, Stresses and Flexure station tables. The worked steps stay at the governing stations (the steel app opens each station's steps on demand).
### Other copies
- None.
### Tests
- check-syntax: all pass. Engine `psbridge tex project-registry`: 41 files, 435 passed (new psbridge-display-c 20).
- Harness B: 48,475 shown and 8,392 step values, 0 differences (normal and --import; +128 Report values: the Analysis section's "Loads and factors used", each equal to the old app's); --control exits 1.
- Smokes: skeleton 271, types 106, 3d 101, figures 225, library 11, undo 7, drawings 6, drawings2 7, autodesign 7, handoffs 12, display 8, tables 5 (new); 0 console errors.
## 2026-11-15 — ADB: the Report's "Auto design basis" (§2, last subsection) and a link to it from the Auto design output tab (display only)
PR #1574: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1574
### Request
- Add an "Auto design basis" section to the printed Report, with an on-screen link to it from the Auto design output. It describes, for the run applied or shown:
  - the objective;
  - the sections searched;
  - the strand pattern, drape and f′c / f′ci rules, with the owner limits;
  - the order of preference;
  - the selected candidate and its governing check, with "see §x.y" links to where each check is worked (CLAUDE.md §6).
- Display only: read from PSBAutoDesign / P.autodesign; no calculation change, no new keys. With no run, the section says so.
### What changed
- **`report/builders.js`**
  - New `keysOf(secs)` and `adSub(B, X, A, secs)`, inserted before `planFig`.
  - `model()`: before the dropped-section fix (anchor `// references from the sections shown into a section left out`):
    ```js
    { const ps = secs.find(q => q.id === 'proj'); if (ps) { try { ps.subs.push(adSub(B, X, opt.autodesign || null, secs)); } catch (e) { … } } }
    ```
  - It is built last, so its links point only to the steps of the sections shown (`keysOf`). No number is recorded in `model.vals`.
  - Content, from the run (`PSBAutoDesign` result `R`, its settings `R.o`, `PSBAutoDesign.conc` / `FRACS` / `GROW` / `DEF`, `PSBSections.rowGrid`, `PBD.OWN_RULES`):
    - the run's status (applied or shown; changed since);
    - Objective and variables;
    - Order of preference;
    - Sections searched (the family, owner and width rules, and a table of every section tried with its result);
    - Strand pattern rules (the row grid of the selected section, even counts, rows of fewer than 4 not used, top strands and debonding kept);
    - Drape rules (the frac range);
    - f′c and f′ci grids and limits: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 5.4.2.1, paraphrased, and the owner rules with their section numbers. A table gives each girder type's searched f′c and f′ci range;
    - Assumptions of the search;
    - Selected candidate and its governing check: each girder type's inputs, then a table of every check (ratio, line, status, and "see §" to the step that works it).
  - The topics are numbered 1 to 8 as the viewer's topic sub-headings (`it.topic.no`).
  - How each check's link is chosen (`see()`):
    - the step of the girder type the report works: single report `B.cell.k`; per-type report the unit `u<j>/<step>`;
    - "(worked for G…)" when the line differs;
    - an owner-limit check goes to `rs.own`;
    - a type the report does not work goes to its result tab with that type chosen.
  - With no run: one note ("No auto design was run in this page view: nothing in this report comes from an auto design …"); while a run is under way: one note.
- **`ui/autodesign.js`**
  - `S.ap` (the run applied in this page view, kept on Apply) and `S.rev` (incremented on a finished run and on Apply).
  - New `basis(P)`: the run shown, else the one applied, with `stale`. New `basisKey()`.
  - The output tab's first note links to the Report subsection (`href="#rp:rs.adb" data-gotab="rpt"`).
  - Memory only: nothing stored.
- **`ui/report.js`**
  - Passes `autodesign: PSBAutoDesignUI.basis(P)` to the model.
  - `basisKey()` and `stale` are in the cache key.
  - Keeps the viewer as `state.V`.
- **`index.html`**: the output-panel `[data-gotab]` handler: an href `#rp:<key>` jumps the Report viewer to that key (`state.V.jump`).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key or field. P.autodesign is read only. The applied run is kept in the page view's memory, as the run itself.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed. The basis cites AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 5.4.2.1 (minimum f′c 4.0 ksi for prestressed concrete; provisions based on up to 10.0 ksi) and the owner rules' sections (RIDOT 5.2.1 and 5.6.1; MassDOT 3.7.2.1; CTDOT V2 5.9.1.2), as the Auto design input tab states them. The values are those PSBAutoDesign searches.
- Harness B: 0 differences (no value recorded).
### Check case (new project, Interior S1 + Exterior S1, AASHTO; `tests/engine/psbridge-adbasis.test.mjs`)
- Before a run: §2.7 "Auto design basis" holds one note. The report still has 14 sections, and no other subsection number changes.
- After Run and Apply of candidate #1:
  - Sections searched: AASHTO Type I to Type V and PCI BT-54 / 63 / 72. Type I to III, BT-54 and Type IV give "none (… live-load deflection fails at the highest f′c …)"; BT-63, BT-72 and Type V are candidates #1, #2 and #3.
  - Interior S1 on PCI BT-63: 36 strands (6 draped), straight rows 12 at 2.00, 12 at 4.00 and 6 at 6.00 in; y_end 50.00, y_mid 10.00 in, hold-down at 0.40 L; f′c / f′ci 8.5 / 7.8 ksi.
  - Its governing check: Confinement steel (5.9.4.4.2), ratio 1.000 on G3, "see §10.7 (worked for G2)" (on main c63d974) (the Interior S1 unit's End zone section).
  - The f′c grid is 4.0 to 10.0 ksi (13 values) for both types.
### How verified
- New `tests/engine/psbridge-adbasis.test.mjs` (4 tests): no run; a run applied on the default and on the new project; shown and stale.
- New smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-adbasis.mjs`.
- PS checks: see the PR.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- ADB-D1. **Placement.** The basis is the last subsection of §2 "Project, basis and assumptions", not a new numbered section. Every existing section and subsection number, and every "see §" reference, stays as it was. Leaving §2 out of the Report leaves the basis out too.
- ADB-D2. **No run.** The subsection is kept, with one note saying no auto design was run and that nothing in the report comes from one. It is not omitted, so that the printed report always states it.
- ADB-D3. **Which run.** The run described is the one shown on the Auto design output tab; if none is shown, the one last applied in this page view. The run is memory only (as before), so a reopened project has no run to describe, and the subsection says so. The subsection says when the project has changed since the run or since its Apply.
- ADB-D4. **What "see §" points to.** It points to the step the report works for that girder type, which is the current inputs. After an Apply with no later change, those are the candidate's inputs. Otherwise the text says the report works the current inputs, not the candidate.
### Other copies
- None.

## 2026-11-15 — Batch D1: demand source per girder type — this app's analysis, a custom demand table or a MIDAS demands file (the old app's MIDAS import; a new calculation input path, CLAUDE.md §4)
PR #1573: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1573
### Request
- Engineer-approved plan A→H (2026-11-15), batch D1: the highest-priority parity gap with the old app (review old-vs-new.md rows #34 / #63,
  ps-vs-steel.md I15). An old design that ran on MIDAS envelopes imported into this app but silently used the built-in HL-93
  (ui/inputs.js placeholder; engine/legacy.js refused the file; PS-18 "MIDAS demands stay kept, restored when the MIDAS import arrives").
### What changed
- `apps/ps-bridge/engine/demands.js` (new, `window.PSBDemands`): the demand source of each girder type, saved as the new optional field
  `P.demands = { '<type id>': { src: 'app' | 'table' | 'midas', midas: { file, name, at }, span, table: { rows } } }`. `external(P, T)` gives
  the engine the old app's own input `inputs.external` (the file as read with the span chosen, `_selSpan`; a custom table put in the file's
  form). `parse()` reads a MIDAS file (the old app's import, O:9539-9548, plus: readable stations, `factored: true` refused); `checks()` the
  input errors / warnings; `slice()` / `fac()` the display helpers of the worked steps (buildExternal's rule, pbd-compute.js fac1).
- `engine/design.js` `inputs()` / `cellInputs()`: `withDemands(P, T, o)` adds `o.external` for a type with a file or a table; nothing else.
- `engine/legacy.js`: `convert()` puts an old design's MIDAS demands in `P.demands.T1` (its stored `_selSpan` kept: the engine inputs are the
  old app's); `restore()` gives a restored cell's MIDAS demands to its type (grouped with them); `fromText()` names the Loads tab for a MIDAS
  file. The summary item is now 'ok' ("the demands of this girder design ... as the old app gave them").
- `engine/inputcheck.js`: the demand errors / warnings (scope = the type). `engine/fields.js`: `tabOf('demands.*')` = 'loads'; new card
  `extll` (the old app's DF +M / −M / V and m on imported live load, `loads.extDFpos / extDFneg / extDFv / extLLmpf`, blank = 1.0), shown
  while a type uses a file or a table; the 'll' card note. `engine/model.js`: the field documented; `validate` (an object).
- `ui/demands.js` (new): the Loads tab's Demands card (source select; MIDAS: choose file, "Running on MIDAS demands" banner, span picker,
  "✕ use this app's analysis", the imported values of the span (details); the import guide dialog (the old app's MidasHelp text); the custom
  table with paste from Excel) and the output tabs' source line `srcBar` (the Steel Bridge app's).
- `engine/worked.js`, `engine/worked-strength.js` (display only): with imported demands the steps `ld.xfp / xfn / xfv` (f = DF m),
  `ld.MLL / VLL` (from the file's stations), `an.Mdc2 / an.Mdw` (the linear interpolation), `an.Mll` (f+M M+file); `sh.Vu`'s components on a
  simple span with imported demands (the engine's own, before the w (L/2 − x) formulas, wrong for a file: a display bug of the import path).
- `ui/analysis.js`: "Imported demands of the span" card (as read and as the engine takes them, linked to the Strength I / Service / pier
  steps), "Loads and factors used" and the reactions' working for imported demands. `ui/loads.js`: "Live load from the imported demands"
  card, DC2 / DW rows say the moments and shears are imported. `ui/inputs.js`: the placeholder card removed, the assumption added.
- `index.html`: the two scripts, the card on the Loads tab, its events (change, click, paste), the source line on the output tabs, CSS.
- Display of the demand warnings (not blocking): the Demands card (`#dmWarn`) and the source line (`.srcBar.warn`, "Check: …").
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- New optional field `P.demands` (engine/model.js doc). Absent in every project saved before = every type on this app's analysis: the
  project text is byte-identical through import / export and computes as before (test). No key added or renamed; the old app's keys and
  its MIDAS file format are read only. `psb2.ui` unchanged.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- No formula, factor, unit or reference of the engine changed (engine/pbd-*.js not edited). New calculation input path: the frozen engine's
  own MIDAS path (the old app's, pbd-compute.js `extLL` / `buildExternal`, AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-1 combinations, Art. 5.12.3.3
  continuity at the pier, 4.6.2.2 / 3.6.1.1.2 for the DF and m entered on imported live load) is reachable from the new app.
### Check case (tests/engine/psbridge-midas.test.mjs, "§4 check case")
- Default BT-72 G2, bridge 100 / 120 / 100 ft made continuous, span 2, the old app's test file `tests/projects/ps/midas_3span.json` (its
  span 2: x = 100 to 220 ft), DF +M 0.62, −M 0.68, V 0.74, m 1.0, AASHTO (η = 1, m_LL = 1).
- Midspan x = 60 ft = file station 160: M_DC2 174.64, M_DW 145.54, M+_LL,file 1631.59 kip-ft; M_g 1486.0625, M_DC1 1957.50 (this app).
  M_DC = 3618.2025; M_LL+IM = 0.62 × 1631.59 = 1011.5858; Strength I M_u = 1.25(3618.2025) + 1.50(145.54) + 1.75(1011.5858) = 6511.34 kip-ft.
  Before (this app's continuous unit, w_DC2 0.30, w_DW 0.25 klf, DF_M 0.7191): M_LL 1627.60, M_u 7589.36 kip-ft.
- Pier: file x = 100 / 220: M_DC2 −365.36, M_DW −304.46, M−_LL −1034.51 / −1336.65 → M_LL,n = 0.68 × 1336.65 = 908.92; M_r,n 604.38;
  M_u,n = 1.25(365.36) + 1.50(304.46) + 1.75(908.92) + 604.38 = 3108.38 kip-ft. Before: M_LL,n 1758.40, M_u,n 4594.98 kip-ft.
- Flexure ratio 0.556 → 0.477; Shear 0.639 → 0.389.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- D1-a. One demand source per girder type (the Steel app chooses per check tab; this engine computes one design per type).
- D1-b. L is the bridge span; the file's span is the type's span unless another is chosen; a length difference over 0.005 ft is a warning
  (not blocking), so imported old designs compute as the old app did.
- D1-c. A new file import refuses `factored: true` and stations without x; when the file has as many spans as the bridge and they differ,
  the page asks to set the bridge spans (the old app set L to the span).
- D1-d. The custom table's shears are in this app's sign; converted to the file's sign for the engine.
- D1-e. The fatigue check keeps this app's fatigue truck and DF (as the old app did with MIDAS demands).
### Other copies
- None (the frozen old app is unchanged).
### How verified
- Node: tests/engine/psbridge-midas.test.mjs (new: 5 designs, worked-step pairs, the §4 case by hand, §5 round trip, the file reader, the
  input checks, the table's signs, restore of MIDAS cells); psbridge-legacy (the 658 harness-A old designs: the 57 with MIDAS demands now
  identical to the old app, engine input `external` = the old app's); psbridge-inputs, psbridge-model (script list) updated.
- Harness B with the 5 new designs (tests/engine/psbridge-midas-cases.mjs): every value shown = the old page's own computeAll.
- Smoke tests/smoke/ps-bridge-demands.mjs (new).

Whether the distribution factor or multiple presence is applied depends on the MIDAS model: apply what is missing with the DF per effect and m on the Loads tab (each 1.0 by default). A refined grillage usually has them; a single line-girder model usually needs the DF.</li></ul>
```diff
+    <h4>The components (per girder, per station)</h4><p><code>M_DC2, V_DC2</code> composite superimposed dead load; <code>M_DW, V_DW</code> wearing surface and utilities; <code>M_LLpos / M_LLneg</code> and <code>V_LLpos / V_LLneg</code> the live-load envelope, both branches. DC1 may be in the file but is not used. The girder self-weight should be excluded (<code>selfWeightExcluded: true</code>).</p>
+    <h4>Conventions</h4><ul><li>Units kip, ft, ft-kip (the file's <code>units</code> block).</li><li>Moment sagging-positive; shear signed (not a magnitude), in MIDAS's element sign (the opposite of this app's; the app negates it).</li><li><code>factored: false</code>: unfactored components (a factored file is refused). This app builds Strength I (1.25 DC + 1.50 DW + 1.75 LL), Service I / III and Fatigue.</li>
+    <li>Stations at any spacing, the supports included; the app interpolates linearly.</li><li><code>member.supports</code> (or <code>spans</code>) so the span picker can slice one span, re-zeroed to its left bearing; the moments at the span ends are the pier negative moments of the continuity check.</li></ul>
+    <h4>What this app does on import</h4><p>Checks the schema, reads the spans, takes the span of the girder type (or the one you pick), re-zeros the stationing and gives the engine the file's DC2, DW and LL envelope for the composite stage (the old app's own path, unchanged). Each girder type has its own source and file.</p>
+    <p class="note"><b>Checklist:</b> self-weight excluded · DC1 not included · barrier in DC2 · wearing surface in DW · LL envelope both branches with IM (and DF if your model has it) · signed shear · supports / spans listed · units kip / ft / ft-kip. Schema id <code>psbeam-external-demands</code>, produced by the MCT Generator's "Organize for PS-Beam tool" action. ## 2026-11-15 — Batch D2: the Analysis tab's views of an imported MIDAS member — span n, the entire beam, "Design span n →" (display; the button sets the span of the file used, an input)
```
PR #1575: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1575
### Request
- Engineer-approved plan A→H (2026-11-15), batch D2 (review old-vs-new.md #63, High): the old app's Diagrams tab with an imported member of
  two or more spans ("Prestressed Bridge Design.html" O:8036-8058, 8100-8118): "View span" (design span / span n / entire beam), the
  member's diagrams from the file with Strength I, "Design Span n →".
### What changed
- `apps/ps-bridge/ui/analysis.js`: `viewOf(ctx)`, `viewBar(ctx, V)`, `viewRows(ctx, V)`, `viewOut(ctx, V)` (new, anchor
  `/* ---- batch D2 (2026-11-15): the views of an imported member`): on the page only (the Report keeps the design span), for a type whose
  demands are a MIDAS file of 2 or more spans: the select `#o_dmView` (`ui.dmView`: 'design' | 's<n>' | 'all', in `psb2.ui`, per browser);
  another span or the entire beam shows the file's stations (member coordinates) in a chart (`#gfx_dmview`, the along-girder chart) and a
  table, Strength I as the old app's view: M_u± = η(1.25(M_DC1 + M_DC2) + 1.50 M_DW + 1.75 m M_LL±) (the same for V) of the file's values
  as read, with the worked line of the largest M_u+ and the smallest M_u−; the design span shows a note that the force effects are the
  imported ones (`#anExtNote`). `onOutChange`: `o_dmView`.
- `apps/ps-bridge/index.html`: the `#out` click `[data-dmdesign]` ("Design span n →"): the girder type shown takes span n of its file
  (`PSBDemands.setSpan`), the view back to the design span; one Undo step, with a notice.
### Code (before / after: the diff of this change)

### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)

  the design span). "Design span n →" writes `P.demands[<type id>].span` (the field of batch D1), one Undo step.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- No engine value changed (harness B: 0 differences; the Report keeps the design span). The view's Strength I is the old app's own view
  (O:8053-8058): η(1.25(DC1 + DC2) + 1.50 DW + 1.75 m LL±), AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-1, from the file's values as read.

  M_u+ = 1.25(M_DC1 + M_DC2) + 1.50 M_DW + 1.75 M_LL+ of the file's row = −2542.2 kip-ft, the table's value (AASHTO, η = m = 1).
  Entire beam: all 62 stations. "Design span 2 →": the engine reads span 2 of the file (R.ext.sel.idx 2); Undo returns span 1.

  effect (the design span applies them); the note says so.
- D2-b. The view is on the page only; the Report shows the design span.

## 2026-11-15 — Batch D3: the MCT demands hand-off ("New analysis data available", Load, version check) and the MCT geometry changes (banner, review window); click only (the auto-adopt lock: HO-D2 pending)
PR #1576: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1576
### Request
- Engineer-approved plan A→H (2026-11-15), batch D3 (review old-vs-new.md #127 High, #128 Med): the old app's receiver of the MCT
  Generator's demands ("Prestressed Bridge Design.html" O:9211-9290 checkHandoff / adoptHandoff, O:9603-9625 banner) and its geometry
  changes (O:9291-9318, 9626-9660), with the existing bridgeSuite.v1 keys unchanged (HANDOFF.md), receiver id psbridge (as PR #1566).
  Auto-adopt locks on hold (engineer decision HO-D2 pending): Load by click only.
### What changed
- `apps/ps-bridge/engine/handoffs.js` (anchor `/* ---- MCT demands (batch D3`): `MCT_VERSION` 1 (the old app's HANDOFF_SUPPORTED_VERSION),
  `MCT_K` (the keys), `verOf`, `tokenOf` (BridgeHandoff's), `mctPending(get)` (the old checkHandoff: latestId → the map's payload → its token
  against this app's marker `bridgeSuite.v1.adopted.psbridge`; `supported` = version ≤ 1), `mctDescribe(p)`, `mctPlan(P, T, payload)` (the
  file reader of engine/demands.js on the payload; the old app's "continuous member" rule; the bridge questions: spans, continuity),
  `geomPending(get)` (the old checkGeometryChanges against `bridgeSuite.v1.geometryChanges.adopted.psbridge`).
- `apps/ps-bridge/ui/handoffs.js`: `mctBanner(P)`, `geoDialog`, `mctLoad(ctx)`, `onMct(e, ctx)`; `init(onMctChange)` also follows the MCT
  keys (storage event). Load: the payload becomes the MIDAS demands of the girder type chosen in the banner (default: the type on the
  member's line `member.key` in the span shown, else the type shown), the two questions (bridge spans = the member's when the counts agree;
  continuity for a continuous member), this app's marker written; one Undo step (the marker is not undone, as the old app's). "Not now" /
  Dismiss write the marker only. A schema newer than v1: "Analysis output is newer than this app" (dismiss only). The geometry review window
  lists the changes (field, detail, current, new); Dismiss; "Load the demands now" when a payload is waiting (both markers).
- `apps/ps-bridge/index.html`: the banners at the top of the output panel (`HOUI.mctBanner`), their clicks (`HOUI.onMct`), `hoCtx` + toast /
  redraw, `HOUI.init(() => drawOut())`, CSS.
- `HANDOFF.md` §4.16: the MCT demands and geometry changes in the new app.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- The old app's keys and formats are read unchanged (`bridgeSuite.v1.handoffs`, `.latestId`, `.updatedAt`, `.geometryChanges`,
  `.geometryChanges.updatedAt`); nothing of them is written. This app writes only its own adoption markers `bridgeSuite.v1.adopted.psbridge`
  (the payload's token `handoffId@producedAt`) and `bridgeSuite.v1.geometryChanges.adopted.psbridge` (its producedAt), the receiver id of
  PR #1566; the old app's `.adopted.psbeam` / `.geometryChanges.adopted.psbeam` are not read or written (smoke). A Load writes the type's
  `P.demands` entry (batch D1 field) and, on the two questions, `P.spans.lengths` / `P.spans.continuity`; one Undo step.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- No engine value changed. Load gives the engine the same inputs as the old app's adoptHandoff for its design (the payload with the
  member's span, L, continuity on for a continuous member): Node test, every computeAll value equal.
### Check case (tests/engine/psbridge-mct.test.mjs)
- New project, bridge 100 / 100 / 100 simple; the MCT fixture (110 / 140 / 110, member G2) published; Load into Interior S1 (on G2), both
  questions yes: bridge 110 / 140 / 110 made continuous; the cell's engine inputs = the old app's adopted inputs (external with span 1
  x = 0–110, L = 110, cont.on true); computeAll identical (R.ext.sel.idx 1); a type of span 2 takes span 2 of the member.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- D3-a. HO-D2 pending: no auto-adopt lock; Load by click only (the banner says so).
- D3-b. Load goes to one girder type, chosen in the banner (default: the type on the member's line `member.key` in the span shown); the old
  app had one design. The type keeps its own span of the member (the old app took span 1 of a new member).
- D3-c. The old app turned continuity on and set L silently; here both are questions (Undo returns them), as continuity is the bridge's
  (every type) in this app.
- D3-d. The geometry review window is the old app's record (no values travel from it); its "Load the demands now" loads the pending
  demands when there are any. The marker of a Load is not undone by Undo (as the old app's).
### Other copies
- None. HANDOFF.md §4.16 updated.

## 2026-11-15 — Batch F1/F2 (PSBF): Bridge Substructure Loading — the reactions of every girder line (allGirders) and the bridge geometry (superGeometry), as the Steel Bridge app sends them (click only; the one-line send unchanged)
PR #1577: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1577
### Request
- Batch F (engineer-approved plan A→H, 2026-11-15), F1: reactions for every girder line to Bridge Substructure Loading as the Steel Bridge app sends them (`allGirders`, the same schema and keys; the receiver learns about the PS sender where needed; the current single-line payload unchanged, CLAUDE.md §5). F2: the bridge geometry (`bridgeSuite.v1.superGeometry`, as apps/steel-bridge/ui/handoffs.js sgPayload), the same schema. Review rows: ps-vs-steel S6, S7 (review-1115). Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception, HANDOFF.md): this app and Bridge Substructure Loading.html in one PR.
### What changed
- `engine/handoffs.js` (`PSBHandoffs`), new (anchor `/* ---- batch F (2026-11-15): Bridge Substructure Loading`): `srAll(P, cells)`, `secDims(g)`, `sgPayload(P, cells)`, `GEO_ID = 'psbridge'`; exported. `cells` = `PSBBridge.results(P, cellR).cells` (every girder type × line, the page's engine cache).
  - `srAll`: for each span s and line g, the cell's `srPayload(inp, R)` (the old app's `bxSuperRxPayload`, unchanged) gives the two end reactions; support k gets the right end of span k and the left end of span k+1, summed (`r3` of the sum of the 3-decimal values). Supports "Abut. 1" / "Pier k" / "Abut. 2", x cumulative; girders G1…Gn with the cell's position; `allGirders:true`, `span:{index:null,length:Σ}`, `liveLoad:null`, `project` from the Project tab name, producer `PS-Beam`, producerFile `apps/ps-bridge/index.html`; notes: basis, DC1 content, continuity or simple, MIDAS cells, each pier's shares per girder ("Pier 1 (span 1 right end + span 2 left end), DC1 / DC2 / DW kip: G1 a + b, …"), live load not sent. Refused when a line of a span has no type or a cell has an input error.
  - `sgPayload`: §4.14 from the inputs (spans, continuity, skews, bays, overhangs, `xs.dl` edges via `PSBBridgeDL.edgeFace`, deck t_s / dead-load thickness / haunch) and each cell's engine section (`R.g`, else `girderGross`) through `secDims`; `section.material:'prestressed concrete'` (new optional field, HANDOFF.md §4.14); contentHash and the shared check (`SharedHandoffStore.geometryHash`, `checkGeometry`).
- `ui/handoffs.js`: a new row in the Hand-offs card under "Send reactions…": **Send to Substructure Loading** + boxes Geometry / Reactions of every girder line (ticked; page-only state `SEND`) + **Export hand-off (JSON)**; `subSend(ctx, file)` (the Steel Bridge app's subSend): build all ticked first, publish (channel key + `.updatedAt`), the `.by` copy (`superGeometry.by.psbridge`; `superReactions.by.psbeam`), the per-project copy and Cloud-sync upload (`SharedHandoffStore.send`, producer id `psbridge`), one alert with the summary; "Last sent" per project in the card (`lastSent`, read only).
- `index.html`: `'../../shared/handoff-store.js'` after github-sync.js; `hoCtx.all` (= `allResults(true)`, as the Report) and `hoCtx.redrawIn`.
- Bridge Substructure Loading.html (receiver; fixlog/Bridge Substructure Loading.md PSBF): producer id `psbridge` listed for both channels; a concrete section disables the "Also update the live-load distribution girder data" option.
- HANDOFF.md §2 table, §4.4, §4.14, §4.16, §5.1.
- Tests: new `tests/engine/psbridge-subloads.test.mjs` (3 tests), new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-subloads.mjs` (7 checks); `psbridge-model.test.mjs`: the script list and the shared-file exemption of the key check (handoff-store.js).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- No project field, psb2.* key or existing hand-off key/format changed. New keys written only on the new button: `bridgeSuite.v1.superGeometry`, `.updatedAt`, `.by.psbridge`, `bridgeSuite.v1.superGeometry.by.psbridge.<project id>`, `bridgeSuite.v1.superReactions.by.psbridge.<project id>` (HANDOFF.md §5.1 pattern; Cloud sync queue `bridgeSuite.v1.handoffStore.pending` only while sync is set up); it also writes `superReactions`, `.updatedAt`, `.by.psbeam` with the every-line payload (the same schema; the receiver already reads it). The one-line button's payload is byte-identical (Node test, smoke).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- No formula, factor, unit or code reference of the design changed (harness B 0 differences). New sent values (callout): a pier reaction = the sum of the two adjacent spans' end reactions of the same line (statics of the line-girder model; the Steel Bridge app sends one support point too); each span end reaction is the existing `bxSuperRxPayload` value (simple span R = wL/2, AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.12.3.3 for the continuous-unit DC2 / DW, unchanged). Geometry: values copied from the inputs; the section dimensions are the engine's library values (largest of each).
### Check case (new project: PCI BT-72, 120 ft, 5 girders at the default bays; tests/engine/psbridge-subloads.test.mjs)
- G2 (interior), Abut. 1: w_g = 0.82559 klf, w_deck+haunch = 1.08750 klf, no diaphragms → DC1 = (0.82559 + 1.08750) × 120 / 2 = 114.785 kip; DC2 = 0.120 × 60 = 7.200; DW = 0.195 × 60 = 11.700 kip (= the Analysis tab's Reactions card of G2). G1 / G5 DC1 105.785 kip. Σ DW over both abutments = Σ_g w_DW,g × L (statics).
- Two spans 100 + 120 ft made continuous: Pier 1, G2: DC1 95.655 + 114.785 = 210.440 kip; DC2 7.860 + 8.750 = 16.610; DW 12.773 + 14.219 = 26.992 → 26.99 shown (the shares are the cells' continuous-unit end shears).
- Geometry: depth 72 in (h), bf 42 (max of 42 / 26), tf 6 (max of d1 3.5, d3 6), tw 6 (bw); deck t_s 8 in, haunch 2 in; edges barrier 1.5 ft (barrier face); skews 0.
- Before: nothing sent for every line / geometry ("Missing" / "Partial"). After: as above; SubLoads applies P.br d 72, bf 42, tf 6, tw 6 and P.rx.data = the payload by girder number (smoke).
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- F-D1. A pier reaction is the sum of both spans' end reactions (one support point per pier, as the Steel Bridge app); for simple spans the notes give each span's share to split between the back and ahead bearing rows by hand (the receiver maps one source support to one row). The schema has no per-span field; none invented.
- F-D2. The every-line send writes the same `.by.psbeam` slot as the one-line button (the receiver's PS slot): the last send wins there; per-project copies use producer id `psbridge`, so the receiver had to list it (the HANDOFF.md cross-tool exception).
- F-D3. producer `PS-Beam` (the identity of this app's other sends, HO-D1), producer id `psbridge` (this app's receiver id).
- F-D4. Section dimensions for a concrete girder: `tf` / `tw` as stated in secDims (thickest flange or slab; bw incl. both webs / stems); `section.material:'prestressed concrete'` added (optional) so the receiver does not estimate K_g from a steel shape.
- F-D5. Deck values: the largest over the girder types when they differ (said in the notes); `total` = the dead-load deck thickness when entered separately.
- F-D6. Live load not sent (liveLoad null), as the Steel Bridge app.
### Other copies
- `subSend` follows apps/steel-bridge/ui/handoffs.js subSend (not shared code; adapted). shared/handoff-store.js loaded unchanged.
### How verified
- See the PR: Node (psbridge-subloads: the Steel Bridge app's payload keys from its own srPayload / sgPayload code; each cell's reactions; statics; the receiver's own check code cut from the HTML), smokes ps-bridge-subloads (PS as the sender into SubLoads), geometry-handoff (Steel → SubLoads unchanged), the PS full checks, bsl-compare.

### Tests
- New: tests/engine/psbridge-subloads.test.mjs (3), tests/smoke/ps-bridge-subloads.mjs (7). Changed: tests/engine/psbridge-model.test.mjs (script list, shared exemption).

## 2026-11-15 — Batch F3 / F4: the old app's "Design beam" chip (read only; girder-count warning; "Show G<i>", interior / exterior follows the line) and "Import hand-off (JSON)" of the distribution factors (click / display only; no calculation change)
PR #1579: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1579
### Request
- Batch F (engineer-approved plan, 2026-11-15). F3: the "Design beam" chip of LL & DL (old app O:8962-8984 `BeamChip`, `BridgeBeam` O:515-565): warn on a girder-count mismatch; interior / exterior follows it, by click / display only. F4: "Import hand-off (JSON)" for the LLDF pull, as the Steel Bridge app offers (apps/steel-bridge/ui/handoffs.js `lldfFile`); dlLoads only if the old app or the Steel app offers it (neither does: not added). Not in scope: the auto-follow locks (HO-D2), designBeam / beamRoster channels beyond the chip. Review rows old-vs-new #28, #129; ps-vs-steel S8.
### What changed
- `engine/handoffs.js`: `DB_K`, `dbRead`, `dbState(P, get)` (anchor `/* ---- batch F3 (2026-11-15): the old app's "Design beam" chip`): reads `bridgeSuite.v1.designBeam` (bridge-design-beam) and `bridgeSuite.v1.beamRoster` (bridge-beam-roster) as the old `BridgeBeam.rd` (schema, version ≤ 1); `mismatch` = the old `BridgeBeam.mismatch(nb)` (roster Nb ≠ xs.nb); with equal counts the line g = the beam index, its type in the span shown (`PSBBridge.typeAt`), its position here (G1 / G<nb> exterior) and LL & DL's class (`type` 'ext' / 'int' of the selection, else of the roster beam) → `posWarn` when they differ.
- `ui/handoffs.js`: `beamChip(P)` (exported): `<div id="dbChip">` "Design beam (LL & DL Distribution, bridgeSuite.v1.designBeam): B4 · INT" + "Show G4 (interior)" (`data-mct="dbShow"`), or "The output tabs show G4", or "⚠ 5≠6" with a note (no Show), or "no roster"; nothing when neither key is published. `onMct`: `dbShow` → `ctx.pick(k, g)`. `init`: the storage event also redraws for designBeam / beamRoster. The lldf row: button `lldfFile` "Import hand-off (JSON)" + hidden `<input type="file" data-ho-file="lldf">`; `lldfPull(ctx, raw0, via)` (was `lldfPull(ctx)`): a file's payload text goes through the same `lldfResolve` / confirm (+ "Via: file <name>") / apply / `markAdopted` as the stored one; `BridgeXfer.importFile(file, 'bridge-lldf-factors', 1, …)` refuses another schema or a newer version. The card's closing note and header comment updated.
- `index.html`: `h += HOUI.beamChip(P);` after the MCT banners; `hoCtx.pick`.
- HANDOFF.md §4.16. Tests: new `tests/engine/psbridge-designbeam.test.mjs` (the old page's BridgeBeam code, cut from the pinned file, on 9 stored states = dbState's sel / roster / mismatch), new smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-designbeam.mjs` (6 checks); `psbridge-model.test.mjs`: the two read keys allowed in engine/handoffs.js.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None changed; no key written by the chip (designBeam / beamRoster read only). "Show G<i>" writes `P.design` (the line shown, as the type and line choice above the output tabs). The file import writes what the pull writes (the girder type's `loads.dfAuto`, `dfm`, `dfv`, `fatM`) and `bridgeSuite.v1.lldf.adopted.psbridge`.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed (harness B 0 differences). Interior / exterior is the line's position as before (engine/design.js); the chip only chooses which line is shown.
### Check case
- New project, 5 girders; LL & DL roster Nb 5, design beam B4 (INT): chip "B4 · INT", "Show G4 (interior)" → P.design.g = 4, the inputs' loads.pos 'interior'. Roster Nb 6: "⚠ 5≠6", no Show. LL & DL class 'ext' for B3 → "⚠ LL & DL classes B3 as exterior; here G3 is interior".
- File `bridge-lldf-factors` with governing.interior gM 0.612345, gV 0.701234, fatM 0.41234, Nb 7 (≠ 5: no design beam, the envelope): DFm 0.6123, DFv 0.7012, fatigue DF 0.4123, DF auto off (= the stored pull of the same payload, item 12 check case). A `bridge-dl-loads` file: "Cannot import the hand-off file: wrong data type (bridge-dl-loads), expected bridge-lldf-factors", nothing changed.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- F-D7. The chip is read only (the old app's chip could change the shared design beam; here it is chosen in LL & DL) and shown only when LL & DL has published a design beam or roster.
- F-D8. "Interior / exterior follows it" = "Show G<i>" puts the output tabs on that line (whose position this app derives from the line, G1 / G<nb> exterior); no automatic following and no position override (the old app's posAuto). When LL & DL's class disagrees with the line's position the chip warns; nothing is changed.
- F-D9. With different girder counts the beam number is not mapped to a line (the old app's mismatch warning; the pull uses the envelope, HO-D5).
- F-D10. dlLoads: no file import (neither the old app nor the Steel Bridge app offers one).
### Other copies
- The chip's rules are the old page's BridgeBeam (rd, mismatch), re-written as dbState (Node test against the old code). `lldfFile` follows the Steel Bridge app's handler.

## 2026-11-15 — E0: no "pending engineer review" wording in the app (Auto design output tab, Project tab / Report assumption; display only)
PR #1578: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1578
### Request
- Engineer rule: "pending engineer review" wording appears only in PRs and the fix log, never in the app UI or the Report. Reword the Auto design output tab's "Assumed (pending engineer review)" neutrally, and fix any other such wording in apps/ps-bridge the same way. The box beam / voided slab "to be confirmed" note (PS #1542 / #1554) is an engineer-requested exception and is kept.
### What changed
- **`ui/autodesign.js`**, the output tab's "How the search works (assumptions)" list (anchor `a higher f′c or f′ci is not worse for any check; a higher y<sub>end</sub>`):
  - Before: `<li>Assumed (pending engineer review): a higher f′c or f′ci …`
  - After: `<li>Assumption (<a href="#rp:rs.adb" data-gotab="rpt">Report, §2, Auto design basis</a>): a higher f′c or f′ci …` (the link is the one the tab's first note already uses; the Report's Auto design basis states the same assumptions under "Assumptions of the search").
- **`ui/inputs.js`** `assumptions(P)`, the "Unequal bays (PS-9 …)" item, shown on the Project tab and in Report §2 Assumptions (anchor `with unequal bays it is an approximation`):
  - Before: `… with unequal bays it is an approximation (pending engineer review).'`
  - After: `… with unequal bays it is an approximation.'`
- **`ui/handoffs.js`**, the MCT hand-off banner (batch D3, #1576; anchor `Auto-adopt (the old app's lock): not in this app yet`):
  - Before: `… not in this app yet (engineer decision HO-D2 pending).</span>`
  - After: `… not in this app yet: the hand-off is loaded only by "Load these demands".</span>` (the banner's own button; behaviour unchanged).
  - and its "Geometry changes from MCT" dialog (anchor `Auto-update (the old app's lock) is not in this app yet`): Before `… not in this app yet (engineer decision HO-D2 pending).</p>`; After `… not in this app yet.</p>`.
- Every other "pending" in apps/ps-bridge (outside the frozen engine/pbd-*.js) is in a code comment, a list's "pending edit" (lists.js, not review wording) or the kept "to be confirmed" note.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed (wording only). Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- Default project: Report text and every input tab's girder-design cards: no match for /pending/i (before: the Unequal bays assumption in Project tab and Report §2 Assumptions matched).
- Auto design output tab: the assumptions list item reads "Assumption (Report, §2, Auto design basis): a higher f′c or f′ci is not worse for any check; …".
### How verified
- New `tests/engine/psbridge-nopending.test.mjs` (4 tests; 2 fail on main before the change): also the MCT banner strings of ui/handoffs.js.
- PS checks: see the PR.
### Other copies

## 2026-11-15 — E1: the HL-93 load rating at every station of the girder, negative moment over the pier included (engine/rating-along.js, Rating tab, Summary, Report; CLAUDE.md §4 change of the governing rating factors shown)
PR #1580: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1580
### Request
- Review finding O17 (scratchpad review ps-vs-steel.md "Rating"): the Steel Bridge app rates every location (apps/steel-bridge/ui/rating.js, engine/rating.js); this app rated only the engine's governing stations and called it a screening, and did not rate the negative-moment region over the piers of continuous units.
- Rate, per MBE 4th Ed. (2026), at every analysis station for each rating the app already makes (HL-93 inventory / operating): flexure positive and negative (the engine's continuity capacity with the deck bars), shear, Service III; an RF-along-the-girder chart and a table of every location; the governing RF of each group; the governing location worked (§6); Report sections. Reuse the engine's demands and capacities; no saved-format change.
### What changed
- **New `engine/rating-along.js`** (`window.PSBRatingAlong`; loaded in index.html before engine/worked-hdr.js). `of(R)` (memoised on R) builds the rows from the frozen engine's own values, the rating factor formed app-side:
  - `flexP`, every `R.flexFull` station with `mLLpos > 1e-6` and `phiMn > 0` (the engine's own filter): `cap = phiCS*phiMn/12 − 1.25*(mSW+mDC1+mDC2) − 1.50*mDW`, `RF = cap/(γ_LL*mLLpos)` — the engine's `rateAt` in the same order of operations, so the lowest is `R.rating.RFinv` exactly.
  - `flexN` (only with `R.cont`): every `R.flexFull` station with `mLLneg < −1e-6` in the half span next to an interior support (`R.cont.unit`: `s > 1 && x ≤ L/2` or `s < spans && x ≥ L/2`, the region of the engine's continuity checks): `C = phiCS*R.cont.phiMnN/12`; hogging-positive `hNC = −(mSW+mDC1)`, `h2 = −mDC2`, `hW = −mDW`, each with γ = 1.25 (DC) / 1.50 (DW) when it adds to the negative moment and 0.90 / 0.65 when it relieves it; `RF = (C − Σγh)/(γ_LL*|mLLneg|)`.
  - `shear`, every grid station from the first non-bearing `R.shear` station (the critical section) to the last: `C = phiCS*R.shearDiag[j].phiVn`, `DC = |V_DC|`, `DW = |V_DW|` (R.diagrams), `LL = max(|V_LLpos|, |V_LLneg|)` (a simple span with the built-in load: also of the mirror station, the engine's `VLLx` from the nearer support); at the engine's governing section (`R.shrRating.x`) its own `phiVn, VDC, VDW, VLL` (added as a row where it is not a grid station).
  - `s3`, every `R.grid` station with `fLL = Mll/Sbc > 1e-6` ksi: `fPS = Pe/A + Pe e/Sb` (`Pe = Aps*fpe`), `fDC = (Mg+Mdk)/Sb + 12 M_DC2/Sbc`, `fDW = 12 M_DW/Sbc`, `RF = (fr + fPS − fDC − fDW)/(0.8 fLL)` — the engine's svcRating expressions; at `R.svcRating.x` its own values.
  - `gov` (the lowest inventory RF of each group), `inv` (of all), `opr` (flexure and shear); `steps(A, row, prefix)` works a row; `govSteps(A)` the governing row of each group (ids `rt.al.fp.*`, `rt.al.fn.*`, `rt.al.v.*`, `rt.al.s3.*`).
- **`engine/worked-hdr.js`** `rating()` (anchor `const AL = window.PSBRatingAlong, A = AL ? AL.of(R) : null;`): after the vehicles, `if (A) K.w.take(AL.govSteps(A));` (no engine path for these steps; nothing else changed).

(2026))" (#card-rtal: each group's governing location, C, RF inventory / operating, § to its worked step; the overall governing RFs; method notes), the graphic "Load rating: RF along the girder" (#gfx_rtal, PSBVizAlong chart as the steel app's: inventory solid, operating dashed, capped scale, RF = 1.0, governing flagged; a click works the lowest rating of that station), "Rating factors at every location (n)" (#card-rtall; a click on a row works it below the table, #rt_selwork, steps `rt.sel.*`, screen only; in the Report with Detail "every station"). New TOPICS `alfp`, `alfn`, `alv`, `als3`. The tile "Governing (inventory)" of the rating-factor graphic shows the along-girder governing RF. Notes on the engine's Shear and Service III cards point to the along-girder card. The engine's cards (values, data-ev paths) are unchanged.

### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key, field or format. The selected row and the chart's series chips are page memory.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- AASHTO MBE 4th Ed. (2026), paraphrased: Art. 6A.4.2.1 and Eqs. 6A.4.2.1-1 to -4 (the rating equation; C = φ_c φ_s φR_n with φ_c φ_s ≥ 0.85; C = f_R at the service limit; rated at each limit state and load effect, the lowest governs: the basis of rating every station); C6A.4.2.1 (no η); Table 6A.4.2.2-1 (prestressed concrete: Strength I 1.25 / 1.50 / 1.75 / 1.35; Service III 1.00 / 1.00 with Table 6A.4.2.2-2, γ_LL = 0.8 without refined losses and elastic gains); Art. 6A.5.3 (φ of LRFD 5.5.4.2); Art. 6A.5.4.1 and C6A.5.4.1 (Strength I and Service III for prestressed components; Service III a design-level check: no operating value); Art. 6A.5.8 (shear by the MCFT general procedure); Art. 6A.5.10 (creep and shrinkage effects need not typically be rated: the restraint moments are not in the rating, as in the engine's rating). AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-2 (minimum γ_p: DC 0.90, DW 0.65) for a dead load relieving the negative moment.
- Before → after (the governing RFs shown on the Rating tab tiles, the check column's Rating chip, the Summary and the Report §1): flexure positive unchanged on every design (same stations and expression); shear and Service III the same or lower (the engine's rows are in the table); negative flexure new (continuity on). On the 19 designs of tests/engine/psbridge-tab-cases.mjs:
  - Service III: where the engine's governing bottom-tension section has no live-load tension (the girder end), the engine shows 99 ("—", n/a) or a meaningless large RF; along the girder the lowest is at midspan, e.g. Type IV 85 ft: — → 2.966; continuous 3 spans: 8.165 → 2.621; two continuous spans MassDOT: 4.3E13 → 2.753.
  - Shear: two designs lower: few strands, two spans 0.608 (x = 84 ft) → 0.599 (x = 86 ft); CTDOT debonded 1.611 → 1.597 (x = 34 ft).
  - Negative flexure (new): continuous 3 spans 1.362 at the pier; two spans MassDOT 1.212; few strands two spans 1.043; flanged two spans 1.164; RIDOT two spans 1.212; MassDOT exterior G1 1.116.
  - Governing inventory RF of the design (lowest of the groups): default simple span 1.430 (Service III) → 1.430 (unchanged); continuous 3 spans 2.032 (shear) → 1.362 (negative flexure at the pier).
### Check case (`tests/engine/psbridge-rating-along.test.mjs`)
- Simple span, default BT-72 interior, L = 120 ft, φ_c φ_s = 1.00 (unchanged): x = 58 ft, M_g = 1484.41, M_DC1 = 1955.33, M_DC2 = 539.40 → M_DC = 3979.14 kip-ft; M_DW = 449.50; M_LL+IM = 2628.73; φM_n = 13638.91 kip-ft (φ from the Flexure tab). RF_inv = (13638.91 − 1.25 × 3979.14 − 1.50 × 449.50)/(1.75 × 2628.73) = (13638.91 − 4973.92 − 674.25)/4600.28 = 7990.74/4600.28 = 1.737 (before 1.737); RF_opr = 7990.74/(1.35 × 2628.73) = 2.252. Shear 1.635 and Service III 1.430 at the engine's sections, before and after.
- Continuous, 3 spans 100 / 125 / 100 ft, exterior G6 in span 2 (restraint on), the left pier x = 0: deck bars A_s = 16 in², f_y = 60 ksi, d = 77.5 in, a = 5.110 in, φ = 0.90: φM_n,neg = 0.90 × 16 × 60 × (77.5 − 5.110/2)/12 = 5396.02 kip-ft; M_g = M_DC1 = 0 (simple span, at its support); M_DC2 = −385.19, M_DW = −320.99 kip-ft (hogging, both add: 1.25, 1.50); M_LL+IM = −1859.53 kip-ft. RF_inv = (5396.02 − 1.25 × 385.19 − 1.50 × 320.99)/(1.75 × 1859.53) = (5396.02 − 962.98)/3254.18 = 4433.05/3254.18 = 1.362; RF_opr = 4433.05/(1.35 × 1859.53) = 1.766. Before: not rated (governing 2.032, shear); after: governing 1.362.
### How verified
- New `tests/engine/psbridge-rating-along.test.mjs` (27 tests): on all 19 designs of psbridge-tab-cases.mjs and the 5 of psbridge-midas-cases.mjs (MIDAS files, a custom table), flexure + governing = the engine's (Object.is, same x), the engine's shear and Service III rows present with its values (Service III where its f_LL > 1e-6 ksi) and the lowest not above them, the pier rows = R.cont's demands and capacity, φV_n of the grid = the design stations' at common stations, V_LL and V_DC = the engine's continuity components, the Service III expression recomputed = R.svcRating.RF, unique step ids, every step in a topic; the hand checks above; the tab HTML (tab and Report), the check column entries and paths, the Summary (no data-sv without a path), the Report §1 table, every reference resolved, the same recorded engine paths, the project unchanged; an old project computes.
- New smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-rating.mjs`.
- PS checks: see the PR. Harness B: see the PR.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- E1-D1. Negative moment: the pier section's φM_n,neg (deck bars A_s of the continuity input) is taken over the whole half span next to the interior support; no bar cut-off is an input.
- E1-D2. Negative moment: a dead load that relieves the negative moment (the noncomposite girder + DC1 moment away from the support; DC2 or DW past their contraflexure) takes the LRFD minimum load factor (DC 0.90, DW 0.65, 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-2), each part on its own; MBE Table 6A.4.2.2-1 lists only the maximum factors.
- E1-D3. No continuity restraint moments in the rating (MBE 4th Ed. Art. 6A.5.10; as the engine's rating; the design checks include them).
- E1-D4. Shear keeps the engine's φ_c φ_s on the capacity (MBE 4th Ed. Art. 6A.4.2.4 takes φ_s = 1.0 for shear; the Steel Bridge app does): the same RF when φ_s = 1.00, lower (conservative) when φ_s < 1.00. Not changed here (an engine-rating change).
- E1-D5. Positive flexure keeps the engine's expression at every station, including near a pier where M_DC is net negative (γ_DC 1.25 on the net DC, as the engine): to be raised, not changed here.
- E1-D6. The legal / permit vehicles stay where the engine rates them (one entered moment and shear each, no station).
- E1-D7. Service III is rated where the live load gives bottom tension (every grid station), the continuity region's top fibre not rated (reinforced concrete there: Strength I only, MBE 6A.5.4.1).
- E1-D9. A live-load effect below 1e-6 (ksi, kip) is "no live load": no rating at that station. The engine's Service III section is sometimes a support where its f_LL is a round-off 1.6E-14 ksi, giving RF 4.3E13 (two continuous spans MassDOT, RIDOT): that row is left out and the lowest Service III RF is at midspan.
- E1-D8. Demands from a MIDAS file or a custom table: each station is rated with its own (concurrent) demands, an interior-support end with that end's DC2, DW and LL; the engine's pier design check takes the most negative of the two ends for each effect separately (pbd-external.js pierNegM): the pier RF of the governing end may differ from one formed with those mixed demands.
### Other copies
- None (the Steel app's rating is its own engine; not changed).

### Request

### What changed
- **`engine/worked.js`** `section(inp, R)`: after the `lt` step (anchor `weakSteps(add, G);`) two additions:
  - `sec.Pj` P_jack = A_ps f_pbt (f_pbt = R.fpbt = k_j f_pu, linked to §ls.fpbt). The old app showed `R.ss.Aps*inp.str.jack*inp.str.fpu` in a hint (O:6074); no check uses it.
  - `weakSteps(add, G)` (new function, anchor `function weakSteps(add, G)`): steps `sec.wk.*` that work the engine's own `weakAxisAndJ(G)` (engine/pbd-section.js, frozen; the psSection hand-off's Iweak / J since the old app): I-girder h_w, I_y = t_tf b_tf³/12 + t_bf b_bf³/12 + h_w b_w³/12, J_tf, J_bf, J_w (rectTorsionJ: a b³[1/3 − 0.21 (b/a)(1 − b⁴/(12 a⁴))]) and J = their sum; NEXT h_s, I_y (two stems + flange), J_s, J_f, J = 2 J_s + J_f; box / slab I_y = h w³/12 and J of the w × h rectangle (as the engine: no void deducted); S_y = I_y / (b_max/2). ## 2026-11-15 — Batch G4 / G6: the Compare tab (the old app's design sweep over span, girder section or spacing) and the Nomenclature tab (the symbols with their live values, search, § links) (display only)
PR #1583: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1583
### Request
- Old-vs-new review 2026-11-15, rows #65 (Compare tab: design sweep, O:8009-8034, engine sweepDesign already moved) and #91 (Nomenclature tab, ≈ 80 symbols with live values and a search box, O:8815-8960), in the Steel Bridge app's formats.
### What changed
- **New `engine/compare.js`** (window.PSBCompare): `presets(inp, mode)` the old tab's presets (span L − 20 … L + 20 by 10, > 20 ft; every library girder but Custom; spacing S − 1 … S + 1 by 0.5, > 3 ft); `inputsOf(inp, mode, v)` (a copy with L / girder / S set; spacing: `rigidX` of unequal bays dropped, equal bays at S); `one()` / `run()`: sweepDesign's body (the same core checks: every check but /Deck|Lifting|Hauling|FS/; flex, s3, rel, shear, maxDC, camber, nPass / nTot; + the governing check's name and the failing checks) on the page's engine call `PSBHoldDown.compute`.
- **New `ui/compare.js`** (window.PSBUiCompare): the output tab "Compare": Vary (Span / Girder section / Girder spacing; `ui.cmpMode` in psb2.ui), Run sweep, a bar graphic of each candidate's governing D/C against 1.0 (PSBVizAlong.hbars, ratio colours) and the results table (Flexure, Service III tension, Release compression, Shear, Max D/C, governing check, camber, checks n/m, the girder sweep's Strand fit column = the input check's rows / draped strand errors of each section for the type shown, Status); "this design" marked; out of date after an input change; the result in page memory only.
- **New `ui/nomen.js`** (window.PSBUiNomen): the output tab "Nomenclature": 11 groups, 91 symbols: symbol, description, unit, value (an engine value at its R path as the result tabs show it, `data-ev`; where the worked step has an R path that path; an input; η without an owner rule: its step's value), the AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. article (MBE for the rating factors), a § link to the worked step on its tab (or "input" to the input tab); a search box (symbol, description, article); the old tab's decimals (≥ 100: 0, ≥ 10: 1, else 3).
- **`index.html`**: the two scripts; OTABS + `['cmp', 'Compare'], ['nom', 'Nomenclature']` before '3D view'; TABUI + `cmp`, `nom` (so each gets the girder type / line bar, ctx and onOutChange).
- **`tests/smoke/ps-bridge-skeleton.mjs`**: the output tab count 17 → 19 (+ Compare, Nomenclature).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- No key changed. psb2.ui (UI state) gets an optional `cmpMode`; the project is not changed by either tab.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- No engineering value of the app changes: the sweep runs the app's own engine call on changed copies of the inputs; the nomenclature shows the engine's values.
- Decision (pending engineer review): the sweep uses this app's engine call (computeAll + PS-19 rigid section, PS-35 types (f)/(g), PS-10 hold-down, PS-34 pier block), not the frozen sweepDesign's raw computeAll, so a candidate's ratios are the ones its result tabs would show. Where those additions do not apply the rows equal sweepDesign's field by field (test). The default design's row therefore shows the PS-10 hold-down check (1.276, FAIL) in Max D/C, which the old tab did not have.
- Decision (pending engineer review): spacing sweep at equal bays S (the old app had one S).
### Check case
- Default project (BT-72, 120 ft, S = 9 ft), Vary = Span: 100, 110, 120, 130, 140 ft; Max D/C 2.208 (Release tens. steel), 1.518, 1.276, 1.150, 2.342 (Srv III tens); the 120 ft row = this design: Max D/C = 1.276 (Hold-down force (PS-10)), 18/19 core checks, FAIL (the PS-10 check only); with the PS-10 box off the five rows = sweepDesign(inp, 'span', [100 … 140]).
- Nomenclature: I_c = 1,126,663 in⁴ shown "1,126,663" (as the Section properties tab), ℓ_t = 36.0 → "36.0" in, M_u = R.MuMid / 12 = 10,251 kip-ft.
### How verified
- New tests/engine/psbridge-compare-tab.test.mjs (5), tests/engine/psbridge-nomen.test.mjs (3), tests/smoke/ps-bridge-gtabs.mjs. PS checks: see the PR.
### Other copies
- None (engine/pbd-optimize.js sweepDesign unchanged, frozen).
### Code (the PR's diff of the app files)
```diff
diff --git a/apps/ps-bridge/engine/compare.js b/apps/ps-bridge/engine/compare.js
new file mode 100644

+++ b/apps/ps-bridge/engine/compare.js
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+/* apps/ps-bridge/engine/compare.js — the Compare tab's design sweep (window.PSBCompare). Classic script, no DOM. Created 2026-11-15
+   (batch G4: the old app's Compare tab, O:8009-8034, "Design Comparison Sweep": the full design re-run over a range of spans, girder
+   sections or girder spacings, everything else held as entered, and the governing demand / capacity of each).
+
+   The old tab called the moved engine's sweepDesign (engine/pbd-optimize.js, frozen) with its presets. sweepDesign calls the global
+   computeAll, not this app's engine call PSBHoldDown.compute (computeAll + the rigid section on the real girder lines PS-19, the type (f) /
+   (g) distribution factors of box beams and voided slabs PS-35, the hold-down check PS-10, the pier block PS-34): with it a candidate would
+   be judged by other numbers than the app's own result tabs show. So run() repeats sweepDesign's body (the same input changes, the same
+   "core" checks: every check but Deck / Lifting / Hauling / FS, the same fields) on the page's engine call; nothing is calculated here.
+   Decision (pending engineer review; recorded in the PR and the fix log only): the sweep uses the app's engine call, not the raw computeAll.
+   tests/engine/psbridge-compare-tab.test.mjs: for a design the app's additions do not touch, run() = sweepDesign() field by field.
+
+   presets(inp, mode) -> values   the old tab's presets (O:8012-8016): span L − 20 … L + 20 by 10 (> 20 ft), every library girder but Custom,
+                                  spacing S − 1 … S + 1 by 0.5 (> 3 ft)
+   inputsOf(inp, mode, v) -> inp  a copy with L, girder or S set (spacing: equal bays at S, so inputs.rigidX of unequal bays is dropped)
+   one(inp, mode, v, compute) -> row  { v, pass, maxDC, flex, s3, rel, shear, camber, nPass, nTot, gov, fails } or { v, error }
+   run(inp, mode, values, compute) -> rows;  MODES: [[key, label, unit]] */
+(function () {
+  'use strict';
+  const NOT_CORE = /Deck|Lifting|Hauling|FS/;   // sweepDesign's filter (pbd-optimize.js)
+  const MODES = [['span', 'Span', 'ft'], ['girder', 'Girder section', ''], ['spacing', 'Girder spacing', 'ft']];
+  function presets(inp, mode) {
+    if (mode === 'span') return [inp.L - 20, inp.L - 10, inp.L, inp.L + 10, inp.L + 20].filter(v => v > 20);
+    if (mode === 'girder') return Object.keys(GIRDERS).filter(k => k !== 'Custom');
+    if (mode === 'spacing') return [inp.S - 1, inp.S - 0.5, inp.S, inp.S + 0.5, inp.S + 1].filter(v => v > 3);
+    return [];
+  }
+  function inputsOf(inp, mode, v) {
+    const i = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(inp));
+    if (mode === 'span') i.L = v;
+    else if (mode === 'girder') i.girder = v;
+    else if (mode === 'spacing') { i.S = v; delete i.rigidX; }
+    return i;
+  }
+  const engine = () => (window.PSBHoldDown ? window.PSBHoldDown.compute : computeAll);
+  function one(inp, mode, v, compute) {
+    let R; try { R = (compute || engine())(inputsOf(inp, mode, v)); } catch (e) { R = { error: e.message }; }
+    if (R.error) return { v, error: R.error };
+    const core = R.checks.filter(c => !NOT_CORE.test(c.n)), r = n => { const c = R.checks.find(q => q.n === n); return c ? c.r : NaN; };
+    const gov = core.reduce((b, c) => (c.r > b.r ? c : b), core[0] || { n: '', r: -Infinity });
+    return { v, pass: core.every(c => c.pass), maxDC: Math.max(...core.map(c => c.r)), flex: r('Flexure'), s3: r('Srv III tens'), rel: r('Release comp'), shear: r('Shear'),
+      camber: R.cam.final, nPass: core.filter(c => c.pass).length, nTot: core.length, gov: gov.n, fails: core.filter(c => !c.pass).map(c => c.n) };
+  }
+  const run = (inp, mode, values, compute) => values.map(v => one(inp, mode, v, compute));
+  window.PSBCompare = { MODES, NOT_CORE, presets, inputsOf, one, run };
+})();

+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/compare.js — the Compare output tab (window.PSBUiCompare): the old app's "Design Comparison Sweep" (O:8009-8034), the full
+   design of the girder type and line shown re-run over a range of spans, girder sections or girder spacings, everything else held as
+   entered; per candidate the governing ratios of the core checks (engine/compare.js, the old app's sweepDesign on the page's engine call)
+   in the Steel Bridge app's formats: a bar graphic of the governing D/C against 1.0 (PSBVizAlong.hbars, ratio colours) and a table.
+   Created 2026-11-15 (batch G4). Classic script; display only: nothing is saved but the "Vary" choice (ui.cmpMode, the page's psb2.ui);
+   the result lives in this page view's memory and is marked out of date when the inputs change.
+     output(ctx) -> HTML; after(el, ctx) mounts the graphic and wires Run; onOutChange(e, ui). ctx = { P, inp, R, W, ui, redraw } */
+(function () {
+  'use strict';
+  const K = () => window.PSBOutKit, VA = () => window.PSBVizAlong, C = () => window.PSBCompare;
+  const S = { key: '', mode: '', rows: null, fit: null, ms: 0, err: '' };
+  const modeOf = ui => (C().MODES.some(m => m[0] === (ui && ui.cmpMode)) ? ui.cmpMode : 'span');
+  const keyOf = (ctx, mode) => JSON.stringify([ctx.inp, mode]);
+  const cls = r => (!(r <= 1.0001) ? 'ng' : r >= 0.9 ? 'hi' : 'ok');
+  const label = (mode, v) => (mode === 'girder' ? String(v) : K().fx(+v, mode === 'span' ? 1 : 2) + ' ft');
+  const isCur = (ctx, mode, v) => (mode === 'span' ? Math.abs(v - ctx.inp.L) < 1e-9 : mode === 'girder' ? v === ctx.inp.girder : Math.abs(v - ctx.inp.S) < 1e-9);
+  /* fitErrs(ctx, v): girder sweep only: the input check's strand-fit errors (PS-28 / PS-33 / PS-39: rows and draped strands) of the type
+     shown with section v (the page's PSBInputCheck.collect, as engine/autodesign.js fitErrors); [] when the strands fit */
+  function fitErrs(ctx, v) {
+    const P = ctx.P, BR = window.PSBBridge, IC = window.PSBInputCheck; if (!IC) return [];
+    const sh = BR && BR.hasTypes(P) ? BR.shown(P) : null, b = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(sh ? BR.effBase(P, sh.k) : P.base)); b.girder = v;
+    const Pv = Object.assign({}, P, { base: b, types: undefined, design: sh ? { g: sh.g, s: sh.s } : P.design });
+    try { return IC.collect(Pv).errors.filter(x => /^base\.(rows|harp)(\.|$)/.test(x.path)).map(x => x.msg); } catch (e) { return []; }
+  }
+  function runNow(ctx) {
+    const mode = modeOf(ctx.ui), t0 = Date.now(); S.err = '';
+    try { const vals = C().presets(ctx.inp, mode); S.rows = C().run(ctx.inp, mode, vals); S.fit = mode === 'girder' ? vals.map(v => fitErrs(ctx, v)) : null; }
+    catch (e) { S.rows = null; S.err = e.message; }
+    S.key = keyOf(ctx, mode); S.mode = mode; S.ms = Date.now() - t0;
+  }
+  function output(ctx) {
+    const k = K(), mode = modeOf(ctx.ui), M = C().MODES, vals = C().presets(ctx.inp, mode);
+    const what = mode === 'span' ? 'spans' : mode === 'girder' ? 'girder sections' : 'girder spacings';
+    let h = k.card('Design comparison sweep', `<div class="fRow"><label for="o_cmpMode">Vary</label><select id="o_cmpMode">${M.map(([v, t]) => `<option value="${v}"${v === mode ? ' selected' : ''}>${t}</option>`).join('')}</select>
+      <button type="button" class="btn pri" id="cmpRun">Run sweep</button><span class="note" id="cmpBusy" hidden>Running…</span></div>
+      <p class="note">Re-runs the whole design of the girder type shown over ${vals.length} ${what} (${mode === 'girder' ? 'every section of the library but Custom' : vals.map(v => label(mode, v)).join(', ')}), holding every other input as entered, and lists the governing demand / capacity of each: a preliminary sizing and type study, as the old app's Compare tab. The deck and handling checks are not in the governing ratio (the old app's rule).${mode === 'spacing' ? ' Spacing: the girders at equal bays of that spacing (the rigid-section factor of unequal bays is not used).' : ''}${mode === 'girder' ? ' The strand rows and draped strands are kept as entered: the Strand fit column gives the input check of each section (a section they do not fit is computed but not a usable design).' : ''}</p>
+      <p class="note">Each candidate is computed by this app's engine call, the one behind every result tab (with the PS-10 hold-down check, the type (f) / (g) distribution factors and the rigid section where they apply), so its ratios match what the result tabs would show for it.</p>`, 'card-cmp');
+    if (!S.rows && !S.err) return h + '<p class="note" id="cmpNone">Choose what to vary and click Run sweep.</p>';
+    if (S.err) return h + `<div class="alert err" role="alert">The sweep stopped: ${k.esc(S.err)}</div>`;
+    const stale = S.key !== keyOf(ctx, mode);
+    if (stale) h += `<div class="alert" id="cmpStale">${S.mode !== mode ? `The results below vary the ${k.esc((M.find(m => m[0] === S.mode) || [, ''])[1].toLowerCase())}, not the ${k.esc((M.find(m => m[0] === mode) || [, ''])[1].toLowerCase())}.` : 'The inputs have changed since this sweep.'} Run the sweep again for the inputs as they are now.</div>`;
+    const md = S.mode, fx = (v, d) => k.fx(v, d), nOk = S.rows.filter((r, i) => !r.error && r.pass && !(S.fit && S.fit[i].length)).length;
+    h += K().gcard('Compare graphic: governing D/C of each candidate', 'gfx_cmp');
+    const head = `<th class="lft">${md === 'span' ? 'Span<br>ft' : md === 'girder' ? 'Girder section' : 'Spacing<br>ft'}</th><th>Flexure</th><th>Service III<br>tension</th><th>Release<br>compression</th><th>Shear</th><th>Max D/C</th><th class="lft">Governing check</th><th>Camber<br>in</th><th>Checks</th>${S.fit ? +    const rows = S.rows.map((r, i) => { const cur = isCur(ctx, md, r.v), f = S.fit ? S.fit[i] : null, nm = `${k.esc(label(md, r.v))}${cur ? ' <b>(this design)</b>' : ''}`;
+      const fitC = f ? `<td class="lft${f.length ? ' ngt' : ''}"${f.length ? ` title="${k.esc(f.join(' '))}"` : ''}>${f.length ? `${f.length} error${f.length > 1 ? 's' : ''}` : 'fits'}</td>` : '';
+      if (r.error) return `<tr class="ng"><td class="lft">${nm}</td><td colspan="8" class="lft">The engine could not compute it: ${k.esc(r.error)}</td>${fitC}<td class="ngt">—</td></tr>`;
+      const c = (v, d) => `<td${cls(v) === 'ng' ? ' class="ngt"' : cls(v) === 'hi' ? ' style="color:var(--warn);font-weight:600"' : ''}>${fx(v, d)}</td>`, okAll = r.pass && !(f && f.length);
+      return `<tr${cur ? ' class="sel"' : !okAll ? ' class="ng"' : ''}><td class="lft">${nm}</td>${c(r.flex, 2)}${c(r.s3, 2)}${c(r.rel, 2)}${c(r.shear, 2)}<td><b>${fx(r.maxDC, 2)}</b></td><td class="lft">${k.esc(r.gov)}</td><td>${fx(r.camber, 2)}</td><td>${r.nPass}/${r.nTot}</td>${fitC}<td class="${okAll ? 'ok' : 'ngt'}">${okAll ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}</td></tr>`; }).join('');
+    h += k.card(`Results: varying the ${k.esc((M.find(m => m[0] === md) || [, ''])[1].toLowerCase())} (${S.rows.length} candidates, ${nOk} pass)`, `<div class="tscroll"><table class="tbl" id="cmpTbl"><thead><tr>${head}</tr></thead><tbody>${rows}</tbody></table></div>
+      <p class="note">Ratios are demand / capacity (≤ 1.00 passes; amber 0.90 to 1.00, red above 1.00), the engine's checks of the same names (Flexure, Srv III tens, Release comp, Shear; <a href="#" data-gotab="flex">Flexure</a>, <a href="#" data-gotab="str">Stresses</a>, <a href="#" data-gotab="shear">Shear</a> tabs, where each is worked for the design shown). Max D/C: the largest ratio of the core checks (every check but deck, lifting, hauling and the handling factors of safety), named in "Governing check". Camber: the engine's final camber (Camber &amp; deflection tab). Checks: core checks passing / core checks. A candidate is worked only when it is the design: to see one in full, enter it and the result tabs show it (Undo puts the design back). Computed in ${S.ms} ms.</p>`, 'card-cmpres');
+    return h;
+  }
+  function after(el, ctx) {
+    const b = el.querySelector('#cmpRun'); if (b) b.addEventListener('click', () => { const busy = el.querySelector('#cmpBusy'); if (busy) busy.hidden = false; b.disabled = true;

+      lab: [`${label(md, r.v)}${isCur(ctx, md, r.v) ? ' (this design)' : ''}${r.error ? '' : ': ' + r.gov}`, r.error ? 'error' : k.fx(r.maxDC, 3)] }));
+    VA().mount(slot, { key: 'cmp', title: 'Governing D/C of each candidate', sub: `varying the ${k.esc((C().MODES.find(m => m[0] === md) || [, ''])[1].toLowerCase())}; bars capped at 3.0`,
+      draw: W => VA().hbars({ aria: 'Governing demand / capacity of each candidate of the sweep', panels: [{ label: 'Max D/C of the core checks', unit: 'D/C', limit: { v: 1, label: '1.0' }, items }] }, W),

+})();
```
