+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/nomen.js — the Nomenclature output tab (window.PSBUiNomen): the old app's "Nomenclature — Live Variable Reference"

+   (R at its path, as the result tabs' data-ev) or an input; nothing is calculated or saved (the search text lives in this page view).
+     output(ctx) -> HTML; after(el, ctx) wires the search box. ctx = { P, inp, R, W, ui } */

+      ['S<sub>td</sub>', 'Composite modulus, deck top (÷ n)', 'in³', 'cp.Std', 'sec.Std', ''],
+      ['n', 'Modular ratio E<sub>c,d</sub> / E<sub>c</sub>', '—', 'cp.n', 'sec.n', '4.6.2.6']]],
+    ['Materials and moduli', [

+      ['f′<sub>ci</sub>', 'Girder concrete strength at release', 'ksi', { inp: 'mat.fci' }, { goin: 'mat' }, '5.4.2.1'],
+      ['f′<sub>c,d</sub>', 'Deck concrete strength', 'ksi', { inp: 'mat.fcd' }, { goin: 'mat' }, '5.4.2.1'],
+      ['E<sub>ci</sub>', 'Girder modulus at release', 'ksi', 'lo.Eci', 'ls.Eci', '5.4.2.4'],
+      ['E<sub>c</sub>', 'Girder modulus, final', 'ksi', 'cp.Ecg', 'sec.Ecg', '5.4.2.4'],
+      ['E<sub>c,d</sub>', 'Deck modulus', 'ksi', 'cp.Ecd', 'sec.Ecd', '5.4.2.4'],
+      ['E<sub>p</sub>', 'Strand modulus', 'ksi', { inp: 'str.Ep' }, { goin: 'mat' }, '5.4.4.2'],
+      ['f<sub>pu</sub>', 'Strand tensile strength', 'ksi', { inp: 'str.fpu' }, { goin: 'mat' }, 'Table 5.4.4.1-1']]],
+    ['Loads and distribution', [

## 2026-11-15 — H2: Drawings tab: bearing reactions and analysis diagrams sheets (display and export only)
PR #1584: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1584
### Request
- Review finding D3 (scratchpad review ps-vs-steel.md "Drawings"), batch H2: the Steel Bridge app's bearing reactions and analysis diagrams sheets (apps/steel-bridge/engine/sheets.js `reac`, `diag`) for this app.
### What changed
- `ui/sheets.js` (anchor `/* ---------- batch H2 (2026-11-15): bearing reactions, analysis diagrams`):
  - `reacBlocks(P, A)`: BEARING REACTIONS of every girder line at every support from `PSBHandoffs.srAll(P, A.cells)` (the values the Project tab sends to Bridge Substructure Loading, allGirders: each span the girder type on the line, its engine's own end reactions `bxSuperRxPayload`; a pier the sum of the two spans' ends, srAll's own sum): GIRDER, SUPPORT, X, DC1, DC2, DW (kip, the payload's values to 0.001 kip as sent; the Analysis tab shows the same to 2 decimals); with more than one span a second table PIER REACTIONS: EACH SPAN'S END (srAll's `shares`, 3 decimals). Live load not listed (not sent).
  - `plot()` / `lab()` / `diag(D, C)`: adapted COPY of the steel app's dxfPlot / dxfLab / dxfDiag: per girder type on its first line (as the girder sheets), R.diagrams at the engine's stations: moments (girder + DC1 as one curve: `M_g + M_DC1`, plotted only; DC2 dashed, DW, LL+IM ±, Strength I max / min), shears (V_DC, V_DW, V_LL±, V_StrI±); labels: M_StrI_pos at the station nearest each tenth point, M_StrI_neg at the ends when negative, V_StrI_pos at the left end and V_StrI_neg at the right end; the demand source named (`PSBDemands.describe`: this app's analysis, custom table, MIDAS file with its stations and span). Plot amplitude 1.1 in (paper D), 0.7 in (paper B, so the sheet fits); `plot(…, amp)`.
  - `build`: after the schedule `diag<k>` per type (kmin 48), then `reac` (block sheets), then `summ`; `typeModels` entries carry `T` (the type object, for describe).
- `ui/drawings.js`: `SRC` `diag` (Analysis tab, Loads input tab), `reac` (Analysis tab, Project input tab); the layer list names S-DIAG-AXIS / -DC / -DW / -LL / -STR.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed; every value is an engine or hand-off value (no new formula; girder + DC1 summed for one plotted curve only). Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- Three spans 80 / 110 / 80 ft made continuous, 6 lines: G1 Abut. 1 DC1 68.524 kip; Pier 1 DC1 162.744 = 68.524 (span 1 right end) + 94.220 (span 2 left end); DC2 10.675 = 5.175 + 5.500; DW 20.683 = 10.027 + 10.656.
- Default simple span: G2 Abut. 1 DC1 114.785, DC2 7.200, DW 11.700 kip (the Analysis tab: 114.79 / 7.20 / 11.70).
- Interior S1 on G2 (span 1, 80 ft): M_u labels at the tenth points 0 … 4257 kip-ft; V_u 267.3 kip at the left end, −302.3 kip at the right end (continuous end).
### How verified
- `tests/engine/psbridge-drawings-h.test.mjs` (+2 tests): every reaction row = srAll (every line × support), the shares; every point of the 13 curves = R.diagrams at its station (x and value, through the plot scale), the axis = L, the tenth-point and end labels, the demand source, the sheet fits (paper D and B).
- `tests/engine/psbridge-drawings.test.mjs`, smokes `ps-bridge-drawings*.mjs`: the new sheet list.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- H2-D1. The analysis diagrams are drawn per girder type on its first line (as the girder sheets of item B); a type's other lines are on the Analysis tab with that line.
- H2-D2. The bearing reactions sheet lists DC1, DC2 and DW only (the hand-off's values; the steel sheet's LL+IM and service sums are not formed here: no new arithmetic, and the PS hand-off sends no live load).
### Other copies
- plot / lab / diag adapted from apps/steel-bridge/engine/sheets.js; keep a fix in step.
## 2026-11-15 — H3: Drawings tab: camber and haunch, end zone reinforcement, diaphragm details and schedule, deck reinforcement and overhang sheets (display and export only)
PR #1585: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1585
### Request
- Review finding D3 (scratchpad review ps-vs-steel.md "Drawings"), batch H3: a camber / haunch sheet, an end-zone (splitting / confinement) reinforcement sheet, diaphragm details (geometry only, as the app has it) and the deck overhang / reinforcement (the Steel Bridge app's camber tables, deck overhang and diaphragm sheets have these PS equivalents).
### What changed
- `ui/sheets.js` (anchor `/* ---------- batch H3 (2026-11-15): camber and haunch, end zone reinforcement, diaphragms, deck`):
  - `tablesAt` / `tableCols`: the H1 `table()` drawn under a figure, one below the other / in columns side by side.
  - `camber(D, C)` (sheet `camb<k>`, each girder type on its first line, kmin 24): R.haunch at the tenth points plotted (erection camber, deck placement (haunch), beam seat, haunch build-up; `plot()` of H2) and tabulated (x, shape factor, erection, deck, seat, build-up: the Camber & deflection tab's table, same decimals); the camber at midspan by stage (R.cam rel, erect, afterDeck, seat, final) and its components (dPS, dSW, dDK, dDia when > 1e-4, dSD, dLL, llLim); a note with the haunch build-up at both ℄ bearings and at midspan (R.haunch[0], [last], the midspan row). The engine computes the haunch (R.haunch.buildup), so it is shown, not derived.
  - `endzone(D, C)` (sheet `endz<k>`, kmin 4): the girder end in elevation (true scale; depth R.g.h; break line), ℄ bearing at e_end (`opt.endOh`, dimension E_END), the splitting zone dashed with its dimension R.splitZone ("SPLITTING ZONE H/4" or W/4 by R.splitDir) and the legs × area (opt.splitN × opt.splitAv); the confinement bars as lines at i × R.conf.s from the end, i = 0 … R.conf.n − 1 (chain dimension = R.conf.provExt), the required extent R.conf.reqExt; tables: splitting (R.splitDem, R.AsSplit, provided = R.AsSplitProv, R.splitZone, orientation, f_y), confinement (bar, spacing, n, extents; or "not required" with R.conf.why), bonded release tension steel (R.relSteel), and the engine's three checks (demand, limit, ratio, status). Bar positions and heights are schematic (noted).
  - `diaphragms(D, C)` (sheet `diaph`, kmin 24) and `diaphBlocks()` (block sheet `diapht`, DIAPHRAGM SCHEDULE): per girder type a line ℄ bearing to ℄ bearing with a mark at each entered diaphragm a (inp.loads.diaph, 0 ≤ a ≤ L) and the chain from ℄ bearing; the schedule: type, span, lines, no., a, L − a (the display difference), P (kip, DC1); the continuity diaphragms of the framing plan's pier lines (PSBPlan.model cont). Drawn when any type has diaphragms or the spans are made continuous; else listed as not in the set. No diaphragm section is an input (noted).
  - `deck(D, C)` (sheet `deck`, kmin 4; the type on G1 with R.deck, else the first with R.deck): the deck from the left edge over G1 into the first bay, true scale: thickness R.deck.ts, OVERHANG R.deck.oh, S = R.deck.Ls, the top and bottom bars at the engine's effective depths (y = ts − neg.dEff, ts − pos.dEff; dimensions D TOP / D BOT), the negative-moment design section R.deck.xneg from ℄ G1, the barrier base R.deck.bBar (height schematic); the bars entered (deck.barTop / sTop, barBot / sBot); a table of every type's R.deck (Mu+, φMn+, ratio; Mu−, φMn−, ratio; Mu overhang, φMn, ratio; distribution steel %). Deck design off: listed as not in the set.
  - `build`: after the schedule `camb<k>` per type, `endz<k>` per type, `diaph` + `diapht`, `deck`, then the H2 `diag<k>`, `reac`, and `summ`; the plot amplitude `amp` (1.1 in on D, 0.7 in on B) shared with the diagrams.
- `ui/drawings.js`: `SRC` `camb` (Camber & deflection tab, Materials), `endz` (End zone & hold-down tab, Girders & strands), `diaph` (Diaphragms / deck, Bridge layout), `diapht` (Diaphragms / deck, Loads & LLDF), `deck` (Deck tab, Diaphragms / deck); the layer list (+ S-CAMB-ERECT, -DECK, -SEAT, S-HAUNCH, S-ZONE, S-REBAR) and the note.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed; every value is an input or an engine value (R.haunch, R.cam, R.splitZone, R.AsSplit, R.AsSplitProv, R.conf, R.relSteel, R.deck, R.checks); the only arithmetic is drawing positions (i × s, ts − d_eff) and the display L − a. Harness B: 0 differences.
### Check case
- Default BT-72, interior S1 on G2, L = 120 ft: haunch build-up 2.00 in at both ℄ bearings, 5.33 in at midspan; erection camber at midspan 5.150 in; release 2.902 in up.
- End zone: splitting zone h/4 = 18.0 in; A_s,req 3.12 in², provided 12 × 0.31 = 3.72 in², ratio 0.838 PASS; confinement No. 4 at 6.00 in, 19 bars, chain 18 @ 6" = 108 in = 1.5d = 108.0 in, ratio 1.000.
- Deck on (S = 9 ft, overhang 3 ft, t = 8 in): d top 5.186 in, d bot 6.686 in, negative design section 14 in; Mu+ 12.20 / φMn+ 17.38 k-ft/ft (0.702), Mu− 7.58 / 13.20 (0.574), overhang 6.81 / 13.20 (0.516).
### How verified

## 2026-11-15 — Batch G5: strand editing by clicking the section (add on the grid, remove, debond, move; edit log; "↺ Revert strand edits"; each edit one Undo step; the strand fit respected) and the table's "Clear debonding on this row" (input editor; no calculation change)
PR #1586: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1586
### Request
- Old-vs-new review 2026-11-15, rows #16 ("Clear debonding on this row", O:6031) and #18 (interactive strand editing in Live Geometry: add mode on the 2 in grid, click a strand to remove / debond / nudge, the edit log, Revert strand edits; O:4936-5024, 6051-6066).
### What changed
- **New `ui/strandedit.js`** (window.PSBStrandEdit): `apply(rows, op, o)` the old app's edit rules (add one strand, NEXT a pair, to the row at that height or a new row, rows sorted; remove one / a pair, the row dropped at 0, one row always kept; debond the next strand / pair of the row, cycling back to none, a row with no length gets round(0.1 L) ft; clear; move the row ±1 in, ≥ 1 in, sorted); `slots(g, rows, o)` the add mode's empty 2 in grid positions (y = 2 … min(0.4 h, 16) in, the bottom flange width), only at heights where one more strand passes the input check and each slot itself fits (PSBInputCheck.misfit); `fitErrs` / `fitCtx` the input check's strand-fit errors (PSBInputCheck.collect on the scope's inputs, as engine/autodesign.js fitErrors) — an edit that would add one is refused with its message; `card(label)` / `mount(host, ctx)` the card "Edit strands on the section" (an SVG of the section at ℄ bearing or midspan, strands clickable, the row panel, the log, Revert).
- **`index.html`**: the script; the card after "Strand pattern" on the Girders & strands tab (anchor `window.PSBStrandEdit.card(`); its mount after drawInputs with the scope's rows (base, or the girder type in scope: its override), `commit(rows, msg)` = the same path as a table edit (`viewOf(scopeK())`, `BR.setOvr`, `changed()` = one Undo step) and a toast with Undo.
- **`ui/inputs.js`** `table('base.rows')`: a "⌁✕" button (data-act="clrdb", title "Clear debonding on this row") on a row with n_d or a debonded length; `onClick`: `act === 'clrdb'` sets the row's nd and dbnd to 0 (one change, one Undo step).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- No key or format changed: the edits write the same base.rows / type overrides as the table. The edit log and the starting layout for Revert live in the page view only.
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed: an input editor. The results follow the rows entered, as with the table.
- Decision (pending engineer review): unlike the old app, an edit that would put a strand outside the input check's strand fit (PS-28 / PS-33 / PS-39) is refused (the old app accepted it); NEXT beams: no add grid (as the old app), remove / debond / move by pairs.
### Check case
- Default project: row y = 2 in (12 strands): debond → n_d 1, length round(0.1 × 120) = 12 ft; again → 2; the 26 in bottom flange holds 12 strands a row on the 2 in grid: a 13th is refused; the bottom row moved to y = 1 in is refused (strands within 2 in of the soffit).
### How verified
- New tests/engine/psbridge-strandedit.test.mjs (3), tests/smoke/ps-bridge-strandedit.mjs. PS checks: see the PR.
## 2026-11-15 — Batch G7 / G9: the splitting steel orientation graphic for slabs and box beams (End zone tab, drawn from the section) and the old app's "↩ MCT Analysis" header button when opened from the MCT Generator (display / navigation only)
PR #1587: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1587
### Request
- Old-vs-new review 2026-11-15, rows #85 (splitting-steel orientation for slabs / boxes, the old app's AASHTO Fig. C5.9.4.4.1-2 image, O:7544-7547: draw our own, do not copy AASHTO art) and #131 ("↩ MCT Analysis", O:9702 with bridgeNav, O:2477).
### What changed
- **`ui/endzone.js`**: a graphic card `gfx_ezsplit` (only for a deck slab or a box beam, after "Girder end") and `splitFig(R, inp, W)`: (1) the end face, true scale, from halfPolygon / sectionVoids: a slab with horizontal bars across the width above and below the voids, a box with vertical legs in the webs (solid) and horizontal flange bars (dashed, the commentary's second direction, not in the check); (2) the plan (slab) or side view (box) of the end region with the provided splitN bars spread evenly within h/4 = R.splitZone; mounted in `after()` with a caption citing 5.9.4.4.1 / C5.9.4.4.1. Exported `splitFig`.
- **New `ui/mctnav.js`** (window.PSBMctNav): `fromMct(w)` 'frame' (framed by another page) / 'tab' (opened from the repo-root index.html: referrer or opener, or `#from=mct` / `?from=mct`) / ''; `back(w, how)`: framed, the old message `{ source: 'bridge-suite', embed: null }` to the parent (the MCT shows itself), else `location.href = '../../index.html'`; `mount(btn, w)`.
- **`index.html`**: the script; a header button `#bMct` "↩ MCT Analysis" (hidden unless opened from the MCT) after "← All tools"; its CSS; `PSBMctNav.mount($('bMct'), window)` after the Undo / Redo wiring.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None. No key read or written (the old app's bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths record is not used: switch-over item).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed (display / navigation). Open item (not changed; raised in the PR): for box beams the engine takes h = the overall height (pbd-compute.js `splitH = g.isDeck ? w : h`), where AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.9.4.4.1 says the lesser of the overall width or height for box / tub girders (e.g. AASHTO BIV-36 (42in): 42 in deep, 35.5 in wide → h/4 = 10.5 in used, 8.9 in by the article).
- Decision (pending engineer review): the old app showed "↩ MCT Analysis" always; here only when the page was opened from the MCT (framed, from the MCT's file, or #from=mct), because the MCT opens the old app until the switch-over.
### Check case
- AASHTO SIV-48 (21in) voided slab: R.splitDir = 'width', h/4 = 47.5 / 4 = 11.9 in (actual width 47.5 in), the plan view "bars across the width"; AASHTO BIII-36 box: 'height', h/4 = 39 / 4 = 9.8 in, "legs in each web".
### How verified
- New tests/engine/psbridge-gsplitmct.test.mjs (2), tests/smoke/ps-bridge-gsplitmct.mjs. PS checks: see the PR.
### Other copies
- None.

+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/strandedit.js — strand editing by clicking the section (window.PSBStrandEdit): the old app's Live Geometry editing
+   (O:4936-5024, 6051-6066): "+ add strands" on the 2 in grid, a strand clicked to debond (cycle), move its row ±1 in or remove one; the
+   edit log ("Strand edits from the graphic"), "↺ Revert strand edits" back to the layout before the first edit of this page view. Created
+   2026-11-15 (batch G5). Classic script; an INPUT editor: it changes only the straight strand rows (base.rows, or a girder type's rows in
+   its scope), as the table does; every edit is one change of the project (one step of the header's Undo). The draped strands are not
+   edited here (as the old app). Nothing is calculated.
+
+   Rules (the old app's, O:4943-4968): add = one strand (NEXT: a pair) to the row at that height, or a new row there; remove = one strand
+   (NEXT: a pair) from the row, the row dropped at 0 (one row always stays: the engine's mergeInputs reads an empty list as its default
+   rows); debond = the next strand (NEXT: pair) of the row debonded, cycling back to none (a row with no debonded length gets 10 % of the
+   span, rounded to 1 ft, as the old app; the length is edited in the table); move = the row's y ± 1 in (≥ 1 in), rows sorted by y.
+   Unlike the old app, an edit whose strands would not fit (the input check's strand fit, PS-28 / PS-33 / PS-39: inside the concrete,
+   2 in from its edges, 1.25 in from a void) is refused with the reason, and the add grid shows only the slots of rows that would fit.
+
+   Pure: apply(rows, op, o) -> { rows, msg } | { err }  (op: 'add' (o.y), 'remove' | 'debond' | 'up' | 'down' | 'clear' (o.i), o.next, o.L);
+         slots(g, rows, o) -> [{ x, y }] the add targets (o.misfit(q) the input check's, o.fits(rows) the whole check).
+   Page: card(label) (HTML) and mount(host, ctx), ctx = { R, rows (the scope's rows), scopeKey, commit(rows, msg) -> { err }, fits, fitWhy (fitCtx) }. */
+(function () {
+  'use strict';
+  const esc = s => String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' }[c]));
+  const fx = (v, d) => (typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v) ? (+v.toFixed(d)).toString() : '—');
+  const copy = rows => (rows || []).map(r => Object.assign({}, r));
+  const S = { add: false, sel: null, view: 'end', start: {}, log: {} };   // page view only: start layout and log per scope key
+
+  function apply(rows0, op, o) {
+    o = o || {}; const inc = o.next ? 2 : 1, rows = copy(rows0), w = o.next ? 'a pair of strands' : '1 strand';
+    if (op === 'add') {
+      const y = Math.round(+o.y), i = rows.findIndex(r => Math.abs(+r.y - y) < 1);
+      if (i >= 0) rows[i].n = (+rows[i].n || 0) + inc; else { rows.push({ n: inc, y, dbnd: 0, nd: 0 }); rows.sort((a, b) => +a.y - +b.y); }
+      return { rows, msg: `Added ${w} at y = ${y} in` };
+    }
+    const i = o.i, r = rows[i]; if (!r) return { err: 'No such row.' };
+    if (op === 'remove') {
+      const n = Math.max(0, (+r.n || 0) - inc);
+      if (n === 0 && rows.length === 1) return { err: 'One straight strand row stays (the engine reads an empty list as its default rows): add a strand elsewhere first, or edit the row in the table.' };
+      if (n === 0) rows.splice(i, 1); else { r.n = n; if ((+r.nd || 0) > n) r.nd = n; }
+      return { rows, msg: `Removed ${w} from y = ${fx(+r.y, 2)} in` };
+    }
+    if (op === 'debond') {
+      if (!(+r.dbnd > 0)) r.dbnd = Math.max(+r.dbnd || 0, Math.round((+o.L || 0) * 0.1));
+      const cur = Math.min(+r.nd || 0, +r.n || 0);
+      r.nd = cur + inc <= +r.n ? cur + inc : 0; if (r.nd === 0) r.dbnd = 0;
+      return { rows, msg: r.nd > 0 ? `Debonded ${r.nd} of ${r.n} strands at y = ${fx(+r.y, 2)} in (${fx(+r.dbnd, 2)} ft)` : `Cleared the debonding at y = ${fx(+r.y, 2)} in` };
+    }
+    if (op === 'clear') { r.nd = 0; r.dbnd = 0; return { rows, msg: `Cleared the debonding at y = ${fx(+r.y, 2)} in` }; }
+    if (op === 'up' || op === 'down') {
+      const y = Math.max(1, Math.round(+r.y + (op === 'up' ? 1 : -1))); if (y === +r.y) return { err: 'The row is at the lowest height (1 in).' };
+      r.y = y; rows.sort((a, b) => +a.y - +b.y);
+      return { rows, msg: `Moved the row to y = ${y} in` };
+    }
+    return { err: 'Unknown edit.' };
+  }
+  /* slots(g, rows, o): the empty 2 in grid positions of the add mode (the old app's: y = 2, 4, … up to min(0.4 h, 16) in, the bottom flange
+     width), only at heights where one more strand keeps the row inside the input check's fit (o.fits(rows) true) and each slot itself fits
+     (o.misfit(q) ''); occupied positions (o.occ: Set of 'x,y') left out */
+  function slots(g, rows, o) {
+    const out = [], bw = +g.bbf || +g.w || 0, maxCols = Math.floor((bw - 4) / 2) + 1, top = Math.min(g.h * 0.4, 16);
+    for (let y = 2; y <= top + 1e-9; y += 2) {
+      const r = apply(rows, 'add', { y }); if (r.err || (o.fits && !o.fits(r.rows))) continue;
+      for (let c = 0; c < maxCols; c++) { const x = (c - (maxCols - 1) / 2) * 2, q = { x, y };
+        if (o.occ && o.occ.has(`${x.toFixed(1)},${y.toFixed(1)}`)) continue; if (o.misfit && o.misfit(q)) continue; out.push(q); }
+    }
+    return out;
+  }
+
+  /* fitErrs(P, sk, rows): the input check's strand-fit errors (paths base.rows… / base.harp…) of the inputs in scope (sk ≥ 0: girder type sk,
+     on its first line and span; else the base design) with these straight rows: the page's PSBInputCheck.collect, as engine/autodesign.js */
+  function fitErrs(P, sk, rows) {
+    const BR = window.PSBBridge, IC = window.PSBInputCheck; if (!IC) return [];
+    const typed = sk >= 0 && BR && BR.hasTypes(P), b = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(typed ? BR.effBase(P, sk) : P.base)); b.rows = copy(rows);
+    const g = typed ? BR.typeLines(P, sk)[0] : null, design = typed && g ? { g, s: P.types[sk].span } : P.design;
+    try { return IC.collect(Object.assign({}, P, { base: b, types: undefined, design })).errors.filter(e => /^base\.(rows|harp)(\.|$)/.test(e.path)).map(e => e.msg); } catch (e) { return []; }
+  }
+  /* fitCtx(P, sk, rows0): fits(rows) = no more strand-fit errors than the rows as they are (an edit may not add one); fitWhy(rows): the first new message */
+  function fitCtx(P, sk, rows0) {
+    const n0 = fitErrs(P, sk, rows0).length, memo = new Map(), errs = rows => { const k = JSON.stringify(rows); if (!memo.has(k)) memo.set(k, fitErrs(P, sk, rows)); return memo.get(k); };
+    return { fits: rows => errs(rows).length <= n0, fitWhy: rows => { const e = errs(rows), e0 = fitErrs(P, sk, rows0); return (e.find(m => !e0.includes(m)) || e[0] || '').replace(/^Straight strand rows, /, ''); } };
+  }
+
+  /* ---------- the page ---------- */
+  function card(label) {
+    return `<section class="sec" id="card-strandEdit"><div class="secHead">Edit strands on the section${label ? ` of ${esc(label)}` : ''}</div><div class="secBody" id="strandEditHost"><p class="note">Shown when the inputs have no error.</p></div></section>`;
+  }
+  function svg(ctx, W) {
+    const { R, rows } = ctx, g = R.g, ss = R.ss, SG = window.PSBStrandGfx, end = S.view === 'end';
+    const half = halfPolygon(g), poly = half.concat(half.slice().reverse().map(p => [-p[0], p[1]]));
+    const bmax = Math.max(+g.bbf || 0, +g.btf || 0, +g.w || 0), pad = 16, sc = Math.min((W - 2 * pad) / bmax, 300 / g.h), H = g.h * sc + 2 * pad, cx = W / 2;

+/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/mctnav.js — the old app's "↩ MCT Analysis" header button (window.PSBMctNav). Classic script. Created 2026-11-15 (batch G9;
+   the old app O:9702 and its bridgeNav(null), O:2477-2486).
+   The old app showed the button always; here it is shown when the page was opened from the MCT Generator (index.html at the repo root):
+   framed by it (window.top is another page), opened by it in a new tab (window.opener set, document.referrer the MCT's file) or with
+   "#from=mct" / "?from=mct" in the address. Click: framed, the old message to the parent window { source: 'bridge-suite', embed: null }
+   (the MCT shows itself again, as for the old app); otherwise this tab goes to the MCT Generator, ../../index.html (the old app's built-in
+   path for the MCT; the old app's appPaths record of where each app was last opened, bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths, is not read: it is part of
+   the switch-over). Nothing is saved; no shared key is read or written.
+     fromMct(w) -> 'frame' | 'tab' | ''   back(w, how)   mount(btn, w) */
+(function () {
+  'use strict';
+  const MCT = '../../index.html';
+  const isMctFile = u => { try { const p = decodeURIComponent(String(u || '').split(/[?#]/)[0]).replace(/\\/g, '/'); return /\/index\.html$/i.test(p) && !/\/apps\/[^/]+\/index\.html$/i.test(p); } catch (e) { return false; } };
+  function fromMct(w) {
+    if (!w) return '';
+    let framed = false; try { framed = w.self !== w.top; } catch (e) { framed = true; }
+    if (framed) return 'frame';
+    const loc = w.location || {}, flag = /(^|[?#&])from=mct(&|$)/i.test(String(loc.search || '') + String(loc.hash || ''));
+    const ref = w.document && w.document.referrer ? isMctFile(w.document.referrer) : false;
+    let op = false; try { op = !!w.opener && isMctFile(w.opener.location.href); } catch (e) { op = false; }   // another file:// page: not readable
+    return flag || ref || op ? 'tab' : '';
+  }
+  function back(w, how) {
+    if (how === 'frame') { try { w.parent.postMessage({ source: 'bridge-suite', embed: null }, '*'); return 'message'; } catch (e) { /* fall through */ } }
+    w.location.href = MCT; return 'navigate';
+  }
+  function mount(btn, w) {
+    if (!btn) return ''; const how = fromMct(w); btn.hidden = !how;
+    if (how) btn.onclick = () => back(w, how);
+    return how;
+  }
+  window.PSBMctNav = { MCT, fromMct, back, mount, isMctFile };
+})();

## 2026-11-15 — Batch G8: the 3D view's reinforcement cage layers (stirrups, longitudinal bars, splitting steel, cambered shape, strand stress colour) and "Capture for the Report" (Report §2 figure) (display only)
PR #1588: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1588
### Request
- Old-vs-new review 2026-11-15, rows #73 (the old 3D reinforcement cage: stirrups, longitudinal bars, splitting / confinement, deformed camber, strand-stress colour; O:5127-5361) and #110 (3D snapshot captured into the report, O:5090, 5348).
### What changed
- **`ui/view3d.js`**: LAY + `stir` Stirrups, `lon` Longitudinal bars, `spl` Splitting steel (h/4), `cam` Cambered shape (× 12), `sfc` Strand stress colour (all off at first; kept in ui.v3d.lay as the other layers); `geom()` adds `out.cage` for the girders whose strands are drawn (the type shown; a close-up's line): the stirrup stations of the old app (from 3 in, s_end within endZoneLen × L of each ℄ bearing, s_int between), U ties in the web (NEXT: each stem; box: each web), two longitudinal top bars, splitN legs within h/4 of each end (deck slab: bars across the width within w/4); `build()` draws them (LineSegments), the cambered outline (R.cam.final × 12 on a parabola, from ctx.res) and the strand stress colour (each straight strand in 24 pieces coloured by strandSys(...).devStress(x) / f_ps, grey → amber → red, the old app's colours; the plain straight strands hidden while it is on); notes `#v3d-cage`; the cage counts in `PSB3DUI.state().cage` (the existing `counts` unchanged); a button "Capture for the Report" (`V.snap = { png, at, key, meta }`, page view only), `PSB3DUI.snapshot()`.
- **`ui/report.js`**: `snap3d` (PSB3DUI.snapshot()) passed to the model, in the rebuild key.
- **`report/builders.js`** `snapFig(P, X)`: §2 "Bridge and the design girder": after the framing plan, the figure "3D view (captured on the 3D view tab, <time>): <view, layers>" (a PNG data URL only), with a note (a warning when the project changed since the capture).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- No key changed; psb2.ui's v3d.lay gets five optional layer flags. The capture is not saved (page view only, as the old app).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4)
- None changed: drawing positions only; camber and f_ps(x) are the engine's (R.cam.final; the strand system's devStress with R.fMid.fps and R.fpe, 5.9.4.3.2).
### Check case
- Default project, type shown Interior S1 on G2 (BT-72, L = 120 ft = 1,440 in, s_end = 6 in within 0.25 L = 360 in of each ℄ bearing, s_int = 18 in): stirrup stations 3, 9, 15, 21, 27 … in, 160 stirrups (the old app's walk); 2 top bars; splitN = 12 legs at each end within h/4 = 72 / 4 = 18 in: 24 legs.
### How verified
- New tests/engine/psbridge-3dcage.test.mjs (4), tests/smoke/ps-bridge-3dcage.mjs. PS checks: see the PR.
### Other copies
- None (apps/steel-bridge/ui/view3d.js not changed).

-/* apps/ps-bridge/ui/mctnav.js — the old app's "↩ MCT Analysis" header button (window.PSBMctNav). Classic script. Created 2026-11-15 (batch G9;
-   the old app O:9702 and its bridgeNav(null), O:2477-2486).
-   The old app showed the button always; here it is shown when the page was opened from the MCT Generator (index.html at the repo root):
-   framed by it (window.top is another page), opened by it in a new tab (window.opener set, document.referrer the MCT's file) or with
-   "#from=mct" / "?from=mct" in the address. Click: framed, the old message to the parent window { source: 'bridge-suite', embed: null }
-   (the MCT shows itself again, as for the old app); otherwise this tab goes to the MCT Generator, ../../index.html (the old app's built-in
-   path for the MCT; the old app's appPaths record of where each app was last opened, bridgeSuite.v1.appPaths, is not read: it is part of
-   the switch-over). Nothing is saved; no shared key is read or written.
-     fromMct(w) -> 'frame' | 'tab' | ''   back(w, how)   mount(btn, w) */
-(function () {
-  'use strict';
-  const MCT = '../../index.html';
-  const isMctFile = u => { try { const p = decodeURIComponent(String(u || '').split(/[?#]/)[0]).replace(/\\/g, '/'); return /\/index\.html$/i.test(p) && !/\/apps\/[^/]+\/index\.html$/i.test(p); } catch (e) { return false; } };
-  function fromMct(w) {

-    const loc = w.location || {}, flag = /(^|[?#&])from=mct(&|$)/i.test(String(loc.search || '') + String(loc.hash || ''));
-    const ref = w.document && w.document.referrer ? isMctFile(w.document.referrer) : false;
-    let op = false; try { op = !!w.opener && isMctFile(w.opener.location.href); } catch (e) { op = false; }   // another file:// page: not readable
-    return flag || ref || op ? 'tab' : '';
-  }
-  function back(w, how) {
-    if (how === 'frame') { try { w.parent.postMessage({ source: 'bridge-suite', embed: null }, '*'); return 'message'; } catch (e) { /* fall through */ } }
-    w.location.href = MCT; return 'navigate';
-  }
-  function mount(btn, w) {
-    if (!btn) return ''; const how = fromMct(w); btn.hidden = !how;
-    if (how) btn.onclick = () => back(w, how);
-    return how;
-  }
-  window.PSBMctNav = { MCT, fromMct, back, mount, isMctFile };
-})();

## 2026-11-21 — PR: claude/ps-handoff-stale-banner (PR #1659: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1659) (HO-D2 decided) — hand-offs stay click only, with a stale banner per channel (display only)
- **Engineer decision HO-D2 (2026-11-21), now decided:** keep the hand-offs click only (no channel locks, nothing sent or loaded on its own, no silent design change) and add a stale banner: when the data on a channel changed since this project last sent or loaded it, a banner names the channel with a one-click Send / Load that runs the existing click action (a Load still shows its confirm). Replaces "HO-D2 pending" in the earlier entries (item 12, batch D3, F, F3).
- **Where:**
  - New `apps/ps-bridge/engine/hostale.js` (`window.PSBHoStale`, pure, no DOM): `sig` (FNV-1a hash of the payload's sorted-key JSON without `producedAt` / `updatedAt` / `device`), `outState`, `inState`, `cellSig`, `capSig`, `allSig`, `pmSig`, `lldfBeam`, `lldfCur`, `dlCur`, `pmCur`, `mctState`, `geoState`, the record helpers `setSent` / `setLoaded` / `sentOf` / `loadedOf`, `carrySent`, `noStep`, `designText`.
  - `apps/ps-bridge/ui/handoffs.js`: new block after `function refresh()` (anchor `HO-D2 (engineer decision 2026-11-21): the stale banners`): `staleItems(ctx)` (memo keyed by the project text, the error count, whether every line's results are ready and the stored channel texts), `cardBody`, `staleBar(ctx)`, `onStale(e, ctx)`. Each send / pull records what it sent / loaded (anchors `// HO-D2`): `pmUse`, `pmShare`, `lldfPull`, `dlPull`, `srSend`, `secSend`, `geoSend`, `capSend`, `subSend` (new 3rd argument `only`); `mctLoad(ctx, tid)` (tid: the banner's girder type; the latest hand-off even after "Not now"); `onClick` / `onMct` first call `onStale`; `init(onMctChange, ctx)`; the storage listener redraws on every channel of the banners. The card: `<div id="hoStale">` at its top; its lock note.
    - Card note before: `The channel locks (auto-follow) of the old app are not part of this app yet.` After: `Every hand-off is a click (the old app's channel locks are not used): when a channel's data changes after this project sent or loaded it, a banner names it (here and above the output tabs) with Send / Load, which is the same click as the button here.`
    - `lldfPull` before: `let nb = null; try { nb = raw ? JSON.parse(raw).Nb : null; } … const db = c && nb != null && +nb === +P.xs.nb ? { index: c.g, label: 'G' + c.g, clsLabel: … } : null;` After: `const db = HSt().lldfBeam(P, c, inp, raw);` (the same rule, moved; HO-D5 unchanged).
    - `secSend` before: `if (write(…psSection…) && write(…updatedAt…)) say('Section properties sent …');` After: `{ HSt().setSent(ctx.P(), 'psSection', { sig: HSt().sig(p), at: p.producedAt, cell: cellRef(ctx) }); say(…same…); ctx.changed(); }` (geoSend, capSend, srSend, subSend, pmShare likewise; capSend `sig: HSt().capSig(r.inp, b.payload)`).
  - `apps/ps-bridge/index.html`: script `engine/hostale.js` after `engine/handoffs.js`; CSS `.hoStaleBar`, `#hoStale .notice`, `.hoStList` (not printed); `hoCtx` + `resultOf(k, g)` (the page's cached results: `result()` for the line shown, else `cellR`), `allNow()` (`allResults()` without force: null while running), `errN()`, `goin()`; `HOUI.init(() => drawOut(), hoCtx)`; `drawOut`: `h += HOUI.staleBar(hoCtx);` after the MCT banner.
    - `onlyShown` before: `(a, b) => { try { const x = JSON.parse(a), y = JSON.parse(b); delete x.design; delete y.design; return JSON.stringify(x) === JSON.stringify(y); } catch (e) { return false; } }` After: `(a, b) => window.PSBHoStale.noStep(a, b)` (also ignores `handoffs.sent`: a send is no Undo step).
    - `restore` before: `snap = from.pop(); P = JSON.parse(snap);` After: `const P0 = P; snap = from.pop(); P = window.PSBHoStale.carrySent(P0, JSON.parse(snap)); snap = JSON.stringify(P);` (a send stays sent through Undo / Redo; the loaded records follow the project text).
  - `apps/ps-bridge/ui/autodesign.js` `keyOf`: + `handoffs: undefined`; `apps/ps-bridge/report/builders.js` `snapFig`: the 3D capture's "captured before the last input change" compares the project texts without `handoffs` (a send is not an input change).
  - `apps/ps-bridge/engine/model.js` header: the optional field `handoffs`.
- **Channels and how staleness is detected:**
  - Outgoing (stale = the payload this project would send now ≠ the one it last sent, stamp fields aside): `psSection`, `lldfGeom`, `capacity`, `superReactions` (line shown) — of the girder type (id) and line recorded at the send (the banner's Send shows that type and line first); `capacity` with MIDAS / MCT demands: the hash of that girder's engine inputs (its payload runs the engine once per span); `superReactions` allGirders and `superGeometry` (every line, only when the page has every line's results); `projectMeta` (the title block fields). The card also notes when the shared key holds a later send (another project / tool).
  - Incoming (stale = the stored payload's `producedAt` ≠ the one loaded AND the values this design would take differ): `lldf` (the pull's `lldfFields` with its design-beam rule), `dlLoads` (`dlTheirs`), `projectMeta` (the pull's plan would change a field); MCT demands: the record `P.demands[type].midas` already kept (`MCT hand-off <id>`, its file with `producedAt`, member, project): stale when the same hand-off has another `producedAt` or a newer `latestId` is for the same member and project; `geometryChanges`: newer than the demands loaded (and not dismissed). The MCT banners already shown above (pending / geometry) are not repeated in the bar.
- **Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5):** no `bridgeSuite.v1.*` key, schema or payload changed; the check writes no key. New optional project field `P.handoffs = { sent: { <id>: { sig, at, cell? } }, loaded: { <id>: { sig, at, cell?, via? } } }` (psb2 project, schema version 1 unchanged), written only by a Send / Load click; absent in every project saved before = no record = no banner (the card: "nothing sent or loaded from this project yet (or only before this app kept a record of it)"). No migration needed; old projects open byte-identical.
- **Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4):** none changed; no computed value changes (display only). The payload builders and the click actions are unchanged; `lldfBeam` is the pull's own rule moved unchanged (the handoffs engine test and smoke pass unchanged).
- **Check case:** new project (Interior S1 on G2), Send section properties → no banner, card "up to date"; Cross-section bays 9 → 9.5 ft → "Girder section (psSection) of Interior S1 on G2: changed since last sent to MCT / LL & DL — Send" (composite Ic 1126663 → 1142965 in⁴); Send → banner gone. Pull lldf gM 0.612345 (09:00) → LL & DL re-publishes 0.612345 at 10:00 → no banner; 0.655 at 11:00 → "Distribution factors (lldf) … the LLDF tool has newer data than this design uses — Load"; Load → DFm 0.655, banner gone. Span 120 → 118 ft after Send to Substructure Loading and capacity → superGeometry, superReactions (every line), capacity named; psSection not (the section does not depend on L).
- **How verified:** `tests/engine/psbridge-hostale.test.mjs` (new, 8 tests); `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-hostale.mjs` (new, 8 checks); `tests/engine/psbridge-model.test.mjs` (script list + hostale.js); full `node tests/engine/run.mjs psbridge`; `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`; PS smokes skeleton, handoffs, subloads, mct, designbeam, undo, library, demands.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- HO-D2-a. The record of what this project sent / loaded is in the project (`P.handoffs`), so it goes with Export JSON and the saved projects; a send marks the saved-project chip "unsaved" (the record changed) but is not an Undo step.
- HO-D2-b. "Export (JSON)" is not recorded as a send (the banner compares with what the project published to the shared keys).
- HO-D2-c. Incoming data re-published with a newer time but the same values is not stale (LL & DL re-sends on recalculation).
- HO-D2-d. An older project that loaded MCT demands (P.demands' existing record) can show the MCT banner when the MCT Generator has since published for the same member and project (that provenance is known, not inferred).
- HO-D2-e. A recorded girder hand-off whose girder type or line was removed shows a neutral note in the card ("no longer in the project"), no banner.

## 2026-11-21 — E1-D4 / E1-D5: the load rating takes φ_s = 1.0 for shear and, in positive flexure, the minimum dead-load factor for a part that relieves the moment (engine/rating-along.js apply; Rating tab, Report) (CALCULATION CHANGE, §4)
PR: claude/ps-rating-e1-d4-d5 (link in the PR)
### Request
- Engineer decisions of 2026-11-21 on the E1 list "Decisions (pending engineer review)" (entry "E1: the HL-93 load rating at every station", PR #1580):
  - **E1-D4 decided:** the shear rating uses φ_s = 1.0 (MBE 4th Ed. (2026) Art. 6A.4.2.4), as the Steel Bridge app (apps/steel-bridge/engine/rating.js `phi()`: `vV = max(φ_c, 0.85)`): C = φ_c φV_n, the 0.85 lower limit of Eq. 6A.4.2.1-3 kept on the product (φ_c × 1.0). Flexure and Service III keep the entered φ_s as before.
  - **E1-D5 decided:** positive flexure at every station takes γ_DC = 1.25 / γ_DW = 1.50 for a dead-load moment that adds to the positive moment and 0.90 / 0.65 for one that relieves it, part by part as the negative-moment (pier) rows (girder + DC1, DC2, DW separately). Wherever the positive-flexure expression is: the engine's rating (R.rating, its midspan comparison and the vehicles' flexure) and the along-girder rows (flexP), so that the governing RF is still the engine's exactly.
- E1-D1, -D2, -D3, -D6, -D7, -D8, -D9 are unchanged (still as listed in the E1 entry). This entry records E1-D4 and E1-D5 as decided; the E1 entry is not edited.
### What changed
- The moved engine (`engine/pbd-compute.js` computeAll, "Load rating (LRFR, MBE)") is **not changed** (a verbatim slice of the frozen old app: tests/engine/psbridge-verbatim.test.mjs, harness A). As the other engine additions (engine/holddown.js, lldf-fg.js, pierblock.js), the change is applied after computeAll:
- **`engine/rating-along.js`** (`window.PSBRatingAlong`), new `posDL`, `posCap`, `shearCS`, `apply(inp, R)`, `dlNote`; exported `apply`, `posDL`, `dlNote`.
  - `posDL(mSW, mDC1, mDC2, mDW)`: `sNC = mSW + mDC1, s2 = mDC2, sW = mDW; gNC = sNC < 0 ? 0.90 : 1.25; g2 = s2 < 0 ? 0.90 : 1.25; gW = sW < 0 ? 0.65 : 1.50; max = (all three the maximum); D = max ? 1.25*DC + 1.50*DW : gNC*sNC + g2*s2 + gW*sW`. A zero part takes the maximum factor (no effect on D). `posCap(C, q) = q.max ? C − 1.25*q.DC − 1.50*q.DW : C − q.D` (with every part adding: the engine's `rateAt` in its order of operations, bit for bit).
  - `shearCS(rt) = clamp(rt.phiC * 1.0, 0.85, 1.0)` (rt.phiC = the entered φ_c, blank = 1.00; the engine's cap at 1.00 kept).
  - `apply(inp, R)` (once: skipped when `R.rating.phiCSv` exists): flexure: over `R.flexFull` with the engine's filter (`mLLpos > 1e-6`, `phiMn > 0`), `cap = posCap(phiCS*phiMn/12, posDL(...))`, RF = cap/(1.75 LL), the lowest (first in x order on a tie, the engine's `rf < rGov.RFinv`) becomes `R.rating` {x, Rn, MDC, MDW, MLL, RFinv, RFopr = cap/(1.35 LL), RTinv, RTopr, okInv, okOpr} plus `dl` (posDL of that station); no station: the engine's midspan fallback kept (dl null). Midspan (`rating.mid`): posDL of `R.fMid` when it is at x = L/2; where a part relieves, `RFinv/RFopr = (phiCS*mid.Rn − D)/(γ_LL mid.MLL)`; `mid.dl` added. Shear: `R.rating.phiCSv = shearCS`, `phiCSvFloor`; `R.shrRating.cs = phiCSv`; when phiCSv ≠ phiCS: `RFinv/RFopr = (phiCSv*phiVn − 1.25 VDC − 1.50 VDW)/(γ_LL VLL)` (the engine's 99 when VLL ≤ 0), RT, ok. Vehicles: `RFm = (phiCS*mid.Rn − D_mid)/M` where a midspan part relieves, `RFv = (phiCSv*phiVn − 1.25 VDC − 1.50 VDW)/V` when phiCSv ≠ phiCS; RF = min, gov, RT, ok recomputed. Nothing else in R is changed.
  - Anchor `// ---- flexure, positive: the engine's own rating expression at each R.flexFull station`. Before: `const Rn = r.phiMn / 12, DC = r.mSW + r.mDC1 + r.mDC2, DW = r.mDW, cap = cs * Rn - 1.25 * DC - 1.50 * DW;` After: `const Rn = r.phiMn / 12, q = posDL(r.mSW, r.mDC1, r.mDC2, r.mDW), cap = posCap(cs * Rn, q);` (row DC = q.DC, DW = q.DW, `parts.dl = q`).
  - Shear rows (anchor `const cap = cs * phiVn - 1.25 * VDC - 1.50 * VDW;` and the engine-section row `const cap = cs * sh.phiVn - ...`): `cs` → `csV` (= `R.rating.phiCSv`), C = `csV * phiVn`. `A.phiCSv` added.
  - `steps()`: flexP with a relieving part: a step `D` (`γ_nc(M_g + M_DC1) + γ_2 M_DC2 + γ_w M_DW` substituted) and RF = (C − D_u)/(γ_LL M_LL+IM); every flexP RF / D step notes the factor of each part and why (`dlNote`: "M_DC2 = −174.3: relieves: 0.90"). Shear C: label "φ_c φ_s φV_n with φ_s = 1.0 for shear", `eq \phi_{c}(1.0)\,\phi V_{n}`, substituted with phiCSv, note "φ_s = 1.0 (MBE 6A.4.2.4: … engineer decision E1-D4, 2026-11-21) …" (before: "the engine applies φ_c φ_s to shear (MBE 4th Ed. Art. 6A.4.2.4 takes φ_s = 1.0 for shear: see the Rating tab note)"). Header comment updated.
- **`engine/holddown.js`** `compute` (anchor `const compute = inp =>`): Before `const compute = inp => { const R = compute0(inp); return window.PSBPierBlock ? window.PSBPierBlock.apply(inp, R) : R; };` After: that line as `compute1`, and `const compute = inp => { const R = compute1(inp); return window.PSBRatingAlong && window.PSBRatingAlong.apply ? window.PSBRatingAlong.apply(inp, R) : R; };` (the page, its Report, Summary, Auto design, Compare and tests all use PSBHoldDown.compute).
- **`engine/worked-hdr.js`** `rating()`: new step `rt.phiCSv` (path `rating.phiCSv`: `\min(\max(\phi_c(1.0), 0.85), 1.0)`, note "φ_s = 1.0 (MBE 6A.4.2.4) …"); the `rt.phiCS` note says flexure only. `rfEq` / `rfF` take the station's `dl`: with a relieving part `(φ_cφ_s φM_n − [γ_nc(M_g+M_DC1) + γ_2 M_DC2 + γ_w M_DW])/(γ_LL M_LL+IM)`, else as before; RFinv / RFmid notes with `dlNote`. Shear steps `rt.RFvInv`, `rt.RFvOpr` and the vehicles' `RF_V` substitute phiCSv (eq `\phi_{c}(1.0)\,\phi V_{n}`); the vehicles' `RF_M` the midspan `dl`. Before (anchor `const rfF = (Rn, Dc, Dw, Ll, g) =>`): `(rt.phiCS * Rn - 1.25 * Dc - 1.50 * Dw) / (g * Ll)` for flexure, shear and vehicles.
- **`ui/rating.js`**: TOPICS `cs` ids `/^rt\.phiCSv?$/`; the Condition and system factors card a row "φ_c(1.0) used, shear (φ_s = 1.0, MBE 4th Ed. Art. 6A.4.2.4)" (data-ev `rating.phiCSv`) and its note; the along-girder notes (Strength I relieving factors E1-D2 / E1-D5; shear C = φ_cφV_n, E1-D4; before: "φ_cφ_s is applied to shear as in the engine's own rating (… the same RF when φ_s = 1.00, a lower RF when φ_s < 1.00)"); the engine flexure card's note and the vehicles card's note state the new rule.
- **`report/builders.js`** §2 Rating assumption (anchor `flexure in positive moment`): adds the E1-D5 rule and "C = φ_c φV_n: φ_s = 1.0 for shear, MBE 4th Ed. Art. 6A.4.2.4 … flexure keeps φ_c φ_s".
- **`tests/psbridge-compare.mjs`** (harness B): the old page gets engine/rating-along.js and its computeAll result goes through `apply` before it is read (the intended difference, as PS-35's lldf-fg.js); the rating values apply changes are logged.
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key, field or format. φ_c, φ_s are the existing `base.opt.rtPhiC`, `rtPhiS`. New result fields only (R.rating.phiCSv, phiCSvFloor, dl, mid.dl; R.shrRating.cs), not saved. Old projects open and compute as before (test).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4) and before → after
- **E1-D4.** AASHTO MBE 4th Ed. (2026) Art. 6A.4.2.4 (paraphrased: the system factor is taken as 1.0 for shear at the strength limit state), with Eq. 6A.4.2.1-2 (C = φ_c φ_s φR_n) and Eq. 6A.4.2.1-3 (φ_c φ_s ≥ 0.85); basis: engineer decision 2026-11-21 (as apps/steel-bridge/engine/rating.js, adopted 2026-11-10).
  - Before: C_V = clamp(φ_c φ_s, 0.85, 1.0) × φV_n. After: C_V = clamp(φ_c × 1.0, 0.85, 1.0) × φV_n. Flexure (C = clamp(φ_c φ_s, 0.85, 1.0) φM_n) and Service III unchanged. Higher (less conservative than before) shear RF when φ_s < 1.00 and φ_c φ_s > 0.85 is not the floor; the same when φ_s = 1.00.
  - Check case (default BT-72 interior simple span, L = 120 ft, φ_c = 1.00, **φ_s = 0.85 entered**; the engine's governing shear section x = 30.01 ft): φV_n = 334.550 kip, V_DC = 66.371, V_DW = 7.498, V_LL+IM = 83.989 kip. Before: (0.85 × 334.550 − 1.25 × 66.371 − 1.50 × 7.498)/(1.75 × 83.989) = (284.368 − 82.963 − 11.246)/146.981 = 190.158/146.981 = **1.294** (operating 190.158/113.385 = 1.677). After: (1.00 × 334.550 − 82.963 − 11.246)/146.981 = 240.341/146.981 = **1.635** (operating 2.120). Flexure 1.292 (φ_cφ_s = 0.85) unchanged; it now governs that design's engine ratings. A vehicle with V = 60 kip: RF_V 190.158/60 = 3.169 → 240.341/60 = 4.006.
  - The 19 + 5 test designs with their own φ_s: only "handling and deck on, rating vehicles, φc φs floored" (φ_c = φ_s = 0.90) changes: shear 1.294 → 1.408 (φ_cφ_s floored 0.85 → φ_c 0.90), its first entered vehicle (governed by shear) RF 2.113 → 2.299 (harness B log). With φ_s = 0.85 put on every design, every shear RF rises by about 25 % (e.g. continuous 3 spans 1.628 → 2.032).
- **E1-D5.** AASHTO MBE 4th Ed. (2026) Table 6A.4.2.2-1 (Strength I, prestressed concrete: γ_DC 1.25, γ_DW 1.50, the maximum factors) and AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Table 3.4.1-2 (the minimum permanent-load factors γ_p: DC 0.90, DW 0.65, for a load that reduces the force effect; LRFD Art. 3.4.1, the factor that gives the extreme effect), the same basis as E1-D2 (negative moment); basis: engineer decision 2026-11-21.
  - Before: cap = φ_cφ_s φM_n − 1.25 (M_g + M_DC1 + M_DC2) − 1.50 M_DW at every station. After: cap = φ_cφ_s φM_n − [γ_nc (M_g + M_DC1) + γ_2 M_DC2 + γ_w M_DW], γ_nc, γ_2 = 1.25 if the part is ≥ 0 (adds) else 0.90; γ_w = 1.50 if ≥ 0 else 0.65. More conservative (a lower RF) where a part is negative: near an interior support of a continuous unit (DC2, DW past their contraflexure) or a MIDAS / custom demand with a negative dead-load moment. Where every part adds (every simple span; midspan regions) the result is bit-identical (the engine's expression and order).
  - Check case (continuous 3 spans 100 / 125 / 100 ft, exterior G6 in span 2, `tests/engine/psbridge-tab-cases.mjs`; x = 12.5 ft from the left pier, M_LL+IM positive): φM_n = 11531.840 kip-ft (φ_cφ_s = 1.00); M_g + M_DC1 = 580.493 + 659.180 = 1239.673 (adds: 1.25); M_DC2 = −174.253 (relieves: 0.90); M_DW = −145.211 (relieves: 0.65); M_LL+IM = 348.458 kip-ft (1.75 × 348.458 = 609.801). Before: (11531.840 − 1.25 × 1065.420 − 1.50 × (−145.211))/609.801 = (11531.840 − 1331.775 + 217.816)/609.801 = 10417.881/609.801 = **17.084** (operating 22.146). After: D_u = 1.25 × 1239.673 + 0.90 × (−174.253) + 0.65 × (−145.211) = 1549.591 − 156.827 − 94.387 = 1298.377; (11531.840 − 1298.377)/609.801 = 10233.463/609.801 = **16.782** (operating 10233.463/470.418 = 21.754).
  - Governing RFs: on all 19 + 5 test designs the governing positive-flexure station has every part adding, so R.rating (station, RF_inv, RF_opr), rating.mid and the vehicles are unchanged (identity test, Object.is); 28 stations of the 3-span design (15 to 30 on the two-span and MIDAS designs) are lower, none governing (the lowest there, x = 25 ft: 6.514 → 6.507). A made-up case in the test (the 3-span design with φM_n = 1400 kip-ft, M_DC2 = −400, M_DW = −300 kip-ft at x = 12.5 ft) governs there: (1400 − 994.591)/609.801 = 0.665 after, against (1400 − 1.25 × 839.673 + 1.50 × 300)/609.801 = 1.312 before; R.rating and the along-girder row are the same value.
### Check case / tests (`tests/engine/psbridge-rating-along.test.mjs`, 4 new tests; 31 in the file)
- Identity: on every design of psbridge-tab-cases.mjs and psbridge-midas-cases.mjs (with a vehicle added), every flexP row whose parts all add = the engine's `rateAt` expression (Object.is); with φ_s = 1.00, R.rating, R.shrRating and R.vehRatings = the engine's own (apply disabled), field by field; a simple span has no relieving part.
- The E1-D5 hand check above (values, factors, the `D` step's substitution and its "relieves: 0.90" note; the governing station unchanged); the made-up governing case (R.rating = the row, the worked step and its pairs).
- The E1-D4 hand check above (before with apply disabled, after; flexure, Service III and the vehicle's RF_M unchanged; vehicle RF_V; the along-girder engine row; the `rt.phiCSv` and `rt.al.v.C` steps state φ_s = 1.0 (MBE 6A.4.2.4); every step's substituted value = the engine's; φ_c = 0.80, φ_s = 0.90: 0.85 for both; the Rating tab row).

### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- E1-D4: decided 2026-11-21 (this entry). E1-D5: decided 2026-11-21 (this entry). The other E1 decisions are as listed in the E1 entry.

## 2026-11-23 — PL-A: pedestrian live load (3.6.1.6) and utility line loads (DW) in the girder design (engine/pl.js, engine/bridge-dl.js; Cross-section tab, Loads & LLDF tab, Report) (CALCULATION CHANGE, §4)
PR #1664: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1664 (claude/ps-pedestrian-load)
### Request
- Engineer, 2026-11-23: close the gaps against the Steel Bridge app ("just go for it"). Gap A: a sidewalk could be entered but the Cross-section tab said "Not offered (no engine input): pedestrian live load, utilities …". Mirror the Steel Bridge app (apps/steel-bridge/engine/loads.js `dead()`: the load and its distribution; engine/analysis.js `analyzeGirder` / `llPL`: the load on the influence lines, added once to LL+IM; its fixlog entry "sb-ped-owner", 2026-10-30).
### What changed
- The moved engine (`engine/pbd-*.js`, verbatim, frozen) is **not changed** (tests/engine/psbridge-verbatim.test.mjs, harness A hold).
- **`engine/bridge-dl.js`** (`window.PSBBridgeDL`):
  - `CATS` (anchor `const CATS = ['DC2', 'DW', 'DC1']`): before `['DC2', 'DW', 'DC1']`; after `['DC2', 'DW', 'DC1', 'UT']`, and `PED_MIN = 2.0` (ft). `checks()`: `if (!blank(q.ped)) nn(q.ped, 'xs.dl.ped', 'Pedestrian live load');`.
  - `distribute()` (anchor `const R = dead({ Nb: N, OL: +x.ohL`): the arguments of the steel app's `dead()` are built by `args(ped, swL, swR)`; the dead loads are `dead(...args(0, sw('L'), sw('R')))`, the same call as before (ped 0). New: with `q.ped > 0` a second call `dead(...args(ped, pw('L'), pw('R')))`, `pw(s) = sw(s) > PED_MIN + 1e-9 ? sw(s) : 0` (only the sidewalks wider than 2.0 ft), from which only the pedestrian rows are kept: `out.ped = { q, per (the PL line loads), pl (klf per girder line), narrow, none, steps (dl.load.ped*, dl.G<g>.ped*, dl.G<g>.PL) }`. Each line load's shares do not depend on the other loads, so the second call changes nothing else.
  - New `pl(P)` (= `distribute(P).ped` or null). `line(P, g)`: after `const o = { DC2, DW }`: `if (R.ut && R.per.some(L => L.cat === 'UT')) { o.UT = R.ut[g - 1]; o.DWonly = o.DW; o.DW = o.DW + o.UT; }` and `if (R.ped && R.ped.pl[g - 1] !== 0) o.PL = R.ped.pl[g - 1];`.
  - `stepsFor()`: the steel app's `.UF` step left out, its `.UT` step relabelled "G<g>: utilities (DW)" (ref AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 3.5.1), a new step `dl.G<g>.DWt` (w_DW = w_DW,ws + w_UT), and the pedestrian steps appended. `withSteps()`: the `ld.wDW` note links `§dl.G<g>.DWt` when the line has a utility share.
- **`engine/pl.js`** (new, `window.PSBPL`): the pedestrian load in the engine's live load. The engine's live load reaches every check through six local functions of `computeAll` (`MLLx`, `VLLx`, `MLLpos`, `MLLneg`, `VLLpos`, `VLLneg`, pbd-compute.js "live load (per girder)") and one expression at the pier (`mll=-dfm*q.nd.Mn`); they are local, so they cannot be wrapped from outside as `distFactors` is (engine/rigid.js). For a girder WITH a pedestrian load (`inputs.pl.w > 0`), `run(inp, inner)` runs the app's engine call with the global `computeAll` replaced, for that call, by a copy made from the engine's own text (`computeAll.toString()`) with the 7 edits `EDITS` (each anchor must be found exactly once, else an error): the six functions renamed `<name>_0`, `<name> = PSBPL.channels(...)` = `<name>_0` + the pedestrian part, and `mll=-dfm*q.nd.Mn+PL_.pierNeg(q)`. A girder without one (no `inputs.pl`) runs the engine's own `computeAll`; nothing of this file is used.
  - `channels()`: simple span `M_PL(x) = w x (L − x)/2`, `V_PL+(x) = w (L − x)²/(2L)`, `V_PL−(x) = −w x²/(2L)`, the shear envelope `+ w (L − x_m)²/(2L)`; continuous unit: `w ×` the + and − areas of each node's influence line, `A± = lanePos / 0.64, laneNeg / 0.64` of the engine's own HL-93 rows (`PBD.contFE` nodes' `ll`, and the shear rows `sgBeam().VLLr / VLL` that `contFE` takes), linear between nodes as `contFE.at`; `MLLx` by the engine's `feM` rule on LL+IM + PL; the pier `M_PL,n = −w A−`; imported demands: nothing added, warning `WARN_EXT`.
  - `R.pl = { w, mode, L, x, Mmid, Vsup, Mhl, Vhl, [AMp, AMn, AVp, AVn], [pier: [{ side, A, M }]] }`. `steps()` (ids `ld.pl.w`, `.M`, `.V`, `.Mn<i>`, `.MLLPL`, `.VLLPL`), `note()` (every step with M_LL / V_LL / f_LL / M_u / V_u in its equation says "LL+IM here includes the pedestrian live load (§ld.pl.MLLPL, Loads & LLDF tab)"), `VplAt()`.
- **`engine/design.js`** `one()` (anchor `if (q && q.DC1 != null) o.loads =`): after it, `if (q && q.PL > 0) o.pl = { w: q.PL };`. `loads.wDW` takes `q.DW` (now DW + UT when a UT row exists).
- **`engine/holddown.js`** (anchor `const compute = inp =>`): before `const compute = inp => { const R = compute1(inp); return … PSBRatingAlong.apply(inp, R) : R; };`; after: that line as `compute2`, and `const compute = inp => (window.PSBPL && inp && inp.pl ? window.PSBPL.run(inp, compute2) : compute2(inp));`.
- **`engine/worked.js`** `loads()`: `if (R.pl && window.PSBPL) window.PSBPL.steps(add, inp, R, { n, g, par });` before `return K.done();`; `analysis()` returns `PSBPL.note(K.done(), R)`. **`engine/worked-stress.js`** (losses, stresses), **`engine/worked-strength.js`** (flexure, shear), **`engine/worked-hdr.js`** (rating): `return window.PSBPL ? window.PSBPL.note(K.done(), R) : K.done();`. `worked-strength.js shear()`: `vll = R.VLL * (L - xm) / L + PSBPL.VplAt(R, x)`; `flexure()` step `pier.MLL`: with a pedestrian load `−DF_M M_LL,lane + M_PL,n`.
- **`engine/model.js`**: header only (the optional fields).
- **`ui/bridgedl.js`**: the input "Pedestrian live load PL" (psf, `xs.dl.ped`, blank or 0 = none) under "Sidewalks and median", with a note (`#plOff`: a sidewalk and no pedestrian load; `#plOn`: the load of each sidewalk); category "Utility (DW)" in the added line loads; the note "Not offered …" rewritten (before: "Not offered (no engine input): pedestrian live load, utilities on the noncomposite section with DW factors (UT), the future utility allowance (UF)."; after: utilities are DW on the composite section, the pedestrian load is entered with the sidewalks, only UF not offered); the per-line table's DW row = the DW the design takes and a PL row; `lineTable()`: the pedestrian line loads, UT, DW + UT and PL rows with § links.
- **`ui/loads.js`**: topic `pl` (steps `ld.pl.*`); card "Pedestrian live load (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.1.6)" (`pedCard`, `#card-pl`): w_PL, M_PL, V_PL, the pier value, LL+IM + PL, each with its §. **`index.html`**: script `engine/pl.js`; the note `#plTabNote` on the Analysis, Losses, Stresses, Flexure, Shear and Rating tabs with the § to `ld.pl.MLLPL`. The Report's loads section shows the card and the steps (it is built from the tab).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- New optional fields inside `psb2.project` v1 (`xs.dl`): `ped` (psf) and `extra[i].cat = 'UT'`. Absent in every project saved before: no pedestrian load, no utility row, `inputs.pl` absent, the engine's own `computeAll` runs: results bit-identical (test below). No key or format changed; no migration needed. A new project has no `ped` (off).
### Governing provisions (CLAUDE.md §4): expressions added (before: none)
- AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) **Art. 3.6.1.6** (paraphrased: a pedestrian load of 0.075 ksf on sidewalks wider than 2.0 ft, considered together with the vehicular design live load); **Art. 3.6.2.1** (the dynamic load allowance is for the vehicles: none on PL); **Table 3.4.1-1** (PL takes γ_LL: Strength I 1.75, Service I 1.00, Service III γ_LL = `opt.gLLs3`, 0.8 by default); Art. 3.6.1.4.1 (fatigue: the fatigue truck only) and 2.5.2.6.2 (live-load deflection: vehicular load): PL in neither. Utilities: **Art. 3.5.1** (DW = wearing surfaces and utilities), Table 3.4.1-2 (γ_DW).
- Load: `w = PL / 1000 × b_walk` per sidewalk, `b_walk = sidewalk width − the deck edge's traffic face` (the barrier width or the curb / railing face), at the middle of the walkable width: the steel app's `dead()` (its `a.ped`), unchanged. Only sidewalks wider than 2.0 ft (PL-A-D2).
- Distribution to the girder lines: the steel app's `dead()` for category PL: method 'massdot' the pile-cap method `P/N_b + max(0, P e c_i / Σc²)` (MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.3); 'aashto' `P / N_b` (4.6.2.2.1, equally to all beams); 'ridot' the two adjacent beams by the lever rule.
- Force effects: simple span `M_PL(x) = w_PL x (L − x)/2`, `V_PL(x_m) = w_PL (L − x_m)²/(2L)`; continuous unit `M_PL± = w_PL A_M±`, `V_PL± = w_PL A_V±` (influence-line areas of the engine's FE unit), pier `M_PL,n = −w_PL A_M−`.
- Combinations (the engine's own expressions, with M_LL → M_LL+IM + M_PL and V_LL → V_LL+IM + V_PL): Strength I `M_u = η[1.25(M_g + M_DC1 + M_DC2) + 1.50 M_DW + 1.75 m (M_LL+IM + M_PL) + M_r]`, `V_u` alike; Service I `+ m (M_LL+IM + M_PL)/S`; Service III `γ_LL m (M_LL+IM + M_PL)/S_bc`; the pier negative moment and the positive moment connection; the load rating `RF = (C − γ_DC DC − γ_DW DW)/(γ_LL (LL+IM + PL))` (as the Steel Bridge app rates). Unchanged: R.MLL, R.VLL (HL-93 only), the live-load deflection, the fatigue check, the deck design, the rating vehicles entered by the user.
- Utility (UT) row: `w_DW,line = w_DW (wearing surface, overlays) + w_UT (the line's share)`; before: the category did not exist (a utility could be entered as a DW or DC2 line load).
### Check case (hand; made-up bridge: a new project, one 120 ft simple span, 5 girders at 9 ft, overhangs 3 ft, barriers 1.5 ft wide, BT-72 defaults, with a 6 ft left sidewalk 9 in thick; PL 75 psf)

- G2 (interior, the girder shown), 'aashto': w_PL = 0.0675 klf; M_PL = 0.0675 × 120²/8 = **121.5 kip-ft**; V_PL at the support = 0.0675 × 120/2 = **4.05 kip**.
  - M_LL at midspan: before 2626.6 kip-ft (HL-93 + IM × DF_M); after 2626.6 + 121.5 = **2748.1 kip-ft**.
  - Strength I M_u at midspan: before **9940.5 kip-ft**; after 9940.5 + 1.75 × 121.5 = 9940.5 + 212.6 = **10153.1 kip-ft** (η = 1, m = 1).
  - Service III bottom stress at midspan (S_bc = 20230.6 in³): before **+0.1012 ksi**; Δ = −0.8 × 121.5 × 12/20230.6 = −0.0577 ksi; after **+0.0436 ksi** (compression +).
  - Shear at the critical section: ΔV_u = 1.75 × w_PL (L − x)²/(2L) (test). Shear ratio 0.6992 → 0.7156; interface shear 0.4431 → 0.4515.
  - Unchanged: R.MLL, R.VLL, Δ_LL, the fatigue moment and stress range, the fatigue permanent stress, w_DC2, w_DW, f_pe.
- Continuous (the same bridge as 2 × 100 ft made continuous, G2): pier influence-line area A− = −1250 ft² (closed form 2 × L²/16; FE within 0.5 %), M_PL,n = 0.0675 × 1250 = 84.4 kip-ft added to the pier M_LL; midspan A+ = 937.5 ft² (0.09375 L²), M_PL = 63.3 kip-ft.

### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- **PL-A-D1 (how PL enters the frozen engine).** A girder with a pedestrian load runs a run-time copy of `computeAll` with 7 marked edits (above), because the engine has no input for it and its live-load functions are local. Proven identical to the engine with w_PL = 0 (658 cases); the anchors are asserted. Alternative: put the pedestrian load into the engine itself (unfreeze `pbd-compute.js` in a PR of its own).
- **PL-A-D2 (2.0 ft).** PL is applied to a sidewalk whose entered width (deck edge to curb face) is wider than 2.0 ft (3.6.1.6), on its walkable width. The Steel Bridge app applies it to any walkable width > 0 (no 2.0 ft test). The test is on the entered width, not the walkable width (the larger measure: PL applied more often).
- **PL-A-D3 (which girders).** PL goes to the girders by the project's dead-load distribution method, exactly as the Steel Bridge app (MassDOT pile-cap; AASHTO equally to all beams; RIDOT the two adjacent beams). With "equally" the exterior girder under the sidewalk gets 1/N_b of it; choose the method (or check the exterior girder by the lever rule) where that is not acceptable.
- **PL-A-D4 (vehicles with PL).** The HL-93 distribution factors are not reduced for the lanes the sidewalk displaces, and the multiple presence factors are unchanged (pedestrians not counted as a loaded lane, 3.6.1.1.2): full HL-93 × DF plus PL (conservative; as the Steel Bridge app).
- **PL-A-D5 (owner multiplier m).** The engine multiplies its whole live-load term by m (RIDOT 1.2), so m also multiplies PL here (conservative). The Steel Bridge app keeps m off PL (GD45, engineer 2026-10-15).
- **PL-A-D6 (rating).** The HL-93 design-load rating takes LL+IM + PL in its denominator, as the Steel Bridge app rates (its `pedestrianInLL`). MBE lets the pedestrian load be left out of a rating unless significant pedestrian loading is expected with the vehicles: to confirm. The user-entered rating vehicles are unchanged (their entered factored effects).
- **PL-A-D7 (shear envelope).** On a simple span the PL shear at a section is the exact partial loading w (L − x_m)²/(2L) (the Steel Bridge app's influence-line areas); the engine's own lane load follows its simplified envelope V_sup (L − x_m)/L.
- **PL-A-D8 (utilities).** A utility row (UT) is DW (3.5.1) on the composite section (on the continuous unit when made continuous), with γ_DW. The Steel Bridge app puts UT on the noncomposite section with DW factors (MassDOT 3.5.5.4) and has a future utility allowance UF (γ 1.25 / 0, 3.5.5.2): the moved engine has no noncomposite load with γ_DW, so UF is not offered and a utility hung before the deck is cast is entered as a DC1 line load (bare girder, γ_DC 1.25).
- **PL-A-D9 (default).** A new project has no pedestrian load until 75 psf is entered (the card says so when a sidewalk is entered). "Entered per girder type" mode has no pedestrian input.
### Open items
- Imported demands (MIDAS file / custom table): PL is not added (warning; include it in the imported live load).
- Hand-offs: the superstructure reactions sent to Substructure Loading are the engine's HL-93 per lane; the pedestrian reaction is not sent (Substructure Loading has its own sidewalk load input).
- The live-load deflection limit with pedestrians (2.5.2.6.2: span/1000) is not switched by the sidewalk (the owner rule's denominator, as before).
### Other copies
- `dead()` in `engine/bridge-dl.js` is the verbatim copy of the Steel Bridge app's (unchanged; its PL branch was already there, called with ped 0 until now). The old app (frozen) has no pedestrian load.

## 2026-11-23 — AP-B: line-girder applicability check and the LLDF ranges of applicability for every section family (engine/applicability.js; Loads & LLDF tab, check summary, Summary, Report) (VERDICT CHANGE for out-of-range designs, §4)
PR #1666: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1666 (claude/ps-lldf-applicability). How verified: `node tests/check-syntax.mjs` all pass; `node tests/engine/run.mjs psbridge tex` 57 files, 534 passed, 0 failed; harness B (24 designs) 61,234 shown values and 10,616 step values, 0 differences; smokes ps-bridge-applic (5), -pl (7), -skeleton (273), -tables (5), -figures (225), -types (106), -display (8), 0 failed.
### Request
- Engineer, 2026-11-23: close the gaps against the Steel Bridge app. Gap B: this app flagged the range of applicability only for box beams and slabs (PS-35, a warning). Mirror the Steel Bridge app's check SA4 (apps/steel-bridge/engine/analysis.js `applicability()`, engine/lldf.js `ranges()`; engineer-approved there 2026-11-21: a COMPUTED distribution factor outside its range is a FAIL that counts in the verdict; an ENTERED factor is not flagged). Engineer correction: Art. 4.6.3.3.2's skew index I_S is for grid / plate analyses of steel bridges, not a line-girder limit and not for concrete: omitted.
### What changed
- The moved engine (`engine/pbd-*.js`) is **not changed**. No distribution factor and no other computed value changes.
- **`engine/applicability.js`** (new, `window.PSBApplic`): `RANGE = { S: [3.5, 16.0], ts: [4.5, 12.0], L: [20, 240], Nb: [4, ∞], Kg: [10000, 7000000], de: [−1.0, 5.5], th: [0, 60] }`; `of(inp, R)` tests the values the factors were computed with; `apply(inp, R)` sets `R.ap` and, only when an item fails, pushes the check `{ n: 'LLDF range of applicability (4.6.2.2)', v: number of items outside, lim: 0, r: the largest exceedance ratio, u: 'items outside', pass: false }` to `R.checks` and the warning text to `R.warns`; `steps()` (ids `ld.ap.<key>`, `ld.ap.r`); `exceed(x, lo, hi)` = x / hi above the range, lo / x below it (1 + the distance where the limit is ≤ 0).
  - I-girders / bulb tees (type k): S = `inputs.S`, t_s = `inputs.ts`, L, N_b = `inputs.nGirders`, K_g = `R.df.Kg`, d_e = `inputs.loads.de` (exterior), θ = `inputs.loads.skew` (before the engine's cap at 60°).
  - NEXT (types i / j acting as a unit, the engine's equations): S = the beam width `R.df.Sf`; with no topping t_s = the integral top flange `g.next.ft` and no K_g item (the engine omits the K_g term); no d_e (the engine has no exterior NEXT factor).
  - Box beams and deck slabs (types f / g, `R.df.fg` of engine/lldf-fg.js, its `LIM`): b, L, N_b, d_e ≤ 2.0 ft (exterior), θ ≤ 60°, d (with a shear skew correction): FAIL outside; I and J: a NOTE (4.6.2.2.3a alternative already applied, PS-35). The PS-35 warning of lldf-fg.js is unchanged.
  - A MassDOT NEDBT with no topping (PS-42, engineer decision 2026-11-14: keeps the engine's type (k) factors, flagged): its t_s = 0 item is a WARNING, not a FAIL. Any other I-girder with t_s outside: FAIL.
  - Other items (no FAIL): horizontal curvature (straight girders only: OK); θ > 20°: a NOTE of what a line-girder analysis does not compute. Entered distribution factors (`loads.dfAuto` false): nothing tested.
- **`engine/holddown.js`** (anchor `const compute = inp =>`): before `const compute = inp => (window.PSBPL && inp && inp.pl ? window.PSBPL.run(inp, compute2) : compute2(inp));`; after: that line as `compute3`, and `const compute = inp => { const R = compute3(inp); return window.PSBApplic ? window.PSBApplic.apply(inp, R) : R; };`.
- **`engine/worked.js`** `loads()`: `if (R.ap && window.PSBApplic) window.PSBApplic.steps(add, inp, R, { n, g, par });`.
- **`ui/dash.js`** `GROUPS`: new group `{ id: 'ap', name: 'LLDF applicability', tab: 'lds', checks: [['LLDF range of applicability (4.6.2.2)', 'ld.ap.r']] }` (a chip only when the check exists, i.e. on a FAIL; the Summary, the Report §1 and Auto design read the same groups).
- **`ui/loads.js`**: the banner card first on the tab (`apCard`, `#card-ap`, `#apBanner[data-aplevel]`, table `#apTbl`: item, value with its §, range, table, result); topic `ap` (steps `ld.ap.*`). **`index.html`**: script `engine/applicability.js`. The Report's loads section shows the banner and the steps (built from the tab).
### Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5)
- None: no key, field or format. New result fields only (`R.ap`, the check when failing).
### Governing provisions and what is new (CLAUDE.md §4)
- AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 4.6.2.2, the "Range of Applicability" columns (paraphrased): **Table 4.6.2.2.2b-1** (moment, interior; types a, e, k, and i, j acting as a unit): 3.5 ≤ S ≤ 16.0 ft, 4.5 ≤ t_s ≤ 12.0 in, 20 ≤ L ≤ 240 ft, N_b ≥ 4, 10,000 ≤ K_g ≤ 7,000,000 in⁴; **Table 4.6.2.2.3a-1** (shear, interior): the same S, L, t_s, N_b; **Tables 4.6.2.2.2d-1, 4.6.2.2.3b-1** (exterior): −1.0 ≤ d_e ≤ 5.5 ft; **Tables 4.6.2.2.2e-1, 4.6.2.2.3c-1** (skew): up to 60° (the moment table takes θ = 60° above it); types f / g: the limits of engine/lldf-fg.js (PS-35).
- New checks: before, a type (k) or NEXT girder outside these ranges was computed with no flag, and a box / slab outside got a warning only. After: the check "LLDF range of applicability (4.6.2.2)" FAILS and counts in the check summary, the Summary verdict, the Report §1 and Auto design (a design outside the ranges cannot pass until the factors are entered or the layout changed). Inside the ranges: no check is added, every ratio and count is as before.
### Check cases (made-up bridge: a new project, one 120 ft span, 5 BT-72 at 9 ft, t_s = 8 in, overhangs 3 ft, barriers 1.5 ft, no skew)
- In range: S = 9 (3.5 to 16), t_s = 8 (4.5 to 12), L = 120 (20 to 240), N_b = 5 (≥ 4), K_g inside 10,000 to 7,000,000, θ = 0; exterior G1 d_e = 3 − 1.5 = 1.5 ft (−1.0 to 5.5): level OK, no check; the result identical to before.
- Out of range (each a FAIL, ratio = value / limit): bays 17 ft: S = 17 > 16, r = 17/16 = **1.0625**; 3 girders: N_b = 3 < 4, r = 4/3 = **1.3333**; skews 65°: θ = 65 > 60, r = 65/60 = **1.0833** (the engine computes the factors with θ = 60°); overhang 8 ft on G1: d_e = 6.5 > 5.5, r = 6.5/5.5 = **1.1818**; t_s = 4 in: r = 4.5/4 = **1.125**. S = 17 with θ = 70°: 2 items, r = 70/60. The distribution factors are the same with and without the check (it changes no value).
- Entered factors with S = 17 ft and θ = 65°: not flagged, no check. Skews 35°: a NOTE, no check.
### Tests
- `tests/engine/psbridge-applic.test.mjs` (new, 6 tests): 144 girder type × line results of the 19 harness B designs and a new project are inside their ranges and identical with and without engine/applicability.js (Object.is on every number; only `R.ap` is new, 0 checks added); the hand cases above; entered factors; the families (NEXT, box N_b = 4, I / J note, PS-42 warning, another I-girder with t_s = 0 FAIL); the steps.
- `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-applic.mjs` (new, 5 checks): the banner in range and with S = 17 ft, the chip (1.063 FAIL) and its link, the verdict, the Summary and the Report, entered factors, the keys, 0 console errors.
### Decisions (pending engineer review)
- **AP-B-D1.** The check exists only when it fails (no PASS chip, so every count of an in-range project is as before); the banner on the Loads & LLDF tab shows the OK state. Alternative: always list it (a PASS more in every count).
- **AP-B-D2.** PS-42 kept: a NEDBT with no topping is a WARNING, not a FAIL (its t_s = 0 is far outside 4.5 to 12 in). By the Steel rule it would be a FAIL: to confirm.
- **AP-B-D3.** Box beams / slabs outside b, L, N_b, d_e, θ, d now FAIL (before: the PS-35 warning only); I and J stay a note (4.6.2.2.3a).
- **AP-B-D4.** N_b = 3 is a FAIL (the tables' "lesser of the equation and the lever rule" for three beams is not computed by the engine); N_b < 4 is not also listed as a separate warning as the Steel Bridge app does.
- **AP-B-D5.** With imported demands the computed factor is used for the fatigue check only; it is still tested (FAIL outside).
- **AP-B-D6.** The ratio shown is value / limit of the worst item (so a FAIL always shows > 1.0); it is not a demand / capacity ratio.
- **AP-B-D7.** NEXT with no topping: t_s is tested on the integral top flange; NEXT S is the beam width (the engine's S). The engine has no exterior NEXT factor, so no d_e item.
- **AP-B-D8 (not done, option C of the request).** The Steel Bridge app's LLDF options "exterior not less than interior" and "shear skew correction on exterior girders only" are not added: the engine's distFactors result is re-derived by engine/rigid.js and worked step by step on the Loads & LLDF tab, so the options need a wrapper ordered after the rigid-section one and new worked steps (not a small change). Today: the exterior factor is not raised to the interior one; the shear skew correction is on every girder.
### Other copies
- None. The Steel Bridge app has its own SA4 (not changed).

- **Decisions (pending engineer review):**
  1. The verdict has the Summary tab's three states (FAIL / REVIEW / PASS); there is no "PASS WITH NOTES" as in the steel report: the items not in the verdict are listed under it instead.

Bill of materials: strand length = the girder length (the slope of the draped strands and the strand past the ends are not added); steel at 490 pcf; mild steel as counts and areas, no weight (bar lengths are not inputs); deck concrete over the full deck width between ℄ bearings; a line with no girder type is left out and named.

## 2026-11-23 — UT-N: utilities on the noncomposite section (DW factors) and the future utility allowance (γ 1.25 / 0), as the Steel Bridge app (engine/ut.js, engine/bridge-dl.js, engine/rating-along.js; Cross-section tab, Loads & LLDF tab, Report) (CALCULATION CHANGE, §4)
PR #1669: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1669 (claude/ps-utilities-noncomposite)
### Request
- Engineer, 2026-11-23: add to Prestressed the two utility categories the Steel Bridge app has (apps/steel-bridge/engine/loads.js `CATS`: `UT: 'Utility (noncomposite, DW factors)'`, `UF: 'Future utility allowance (noncomposite, γ 1.25/0)'`), mirrored for a prestressed girder; the composite "Utility (DW)" of PL-A stays. **This supersedes decision PL-A-D8** of the PL-A entry above ("UF is not offered and a utility hung before the deck is cast is entered as a DC1 line load"): both categories are now offered.
- What the Steel Bridge app does (read first; its fixlog entry OWN16 in `fixlog/Steel Bridge Design.md`, decision GD42): `dead()` distributes UT / UF rows by the project's method (`rAuto`: RIDOT the two adjacent beams; MassDOT the pile-cap method; AASHTO equally; or the row's own distribution); `engine/analysis.js` puts both on the steel (noncomposite) section; `engine/flexure.js` (`envelopeStrI`, `gSet`): UT with γ_DW 1.50 / 0.65 by the sign of its moment, UF with γ_DC 1.25 or 0; Service: UT 1.00, UF 1.00 only where it adds (`svU`); `engine/rating.js`: UT with DW and UF with DC, each only where it adds (`adds`); the camber takes the existing utilities, not the future allowance. Its recorded basis: MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I 3.5.5.4 and 3.5.5.2; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-2. The categories are offered there for every owner, and so here.

### The route into the frozen engine, and why
1. Both loads are fed to the engine's existing input for a noncomposite line load, `loads.wNC` (as the DC1 line loads of PR 9). The engine then treats them exactly as DC1 everywhere. That is the whole of "UF present" (γ 1.25, Service 1.00, girder section), with no engine edit.
2. UT needs γ 1.50 where DC1 gets 1.25. A correction after the engine (the pattern of `rating-along.js apply`) is not exact here: the Strength I `M_u` and `V_u` are local expressions of `computeAll` that feed the MCFT shear iteration (ε_s, β, θ, V_c, V_s), the longitudinal tie, the interface shear and the minimum reinforcement, none of which can be redone outside. So the run-time copy of `computeAll` (the mechanism of `engine/pl.js`, PL-A-D1) is used, with 10 wrapped expressions. Each wrapper returns its argument unchanged without a load, so the copy with no load is the engine bit for bit (658 parity cases, tolerance 0; and on top of the pedestrian copy).
3. UF absent: a second run of the same chain without w_UF. The larger ratio of each check governs: a check whose ratio is larger with the allowance absent is added to `R.checks` as "UF absent: <check>".
