## 2026-11-25 — PR: claude/ps-ez-exact (PR #1720: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1720) (EZX) — the concrete tensile force of 5.9.2.3.1b summed exactly by parts instead of 240 strips (§4 calculation change; approved by the engineer 2026-11-25)
### Request (engineer, 2026-11-25: "Merge, then exact")
After PR #1714 (EZNI) showed the by-parts sum beside the engine's 240-strip value, make the exact by-parts sum the value the engine uses: the tension force at release, top and bottom (bonded release-tension steel), and the tension force in the girder top near an interior support.
### Where
- New `apps/ps-bridge/engine/reltension.js` (`window.PSBRelTension`): `parts(G, fTop, fBot)` (moved unchanged from `engine/worked-end.js` `tensionParts`, PR #1714) and `apply(inp, R)`.
- `apps/ps-bridge/engine/holddown.js`, anchor `const compute0 = inp =>`: before: `apply(inp, window.PSBLldfFG ? window.PSBLldfFG.run(inp, engine) : engine(inp))`; after: `apply(inp, relT(inp, window.PSBLldfFG ? window.PSBLldfFG.run(inp, engine) : engine(inp)))` with `relT = (inp, R) => (window.PSBRelTension ? window.PSBRelTension.apply(inp, R) : R)`: on each engine result, before the PS-10 check and before the stages that run the chain more than once (UT-N `engine/ut.js` and PL-A `engine/pl.js` compare their present / absent states on the same values).
- `apps/ps-bridge/index.html`: `'engine/reltension.js'` loaded before `'engine/holddown.js'`.
- The frozen `engine/pbd-section.js` `releaseTensionForce` and `engine/pbd-compute.js` (`relSteel`, `cont.svc`) are unchanged byte for byte; the exact value replaces the strip value in R after `computeAll`, in the app's engine call (`PSBHoldDown.compute`). The frozen optimizer `pbd-optimize.js` (it calls `computeAll` directly) still uses the strip sum.
- `engine/worked-end.js`: `tensionParts` now calls `PSBRelTension.parts`; the T step's note "Sum of the parts X kip; the result used is the engine's value Y kip (… 240 horizontal strips …)" is replaced by "The sum of the parts is the engine's value (EZX …). Gross outline: voids ignored, which over-states T.", and the step's shown value is the parts' sum (pair-tested = the engine to 1e-9). `ui/endzone.js` `partsTbl`: the rows "Sum ΣF_i" and "T used (the engine's, 240 strips)" replaced by one row "T = ΣF_i" (the engine's value, §).
### Before / After (expressions)
- Before (`pbd-section.js` `releaseTensionForce`, unchanged and still in R as `R.relT.strip`): `T = Σ_{i=1..240} max(0, −f(y_i)) · b(y_i) · h/240`, y_i = (i − ½)h/240, f(y) = f_bot + (f_top − f_bot) y/h, b(y) = `sectionWidthAt`.
- After (`reltension.js` `parts`): `c = h|f_t| / (|f_t| + |f_c|)` (c = h when both fibres are in tension); the outline cut at its corners and at c into trapezoids; per part `A = (b_a + b_b)/2 · t`, `ȳ = d_a + t(b_a + 2b_b)/(3(b_a + b_b))`, `f = |f_t|(1 − ȳ/c)` (full depth: `|f_t| + (|f_o| − |f_t|) ȳ/h`), `F = A f`; `T = ΣF`. Then, as the engine: `T = T_top if T_top ≥ T_bot else T_bot`, `A_s,req = T / f_s`, `D/C = A_s,req / A_s,prov` (99 with none), PASS at D/C ≤ 1.0001; near an interior support `A_s,req = T / f_s` and its check where the engine has it.
### Governing provision
AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 5.9.2.3.1b, Table 5.9.2.3.1b-1 (bonded reinforcement for the tensile force in the concrete of an uncracked section, at f_s = 0.5 f_y ≤ 30 ksi); near an interior support Art. 5.12.3.3.5 with the same table. Unchanged; only the summation of that force changes.
### Check case (by hand)
MassDOT NEDBT 48 (h = 48 in, top flange 60 × 8 in), f_top = −0.631 ksi, f_bot = 4.696 ksi: c = 48(0.631)/5.327 = 5.686 in; A = 60 × 5.686 = 341.15 in²; ȳ = 2.843 in; f = 0.631(1 − 2.843/5.686) = 0.3155 ksi; T = 341.15 × 0.3155 = 107.63 kip. Before (240 strips): 107.61 kip; after: 107.63 kip. A_s,req = T/30: 3.587 → 3.588 in².
Reproducible project (the smoke test): MassDOT NEDBT 48, 12 draped strands at y_end = 12 in, third row 12 strands, A_s,prov 0.62 in²: f_top = −0.626, f_bot = 4.732 ksi at x = 3.00 ft; T_top 105.38 kip both (to 0.01), D/C 5.665 both.
### Changes at displayed precision (T 0.1 kip, A_s,req 0.01 in², D/C 0.001; before → after)
See the PR description (58 designs + the library sweep of 92 girder types). No verdict changes; no check added or removed; the pier T values change by ≤ 0.005 kip (none at 0.1 kip).
### How verified
Node, the branch before vs after on 58 designs (19 tab designs, 10 girder variants, each with the bonded steel off and on) and 184 library designs: every field of R other than `relSteel`, `cont.svc.Ttop / AsTop`, the two checks and the new `R.relT` identical. `tests/engine/psbridge-ez-noint.test.mjs` (T = the parts to 1e-9; the strip value kept in R.relT.strip within 0.05 kip + 0.1 %; the 200,000-strip check; the hand check; R.relSteel and the check carry the exact value); `tests/engine/psbridge-tabs.test.mjs` (the PS-10 test compares with computeAll + PSBRelTension.apply); the psbridge tests, check-syntax, the full engine suite, `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-ez-noint.mjs`.
### Saved data
None (no key, no format; R.relT is a computed result only).
### Other copies
Engine test file lists: `'reltension'` added next to `'holddown'` in every test that loads it (61 files), so the tests run the app's chain.
Merge of main with PR #1725 (2026-11-26): its new `tests/engine/psbridge-report-governing.test.mjs` loads `holddown` and `worked-end` without `reltension`, so the End zone steps threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parts')" in that test only (the app loads `engine/reltension.js` in index.html). `'reltension'` added after `'lldf-fg'` in its list, as in the other 61 files; RG 1–6 pass. Before: `['sections', 'model', 'rigid', 'lldf-fg', 'holddown', 'pierblock', …]`; after: `['sections', 'model', 'rigid', 'lldf-fg', 'reltension', 'holddown', 'pierblock', …]`. No computed result of the app changes.
### Decisions
- EZX-a (approved by the engineer 2026-11-25): the exact sum applies to every engine result inside the app's engine call (`holddown.js` `compute0`), after `computeAll`; the frozen engine keeps its strip function, and its strip values stay in `R.relT.strip`.
- EZX-b (approved by the engineer 2026-11-25): the frozen optimizer (`pbd-optimize.js`) stays on the strip sum; the app does not call it.
- The change table of PR #1720 (no verdict changes; last-digit changes only) approved by the engineer 2026-11-25 with the merge.
### Open items
- EZNI-2 (NEXT: the gap between the stems counted as concrete) is not touched here.
- The frozen optimizer (pbd-optimize.js `optimizeStrands`, `sweepDesign`) still uses the strip sum; the app's Compare tab uses the app's engine call (engine/compare.js).

## 2026-11-25 — PR: claude/ps-ez-next-stems (PR #1721: https://github.com/mlococo88/All-Structural/pull/1721) (EZN) — NEXT beams: the concrete tensile force of 5.9.2.3.1b counts the two stems only, not the gap between them (§4 calculation change; approved by the engineer 2026-11-25)
### Request (engineer, 2026-11-25: "Fix NEXT stems only")
EZNI open item 2: for a NEXT beam below the flange the engine's width (`sectionWidthAt`, the outermost edge of the outline at y) counts the gap between the two stems as concrete (NEXT 36F: 73 in instead of 2 × 13 = 26 in), over-stating the tension force there. NEXT shapes only; box beams and voided slabs keep their voids-ignored (conservative) basis.
### Where
- `apps/ps-bridge/engine/reltension.js` (EZX): new `chordWidth(G, y)` (the length of the horizontal line at y inside the closed outline `halfPolygon(G)`, × 2) and `widthAt(G, y) = G.isNext ? chordWidth(G, y) : sectionWidthAt(G, y)`; `parts()` reads `widthAt` instead of `sectionWidthAt`; the NEXT part below the flange is named "stems (the two stems; the gap between them not counted)" (was "stems (outline to the outer stem faces, as the engine)").
- NEXT = `G.isNext`: the library's NEXT 24F–36F and MassDOT's NEXT F (24–36) and D (28–40) (sections.js gives both the engine's NEXT object; MassDOT's outline has tapered stems and fillets, read as drawn).
- Frozen `engine/pbd-*.js` unchanged byte for byte. `sectionWidthAt` is read only by the engine's `releaseTensionForce` (release T top / bottom and the pier T, now replaced in R by reltension.js); `halfPolygon` (the outline) also feeds the drawings, the strand / input checks and the 3D view, which are not changed. Section properties (A, I, y_b) come from the shape tables, not from the outline width.
### Before / After
- Before (EZX): width b(y) = `sectionWidthAt(G, y)` = 2 × (the largest x of the half outline at y). NEXT below the flange: 2 × (outer stem face) = 2(stemCC/2 + B/2) (NEXT 36F: 2(30 + 6.5) = 73 in).
- After: NEXT: b(y) = 2 × Σ(x_out − x_in) over the outline's crossings at y = the two stems (NEXT 36F: 2 × 13 = 26 in); every other shape as before. The sum T = Σ A_i f_i (EZX) is otherwise unchanged.
### Governing provision
AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 5.9.2.3.1b, Table 5.9.2.3.1b-1 (the tensile force in the concrete computed on the uncracked section, carried by bonded reinforcement at 0.5 f_y ≤ 30 ksi); near an interior support Art. 5.12.3.3.5 with the same table. Unchanged; the section's concrete width is corrected for NEXT.
### Check case (by hand): NEXT 36F, bottom tension at midspan (default project with this girder, 10 strands at y = 2 in, no draped strands)
f_top = 2.158 ksi, f_bot = −2.542 ksi at x = 60 ft. c = 36(2.542)/(2.542 + 2.158) = 19.474 in (below the 28 in stems' top: one part, the stems).
- Before: b = 73 in; A = 73 × 19.474 = 1421.6 in²; ȳ = 9.737 in; f = 2.542(1 − 9.737/19.474) = 1.2712 ksi; T = 1421.6 × 1.2712 = 1807.1 kip; A_s,req = 1807.1/30 = 60.24 in².
- After: b = 26 in; A = 26 × 19.474 = 506.32 in²; same ȳ and f; T = 506.32 × 1.2712 = 643.6 kip; A_s,req = 643.6/30 = 21.45 in².
### Changes at displayed precision
See the PR description: every NEXT design tried (library and MassDOT NEXT F and D, simple and 2 × 80 ft continuous, the tab design NEXT 36F with a topping). With A_s,prov = 0.62 in² no verdict changes (D/C stays above 1); a verdict can change NG → OK where A_s,prov lies between the new and old A_s,req (test: NEXT 36F with 25 in²).
### How verified
`tests/engine/psbridge-ez-next-stems.test.mjs` (the widths; NEXT only; the hand check; other shapes unchanged; the NG → OK case); `tests/engine/psbridge-ez-noint.test.mjs` (the fine strip check on `widthAt`); before / after in Node: only R.relSteel, R.cont.svc.Ttop / AsTop, their checks and R.relT differ, on NEXT designs only; psbridge tests, check-syntax, the full engine suite, `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-ez-noint.mjs`.
### Decisions
- EZN-a (approved by the engineer 2026-11-25): "NEXT" is `G.isNext` (the library NEXT and MassDOT NEXT F and D); the MassDOT stems are read from the drawn outline (tapered, with fillets and the 0.75 in bottom chamfers).
- The change table of PR #1721 (the NEXT reductions; a NEXT verdict can change NG → OK) approved by the engineer 2026-11-25 with the merge.
### Saved data
None.

## 2026-11-28 — PR: claude/ps-ad-refine (PSAD-A) — Auto design: Refine mode (item 4) and a target ratio (item 7)   [§4: the auto design's search and pass rule; no engine formula, factor, unit or reference changed; defaults leave every result unchanged]
- **Request (engineer's choice of 2026-11-28, items 4 and 7 of the PS Auto design improvements):** a Refine mode that keeps the current section and searches the smallest change from the entered design (also reducing an over-designed pattern); a target ratio: a candidate passes only if every check's ratio is ≤ the target.
- **Where:** `apps/ps-bridge/engine/autodesign.js`: `DEF` (+ `mode: 'new'`, `maxRatio: 1.00`), new `RULE`, `TOL`, `over()`; `settings()` (anchor `const mr = num(a.maxRatio, DEF.maxRatio);`); `evalCand()` (anchor `if (!c.pass || over(c, tgt))`, + `govT`); new `distance()`, `cmpDist()`, `modRows()`, `refine()` (generator, before `hdOf`); `run()` (anchor `if (ref) {   // Refine: the current section`; `ctx.o`). `ui/autodesign.js`: the Mode select and Target ratio field on the input tab (`data-ad="mode"`, `data-ad="maxRatio"`), `onChange` (`id === 'mode'`), the output tab's run note (mode, target), the governing column (`govTxt(g, ev, o)`: `; target 0.95: <check> r (G#)`), Refine's change column (`distTxt`), two assumption lines. `ui/settings.js`: Auto design › Search: `mode` and `maxRatio` (borderline: they stay on the input tab too). `report/builders.js` `adSub`: a Mode row (Refine only) and a Target ratio row (target < 1 only).
- **Before / after (code):**
  - Pass of a candidate. Before: `if (!c.pass) { out.pass = false; … }`. After: `if (!c.pass || over(c, tgt)) { … }` with `over = (c, t) => t < 1 && !RULE.test(c.n) && !(c.r <= t + 1e-4)`, `tgt = ctx.o.maxRatio` (1 when absent). At the default target 1.00 `over` is false for every check: the pass is the engine's `c.pass` (r ≤ 1.0001) exactly as before.
  - RULE (the target does not apply; the check must pass): `/^(Confinement steel|LLDF range of applicability|Hold-down force|Girder f′c|Release strength f′ci|Girder age at continuity|Debonded strands)/`.
  - Mode. Before: one search (sections of the family). After: `settings.mode === 'refine'` → the current section only and `refine()` per girder type; `'new'` (default, and any other value) → the code before, unchanged.
- **Refine (refine()):** 1. the entered design itself; 2. N = N0, then N0 − 2, N0 − 4, … (stops at the first N with no passing design once one passed, when every trial failed only on GROW checks, or on the live-load deflection), and only when nothing passes at N0: N0 + 2, … to the first that passes; 3. at each N: n_h by |Δn_h| (then the fewer); the entered rows changed by pairs (`modRows`: off the highest row; onto the lowest row they fit, then a new grid row above); the drape: per frac (nearest the entered frac first) the passing y_end range by bisection as the new-design search, then the y_end in it nearest the entered one (with the hold-down force bisection when the nearest fails it); judged at the highest f′c / f′ci; 4. at that pattern the f′c nearest the entered (with its highest f′ci), then the f′ci nearest the entered, by bisection on the 0.5 ksi grids. Listed: the passing designs ranked by distance, the first topN − 1, and the passing design with the fewest strands.
- **Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5):** two new optional fields of `P.autodesign`: `mode` ('refine'; absent = 'new') and `maxRatio` (number; absent = 1.00). Old projects open unchanged and run as before. No browser key added.
- **Governing provision:** none changed. The target ratio is a margin on the engine's own checks (each worked on its tab: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. as cited there); no check, formula or factor is changed.
- **Check case (target 0.90; tab case "AASHTO Type IV exterior G1, 85 ft, entered DF", section and f′c / f′ci locked (8.5 / 6.8 ksi), hold-down points 0.40 / 0.45 L):**
  - Target 1.00 (as before): 22 strands, 18 straight (12 at y = 2, 6 at y = 4 in), 4 draped, y_end 41 in, y_mid 7 in, frac 0.45: Flexure M_u / φM_n = 5246.36 / 5927.18 = 0.885 (x = 41.08 ft), Shear V_u / φV_n = 181.45 / 199.59 = 0.909 (x = 21.26 ft), Release tens. steel 0.959.
  - Target 0.90: the same 22 strands with frac 0.40, y_end 43 in (frac 0.45 fails Shear 0.909 > 0.90; at 0.40 y_end 41 fails release tension steel): Shear 181.45 / 205.11 = 0.885, Flexure 0.885 (governing against the target, G1), Confinement 6.00 / 6.00 = 1.000 (a rule of fact: must pass only).
  - Hand check of the governing check (Flexure, Strength I, from the Flexure tab's steps): M_u = 5246.36 k-ft ≤ 0.90 × φM_n = 0.90 × 5927.18 = 5334.46 k-ft → ratio 5246.36 / 5927.18 = 0.8851 ≤ 0.90 ✓.
- **Check case (Refine, the new project: PCI BT-72, 120 ft, 40 strands, 12 draped at y_end 60 / frac 0.40, f′c 8.5 / f′ci 6.8; it fails the Hold-down force (PS-10) 1.276):** Refine keeps 40 strands and 12 draped, the drape nearest the entered one that passes: y_end 57 in, frac 0.44 (distance 0, 0, 3 in, 0.04, 0, 0); the hold-down force F_hd = 2 n_h f_pbt A_b sin α falls with the flatter slope (57 − 13)/(0.44 L) and passes; f′c / f′ci kept. Listed next: 38 strands (12 draped) and the fewest, 30 strands (12 draped, f′c 10.0 / 9.8 and 9.0 / 8.8 ksi for the exterior type).
- **How verified:** new `tests/engine/psbridge-autodesign-refine.test.mjs` (5 tests: the defaults, target 0.90 on every line, Refine over-designed and failing, the distance order); `psbridge-autodesign.test.mjs` unchanged and passing; the smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-autodesign.mjs` (+ step 4b); the hash of the Auto design result of 59 built-in and recorded designs, origin/main vs this branch at the default settings (see the PR).
- **Decisions (pending engineer review):**
  - PSAD-D1. Refine's distance: |ΔN|, then |Δn_h|, then the drape change (with draped strands entered: |Δy_end|, then |Δfrac|; none entered: the slope (y_end − y_mid)/frac, then |frac − 0.40|), then |Δf′c|, then |Δf′ci|, lexicographic.
  - PSAD-D2. Refine lists the passing designs nearest first (topN − 1 of them) and the passing design with the fewest strands, so an over-designed pattern is reduced; more strands than N0 are searched only when nothing passes at N0.
  - PSAD-D3. Refine changes the entered rows by pairs: removing from the highest row, adding to the lowest row that fits, then a new row on the row grid; top strands and entered debonding kept.
  - PSAD-D4. The target ratio applies to every check except the rules of fact (RULE above), including the hold-down force limit (a fabrication limit), which must pass; the engine's 1e-4 tolerance is kept; a target above 1.00 is taken as 1.00.


## 2026-11-28 — PR: claude/ps-ad-count (PSAD-B) — Auto design: the girder count N_b as a variable (item 1)   [§4: the auto design's search; no engine formula, factor, unit or reference changed; the default (Lock) leaves every result unchanged]
- **Request (engineer's choice of 2026-11-28, item 1):** the girder count as an Auto design variable (Auto / Lock / Range, as the Steel Bridge app), each count a full re-layout (equal spacing over the out-to-out width with the app's overhang rule, the LLDF by the app's own path, the girder types re-assigned by BR.renumber), N_b part of the objective (the total concrete of all girders), Apply as one Undo step.
- **Where:** `apps/ps-bridge/engine/autodesign.js`: `DEF.vars.nb = 'lock'`, `DEF.nbMin / nbMax / sLo / sHi`, `S_LO = 3.5`, `S_HI = 16.0`; `settings()` (vars.nb 'auto' | 'range' | 'lock'); new `nbLock()`, `counts()`, `applyLayout()`, `layoutFor()` (before `run`); `run()` (anchors `// PSAD-B: the girder counts searched`, `if (multi) {   // PSAD-B: every (count, section)`, `out.nb.pick`); `apply()` (anchor `// PSAD-B: a candidate at another girder count`). `ui/autodesign.js`: the variable row N_b (Lock / Auto / Range), N_b fewest / most (Range), spacing least / most; the output's N_b (S) column, the counts searched, the default count, the layout note before Apply, Apply refused for candidates of different counts. `ui/settings.js`: Auto design › Girder count (borderline: also on the input tab). `report/builders.js` `adSub`: a Girder count row (Auto / Range only).
- **The layout of a count n (applyLayout):** W_cc = Σ bays (the present exterior girder spacing), every bay S = W_cc / (n − 1), the overhangs ohL / ohR kept (the app's equal-spacing rule, EQSP: `PSBModel.equalSpacing`, the out-to-out width ohL + W_cc + ohR unchanged); `xs.Wcc = W_cc` in equal spacing mode; `PSBBridge.renumber(Q, nb0, snapshot)` (the page's rule on a count change, SB-14: the outer lines keep the exterior types, an inner line its type or the span's Interior type); the design girder within N_b; an entered b_eff (base or a type's override) back to the calculated width. Everything computed then comes from `PSBDesign.cellInputs` of that layout (S, N_b, position, overhang → the LLDF of Art. 4.6.2.2 by the engine, b_eff by 4.6.2.6.1, DC2 / DW by the bridge-level distribution).
- **Counts searched (counts):** Lock (default): the current count. Auto: the current count ± 1, at least 3 girders, with S within 3.5 … 16.0 ft (Table 4.6.2.2.2b-1, the range engine/applicability.js checks) narrowed by sLo / sHi when entered. Range: nbMin … nbMax. The current count only (with a note) for adjacent boxes and slabs and NEXT beams (their width sets the lines), entered distribution factors, entered live load, or a demand table.
- **Ranking:** with one count, as before (sections by A then h, or h then A). With several: every (count, section) in the order of A × N_b (the concrete of all the span's girders; W = w_sw (L + 2 e/12) N_b with w_sw ∝ A), then h, then the current count first, then the section order (objective depth: h first, then A × N_b); the first topN that pass every type of the span are listed; a candidate's weight W is the sum over every girder of the span. The default choice: the count with the least total concrete over all spans (each span's lightest candidate at it); Apply needs one count in every span.
- **Apply:** `applyLayout(P, n)` then each type's design (`setOvr`), in one `apply()` call: one change of the project, one Undo step (the page's `changed()`), the notice naming the layout change, the re-assigned lines and the b_eff reset.
- **Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5):** new optional `P.autodesign.vars.nb` ('auto' | 'range'; absent = Lock), `nbMin`, `nbMax`, `sLo`, `sHi`. Old projects open unchanged. No browser key added. Apply writes `xs.nb`, `xs.bays` (and `xs.Wcc` in equal spacing), `types[].lines`, possibly a new type (renumber's "Interior S<s>", as a count change on the Cross-section tab), `base.beffAuto` / `types[].ovr.beffAuto`: fields the input tabs already write.
- **Governing provision:** none changed. The LLDF of AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 4.6.2.2.2b / 4.6.2.2.3a (interior), 4.6.2.2.2d / 4.6.2.2.3b (exterior) are the engine's, recomputed for each layout.
- **Check case (the new project: PCI BT-72, 120 ft, 5 girders at 9.0 ft, overhangs 3.0 ft; N_b Auto, every other variable Auto):** counts 5, 4 (S = 36 / 3 = 12.00 ft), 6 (S = 36 / 5 = 7.20 ft). Candidates: #1 N_b = 4 PCI BT-72 (Interior on G2–G3: 40 strands, 6 draped, f′c 10.0 / f′ci 7.8; Exterior on G1, G4: 36 strands, 6 draped, 8.5 / 6.8), W = 396.3 kip; #2 N_b = 5 PCI BT-63, 460.5 kip; #3 N_b = 5 PCI BT-72, 495.4 kip. Default choice N_b = 4.
  - LLDF at S = 12.00 ft (engine, interior, two or more lanes): g_M = 0.075 + (S/9.5)^0.6 (S/L)^0.2 (K_g / 12 L t_s³)^0.1 = 0.075 + (1.2632)^0.6 (0.1000)^0.2 (2,352,359 / (12 × 120 × 8³))^0.1 = 0.075 + 1.1505 × 0.6310 × 1.1231 = 0.890 (at 9.0 ft: 0.719); g_V = 0.2 + S/12 − (S/35)² = 0.2 + 1.000 − 0.1176 = 1.082 (at 9.0 ft: 0.884).
  - Governing check of #1 (Interior, G2): Shear V_u / φV_n = 279.55 / 279.71 = 0.9994 at x = 30.01 ft (Shear tab, worked step); Exterior G1: Shear 242.12 / 244.28 = 0.991.
- **Run time:** the new project, every variable Auto: 6.4 s (N_b Lock, as before) → 7.9 s (N_b Auto, 3 counts; 1,199 engine runs): the (count, section) pairs are run lightest first and the run stops at topN candidates, so the counts add only the pairs lighter than the third candidate.
- **How verified:** new `tests/engine/psbridge-autodesign-count.test.mjs` (4 tests); `psbridge-autodesign*.test.mjs`; the smoke `tests/smoke/ps-bridge-autodesign.mjs` (+ step 4c); the Auto design hash of 59 built-in and recorded designs at the default settings, origin/main vs this branch (see the PR).
- **Decisions (pending engineer review; the defaults confirmed by the engineer 2026-11-28 to build as proposed):**
  - PSAD-D5. The overhangs and W_cc are kept, with equal spacing S = W_cc / (N_b − 1) (the app's EQSP rule); the spacing limits are the LLDF range 3.5 ≤ S ≤ 16 ft, plus optional sLo / sHi (blank).
  - PSAD-D6. The count is locked (the current count, with a note) for adjacent boxes and slabs and NEXT beams, entered distribution factors or live load, and a demand table or imported demands.
  - PSAD-D7. An entered b_eff goes back to the calculated width for another count (the Steel Bridge app's BEFF-3).
  - PSAD-D8. N_b default Lock (the steel app's default is Auto) so that the default run is the run before; Auto needs at least 3 girders.
  - PSAD-D9. Several counts: ranked by A × N_b (∝ the total concrete of the span), then h, then the current count; the default choice is the count with the least concrete over all spans; candidates of different counts in two spans are not applied together.
